httpjet · documentation · v0.2.0

# httpjet

A from-scratch **Rust web server** and **drop-in LiteSpeed replacement**: it reads the same `conf/httpd_config.xml` tree, speaks native LSAPI to `lsphp`, evaluates the same `.htaccess` files, and adds native HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, reverse-proxy and FastCGI gateways, and an opt-in LSCache-protocol page cache — all on one io_uring transport.

            resolve  SNI / Host → vhost
            acl  identity · throttle · geo · WAF
            rewrite  .htaccess · auth
            cache  lookup → hit?
            dispatch  ws · proxy · php · fcgi · static
            finalize  headers · compress
            store  cache write

       One pipeline per request, any protocol.

           GitHub · faratech/httpjet ↗
           Drop-in LiteSpeed XML config
           HTTP/1.1 · native HTTP/2 · HTTP/3
           Native LSAPI → lsphp · FastCGI
           Apache .htaccess · Basic auth
           Opt-in origin page cache

### Choose your path

          New to httpjet →  Install and serve.
          Migrating →  Move from LiteSpeed safely.
          Operating →   Operations  ·  Configuration
          Reference →  Commands, flags, and variables.

## What httpjet is

Point `--root` at your LiteSpeed Web Server (LSWS 6.3.5) or OpenLiteSpeed tree. httpjet runs it unchanged. Compatibility is the feature. Native additions stay opt-in.

### Compatible surface

- LiteSpeed XML and `mime.properties`

- Native LSAPI to `lsphp`

- mod_rewrite , access control, Basic auth, `Header`, `ErrorDocument`

- LSCache protocol (`X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control` / `-Tag` / `-Vary` / `-Purge`)

- LiteSpeed `fileETag=28` ETags, `.html`→PHP dispatch order

### httpjet-native (opt-in)

- Throttle, GeoIP/ASN , PROXY protocol , Unix-socket listeners

- Weighted groups with health checks; `h2://` / `h2s://`; FastCGI

- Per-context body/timeout/bandwidth, `sub_filter`, request decompression

- ACME , OCSP , kTLS/sendfile, OpenTelemetry

- Loopback admin API , WAF sidecar , compile-time extensions

        i   Where it runs
httpjet serves WindowsForum.com (x86_64) and MoonTimeNow.com + ThisDayInHistory.ai (ARM64) behind Cloudflare, on pure io_uring with the file tier live. It replaced LiteSpeed for all three (0.1.12, Rust 1.99.1+, edition 2024, GPL-3.0-only). Run `check --strict` and test on alternate ports before cutover. See Capabilities & limits .

## How the pieces fit

Select a node to open its page.

> [Diagram: pipeline] The request pipeline. pipeline::handle() resolves vhost and identity. dispatch() mirrors OpenLiteSpeed ordering. finalize_response finishes each terminal.

## By the numbers

See Performance for method and receipts.

          1,183 k rps   h2 empty, c=50, dedicated client VM, median of 3, 0.1.12 (2026-11-08): OLS 892k, nginx 388k; 1 KiB 1,097k vs 740k/319k
          44.8 k rps   PHP/LSAPI h1, PGO loopback (2026-06): LiteSpeed ~38.5k
          40 ×   cache hit vs PHP render: 19,215 vs 480 rps; p50 2 ms vs 34 ms
          146 /146   h2spec, native HTTP/2, TLS, three runs
          0.2 %   httpjet phases, June 2026 production (~138 µs/req); PHP 86.5–98.8% of wall time
          3,100 +   test functions, 20 crates; suite green at v0.2.0 (3,171 tests)

## Project status

| Aspect | State |

| Version | **0.2.0** · November 11, 2026 · latest public release |

| Release detail | Security audit fixes (WebSocket handshake, capsule revalidation, multi-member gzip, QUIC handshake cleanup, H3 body budget) and cold-start latency: the `.htaccess` chain is parsed once before the first connection, so the slowest request after boot falls from 508 ms to 3 ms. Lab VM, same run, 0.2.0 vs 0.1.12: HTTP/2 1 KiB static 625.5k vs 591.8k req/s, heavy-`.htaccess` HTTP/2 515.3k vs 402.9k, page-cache hits 544.5k vs 410.5k; see Performance . Semantic versioning adopted 2026-09-17; MSRV Rust 1.99.1, edition 2024. |

| Configuration | LiteSpeed XML stays authoritative. Native directives stay opt-in. `check --strict` gates deploys. |

| Transport | Pure io_uring (monoio), H1/H2/H3 only. No epoll fallback or Windows/macOS port. |

| PHP | Native LSAPI; you supply `lsphp`. Production: persistent external pool, zero-downtime generation reloads. |

| Page cache | Off by default; opt-in LSCache, private tier, cookie vary, tmpfs file tier, per-vhost dictionaries, generation namespaces. Live in production. |

| Optional features | `acme`, `ocsp`, `otel`, `ktls`, `profiling` build features. Each still needs runtime opt-in. |

| Security posture | Reviews through 2026-10-23 plus October bug-bash (rounds 1–16, 0.0.6–0.1.1; five rounds in 0.1.10 closed 23 issues; see audit posture ). Defaults stay fail-closed. |

| Release | Linux installer plus signed DEB, RPM and static archives via GitHub Releases . Full distribution matrix not completed for this release. |

==============================================================================
PAGE: Quickstart (https://httpjet.net/docs/quickstart)
SUMMARY: Install httpjet and serve your first page.
==============================================================================

# Quickstart

Install httpjet on a fresh Linux server in a few commands. You can also build it from source and try an example configuration.

Choose the packaged install for a fresh server. Choose the source build for development or testing. The packaged install serves a static welcome page over HTTP and HTTPS.

## Install a published release

Use a fresh Linux server on **amd64/x86-64 or arm64/aarch64**. Run the installer as root. You need Linux **io_uring** and free ports 80 and 443. You need no Rust toolchain, LiteSpeed, PHP or domain name.

           **install** · Linux
```
curl -fsSLo install.sh https://github.com/faratech/httpjet/releases/latest/download/install.sh
sudo sh ./install.sh
```

The installer selects signed DEB/APT or RPM packages on supported systemd systems. It can also select a signed portable archive. It verifies the release before installing. It creates a dedicated `httpjet` account. It starts the service on a fresh install. GitHub Releases also provides DEB, RPM and static archives.

Fresh installs serve `http://SERVER-IP/` on port 80. They serve `https://SERVER-IP/` on port 443. Each install generates its own self-signed certificate. Browsers warn until you configure a trusted certificate. HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS automatically. Open TCP ports 80 and 443 in your firewall for remote access.

           **check** · local welcome page
```
curl -f http://127.0.0.1/
# Accept the self-signed certificate for this loopback check only
curl -fk https://127.0.0.1/
```

Put site files in `/var/www/httpjet`. Find configuration under `/etc/httpjet/conf/`. Find logs under `/var/log/httpjet`. For a trusted certificate, update `keyFile` and `certFile` in `/etc/httpjet/conf/httpd_config.xml`. Run `httpjet --root /etc/httpjet check --strict` next. Restart the service after the check passes. Upgrades preserve existing configuration and certificates. See installation options and service commands .

        i   GitHub attribution
Release files have GitHub Actions publication attestations. Verify the installer with `gh attestation verify ./install.sh --repo faratech/httpjet --signer-workflow faratech/httpjet/.github/workflows/installer-publish-now.yml`. The release's full distribution matrix was not completed.

## Docker and Docker Desktop with WSL 2

Run the published Linux image on Docker Engine. You can also use Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks io_uring. Download the Compose file and supplied profile first:

           **container** · Docker Compose
```
curl -fsSLo compose.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/faratech/httpjet/main/packaging/docker/compose.yaml
curl -fsSLo seccomp-httpjet.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/faratech/httpjet/main/packaging/oci/seccomp-httpjet.json
docker compose up -d
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/` or `https://localhost:8443/`. The container generates a self-signed certificate. The certificate persists in a named volume. Browsers warn until you configure a trusted certificate. Your host kernel and runtime must allow io_uring. See the Docker and WSL 2 guide for details.

## Microsoft WSL Containers (wslc)

httpjet does not support Microsoft WSL Containers (`wslc`) today. See the Docker and WSL guide for the current status.

## Build from source

Build from source only for development or testing. Start with Source-build prerequisites below.

## Source-build prerequisites

You need the items below for a source build. You serve the example on loopback after the build.

| Requirement | Why |

| Linux with **io_uring** | The monoio/io_uring transport is the only transport. Limit: runtimes must allow `io_uring_setup`/`io_uring_enter`/`io_uring_register` (see OCI ). |

| **Rust 1.99.1+**, edition 2024 | The workspace MSRV. Limit: you also need a C toolchain for aws-lc-rs and mimalloc. |

| OpenSSL 3.x headers + pkg-config | Required only for `--features ocsp`. Limit: other builds do not need it. |

| An LSAPI-capable `lsphp` | Required only for PHP. Limit: static, proxy and FastCGI deployments need no PHP. |

## 1 · Build the binary

Clone the public repository from github.com/faratech/httpjet . Compile only the `httpjet` binary crate in release mode:

            **build** · cargo

```
git clone https://github.com/faratech/httpjet.git
cd httpjet

# release build of just the binary crate (the workspace is large — always scope with -p)
cargo build --release -p httpjet        # → target/release/httpjet

# optional build features (each still needs explicit runtime opt-in):
cargo build --release -p httpjet --features acme,ocsp,otel
```

A debug build compiles faster but runs ~5× slower. Use a debug build only for iteration. Use `--locked` for reproducible results.

## 2 · Validate a configuration tree

Configure httpjet with a *server root*. The root holds `conf/httpd_config.xml` and optional `conf/mime.properties`. It also holds the referenced per-vhost XML files. The `examples/litespeed/` tree gives you one listener on `127.0.0.1:8080`. It gives you one static vhost, `example.test`, with scripting and symlinks off.

            **check** · config lint

```
# parse the tree and print a summary (check is also the default subcommand)
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check

# strict: exit non-zero on lint errors (warnings never fail) — the deploy gate
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check --strict
```

`check --strict` hard-errors on three cases:

- A docroot shared by two vhosts fails.

- A vhost with a missing docroot fails.

- A mapped vhost whose config did not load fails.

Geo rules without a database fail even a plain `check`. Other findings warn without failing. Always use an absolute `--root`. See Configuration and Capabilities & limits for warnings.

## 3 · Serve on loopback

The XML holds persistent policy. The `serve` flags hold operational overrides. The example is HTTP-only, PHP-off and cache-off. You can run it safely beside an existing server.

            **serve** · development

```
target/release/httpjet --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" serve \
  --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --https-addr "" \
  --workers 1 --no-php
```

For TLS and HTTP/3, add a secure listener first. Set `keyFile`/`certFile` in the XML. Set ` 1 ` next. Pass `--https-addr 127.0.0.1:8443` when you serve. Reach the same port over TCP and UDP. See TLS, ACME & OCSP .

        !   Keep test state isolated
Use alternate ports and a separate `--php-socket`. Use low `--php-children` and a separate `--page-cache-store-path`. Never point a test instance at a production LSAPI socket.

## 4 · Verify

            **verify** · curl

```
printf 'hello from httpjet\n' > examples/litespeed/example/public/index.html
curl -i -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/

# h2c prior knowledge on the same plain port
curl -i --http2-prior-knowledge -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/

# Prometheus metrics (loopback-only by design)
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep -E '^httpjet_(requests_total|active_connections)'
```

Expect a LiteSpeed-style ETag, `"size-mtime-inode;;;"`. Expect `Vary: Accept-Encoding` on compressible bodies. Expect an `Alt-Svc` header once QUIC is on.

## 5 · Add PHP (optional)

Configure an LSAPI-capable `lsphp` in the XML first. Use ` ` or an `lsapi` `extProcessor` plus a `scriptHandler`. Drop `--no-php` to spawn a private pool. For zero-downtime deploys, run the pool separately:

            **two processes** · external pool

```
# terminal 1 — the persistent PHP pool
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp --php-socket /run/httpjet-test/php.sock --php-children 4

# terminal 2 — the web tier dials it and never spawns lsphp itself
httpjet --root /abs/root serve --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --https-addr "" \
  --lsphp-external /run/httpjet-test/php.sock \
  --lsphp-generation-file /run/httpjet-test/php.sock.generation
```

See LSAPI & PHP for pool and reload details.

## Where to go next

- Configuration — the XML reference.

- CLI reference — every `serve` flag.

- Operations — systemd, PHP pool and rollback.

- Page cache — enable `--page-cache` safely.

- Migrating from LiteSpeed — validate a real tree.

- github.com/faratech/httpjet — source and issue tracker.

PAGE: Migrating from LiteSpeed (https://httpjet.net/docs/migration)
SUMMARY: Move an existing LiteSpeed site step by step.
==============================================================================

# Migrating from LiteSpeed

httpjet reads LiteSpeed-compatible XML and speaks LSAPI. You still must prove compatibility for your tree before you move traffic.

> [Diagram: migration-path] Eight steps, three gates. Nothing binds the incumbent ports until behavior — not just startup — has been proved on an isolated candidate; caching is introduced only after uncached parity.

      i   Prerequisites
Start with a copied configuration root. Keep your `lsphp` binary available for PHP tests. Run every candidate on alternate ports first.

## 1 · Inventory before changing traffic

### Config

- Collect main XML and per-vhost XML. Include included files and variables.

- List listener maps and vhost maps. Record document roots and symlink policy.

- Collect `.htaccess` files and error documents. Add MIME maps and htpasswd files.

- Record TLS identities and chains. Note client-CA/CRL policy and renewal ownership.

### Traffic

- List LSAPI processors and PHP environment. Record child limits and socket owner/mode.

- Add application health checks. List proxy and WebSocket targets.

- Record timeout and retry assumptions. List trusted-proxy networks.

- Record cache opt-in and purge headers. Note public/private variation and stale behavior.

- List every external cache and CDN layer.

### Ops

- Record service user and group. List writable paths and resource limits.

- Note socket activation and firewall rules. Add monitoring probes.

Keep secrets and host-specific paths out of migration reports and example repositories.

## 2 · Validate a copied configuration

           **gate 1**
```
target/release/httpjet --root /abs/copied-root check --strict
sudo -u   target/release/httpjet --root /abs/copied-root check --strict
```

Treat three errors as blockers:

- Shared or missing docroots block you.

- Mapped vhosts whose config did not load block you.

- Geo rules without their database block you.

Run the check as the runtime identity too. Readable-by-root does not prove service access. Review all warnings before you proceed. See Capabilities & limits for ignored directives.

## 3 · Build the smallest required binary

           **build**
```
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo build --locked --release -p httpjet
```

Add `acme`, `ocsp`, `otel`, `profiling` or `ktls` only for a reviewed need. Keep default-off features off during parity testing. A `ktls` build defaults to `--ktls=auto`. It stays on rustls without active `tls-hw-tx-offload` on a physical NIC.

## 4 · Start an isolated candidate

           **serve** · alternate everything
```
target/release/httpjet --root /abs/copied-root serve \
  --http-addr 127.0.0.1:18080 --https-addr 127.0.0.1:18443 --workers 1 \
  --php-socket /tmp/httpjet-migration-test.sock --php-children 4 \
  --metrics-addr 127.0.0.1:19090
```

Never bind the incumbent ports for the first run. Use loopback or alternate ports. Use a separate LSAPI socket. Use distinct logs and a separate cache path. Use `--no-php` only when PHP stays out of scope. Never point two supervisors at one LSAPI socket.

## 5 · Prove behavior, not only startup

### Routing & transport

- Test exact, default and foreign Host routing. Check HTTP→HTTPS behavior.
- Test SNI, chains and ALPN. Test client certificates and CRL rejection.
- Test h1 keep-alive and chunking. Test h2 multiplexing and h3 over UDP.
- Test large files and ranges. Test conditional requests, compression and HEAD.

### Application

- Test rewrites and front controllers. Test PATH_INFO and per-directory access.
- Test Basic auth and custom headers. Test error documents.
- Test PHP/FastCGI environment and uploads. Test streaming, timeouts and worker recycling.
- Test source-disclosure failure cases. Test proxy, WebSocket and SSE behavior.
- Test upstream TLS and load distribution. Test all-backends-down and health recovery.
- Check logs, request ids and metrics. Test readiness, shutdown, restart and reload.

Compare status, headers and body bytes with the incumbent. Normalize only variable fields such as Date and request ids. Keep your comparison commands in the acceptance record. Repeat each failed case after every fix. Do not discard headers to force a pass.

## 6 · Introduce caching separately

Leave `--page-cache` off until you prove uncached parity. Then prove each item below:

- Distinct paths, hosts and schemes never replay each other.

- Distinct queries, cookies and encodings never replay each other.

- Public responses never store private or authenticated data.

- Private entries stay bound to their session.

- Purge tags invalidate every tier.

- Stale windows, restart scan and eviction fail safe.

Run the executable checks in page-cache deploy gates .

## 7 · Stage traffic and retain rollback

Package the exact tested binary at a stable path. Prefer socket activation with non-root permissions. Validate the systemd or OCI example for your environment. Canary through a load balancer, CDN or dedicated address first. Monitor status, latency, cache, connections and memory separately. Monitor file descriptors and PHP/upstream health too.

Write and drill the rollback before cutover. Include the prior binary, config and unit. Include certificate, socket and cache/CDN purge steps. A binary rollback does not remove bad cached objects.

## 8 · Reload only what is reloadable

Validate before SIGHUP or an API submission. See Admin API & reload and the acceptance record below.

## Minimum acceptance record

Reloadable state publishes without dropping in-flight requests. Listener, QUIC, PHP, cache-store and privilege changes need a restart. An API `restart_required` result blocks the transaction.

- Record the source commit and build features.

- Save the sanitized `vhost-map-fingerprint` and validation output.

- Record service identity, kernel/runtime and resource limits.

- Record exact test commands, clients and pass/fail counts.

- Record the canary window and observed deltas.

- Record the rollback command and a successful drill.

Do not claim completion from one HTTP 200. Prove the workload, failure modes, operations and rollback.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Capabilities & limits (https://httpjet.net/docs/capabilities)
SUMMARY: See what is supported, optional, or unsupported.
==============================================================================

# Capabilities & limits

This page lists 25 capabilities, 6 build features and 14 operational bounds. **Supported** means an implemented, tested code path, not parity with another server.

        supported  implemented + tested
        optional  build feature + runtime opt-in
        partial  tested subset — review the boundary
        unsupported  deliberate, documented

## Capability matrix

| Area | Status | Scope and important limits |

| HTTP/1.1 | supported | Keep-alive, pipelining, chunked bodies and 103 Early Hints. Limit: `CONNECT` gets 405; limits configure headers, URL, body and timeouts. → |

| HTTP/2 | supported | Native TLS h2 and h2c prior knowledge with h2spec 146/146. Limit: no server push and no `Upgrade: h2c`. → |

| HTTP/3 | supported | QUIC over UDP through the same pipeline. Limit: publish TCP and UDP HTTPS ports; migration stays disabled. → |

| TLS | supported | rustls (aws-lc-rs) TLS 1.2/1.3 with SNI and ALPN. Limit: dual ECDSA+RSA, reload, client certs and CRLs only as configured. → |

| Automatic certificates | optional | HTTP-01 and DNS-01 behind `--features acme` plus CLI opt-in. Limit: one account/identifier set per process; DNS-01 needs your webhook. → |

| OCSP stapling | optional | Stapling behind `--features ocsp` with OpenSSL 3.x. Limit: your responder must cover every issuer; not for Let's Encrypt. → |

| kTLS / sendfile | partial | Plain-TCP H1 file bodies always use `sendfile(2)`. Limit: TLS 1.3 H1 sendfile needs `--features ktls`, `--ktls=auto` and `tls-hw-tx-offload`. → |

| Virtual hosts | supported | Exact Host/SNI maps with parent-domain and bare `*` fallback. Limit: glob patterns like `*.example.test` never match; `check` warns. |

| Static content | supported | Conditional requests, LiteSpeed ETags and ranges. Limit: precompressed `.br`/`.gz` siblings only; opens stay traversal-safe. → |

| Reverse proxy | supported | HTTP/1 upstreams plus explicit `h2://`/`h2s://` with streaming and SSE. Limit: upstream mTLS only as configured. → |

| WebSocket | partial | HTTP/1 upgrade and raw relay. Limit: relay excludes TLS, H2 and Unix-socket upstreams. → |

| Upstream groups | supported | Primary-first, weighted selection and passive breaker. Limit: probes use connect/GET/HEAD only; unsafe requests never replay. → |

| PHP / LSAPI | supported | Native LSAPI with owned or external pools. Limit: external pools need generation tracking and candidate-first reload. → |

| FastCGI | supported opt-in | Explicit `fcgi`/`fastcgi` routing over TCP or Unix sockets. Limit: you supervise the app externally; bodies buffer. → |

| CGI execution, uWSGI | unsupported | Design contracts exist for both. Limit: nothing routes; a bare `cgi` handler fails closed. → |

| Rewrites & `.htaccess` | partial | Common rewrite, access, auth, header, expiry, cache and env directives. Limit: `Header edit`, `Header setifempty`, `Header echo` and `RequestHeader` are ignored. → |

| Compression | supported | Dynamic gzip/brotli/zstd plus precompressed siblings. Limit: gzip request decoding defaults on; brotli/zstd decoding is opt-in and bounded. → |

| Origin page cache | supported opt-in | Public/private tiers, vary, purge tags, stale, single flight and file tiers. Limit: route-level *microcache policy* is specified, not implemented. → |

| Access controls | supported | Peer ACLs, trusted-proxy IP, GeoIP/ASN rules, rate and body limits. Limit: bcrypt caps at 14; use bcrypt, `$apr1$`, `$1$` or `{SHA}`; files need docroot or `--auth-user-file-roots`. → |

| WAF | external opt-in | Bounded sidecar inspection over Unix or loopback TCP. Limit: it fails closed by default; no embedded ModSecurity/CRS. → |

| Logs and metrics | supported | Combined or JSON access logs and Prometheus metrics. Limit: error logs redact; syslog and slow logs stay optional. → |

| OpenTelemetry | optional | OTLP traces and metrics behind `--features otel` plus `HTTPJET_OTEL=1`. Limit: queues bound output; payloads never export. → |

| Runtime APIs | opt-in | Loopback status API and authenticated config API. Limit: boot-owned resources stay restart-required. → |

| Extensions | compile-time only | Trusted Rust crates register handlers and transforms. Limit: no dynamic ABI and no in-process sandbox. → |

| Deployment | examples | Generic systemd units and a hardened OCI example. Limit: your runtime must still permit io_uring. → |

## Deliberately unsupported or deferred

- **Generic CGI and uWSGI** never route. Use FastCGI, LSAPI or HTTP proxying instead.

- **HTTP/2 server push** is not implemented. Use `Link` preload plus 103 Early Hints.

- **HTTP trailers** are discarded, never forwarded. LSAPI has no trailer concept.

- **h2c is prior-knowledge only**. The `Upgrade: h2c` handshake is not implemented.

- **QUIC connection migration** is disabled. Listener steering cannot preserve ownership across address changes.

- **No epoll/tokio transport fallback**, no Windows/macOS. Linux io_uring is mandatory.

- **No native dynamic-module ABI.** Untrusted inspection belongs behind the bounded sidecar contract.

- **LiteSpeed anti-abuse elements** (`lsrecaptcha`, `censorshipControl`, permission masks, `cgiRlimit`) are parsed and warned about, never enforced.

- **Legacy htpasswd** (DES, `$5$`/`$6$`, plaintext) verifies *false*. Use bcrypt, APR1 (`$apr1$`), MD5-crypt (`$1$`) or `{SHA}`.

- **Cross-node cache peers** (`--cache-peer`, peer fill/purge fan-out) were removed in August 2026; the loopback purge and readiness endpoints remain.

- **Multipath QUIC** was assessed and deferred (June 2026).

## Build-time feature gates

The default binary includes serving, LSAPI, FastCGI, proxy and cache. It also includes logging, metrics and the WAF client. Each feature below needs an explicit build plus its runtime switch.

| Cargo feature | Adds | Runtime opt-in |

| `acme` | `hj-acme`: HTTP-01 / DNS-01 issuance and renewal | `--acme-directory … --acme-domains … --acme-store … --acme-accept-terms` |

| `ocsp` | `hj-ocsp`: fetch, validate, staple (OpenSSL 3.x) | `--ocsp-responder URL` (+ `--ocsp-required`) |

| `otel` | OTLP HTTP/protobuf tracing and metrics exporters | `HTTPJET_OTEL=1` (+ `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1`) |

| `profiling` | Loopback pprof CPU profile endpoint | `--profile-token` policy; loopback only regardless |

| `ktls` | Kernel TLS on the io_uring TLS path | `--ktls=auto|on|off`; `auto` requires a physical NIC with `tls-hw-tx-offload` |

| `allocount` | Allocation-measurement harness | Diagnostic builds only |

## Operational bounds

Request limits come from ` ` and per-context overrides. Inspect effective values with `check --strict` and `serve --help`.

| Bound | Value |

| Page-cache single object | 100 MiB — larger responses serve uncached |

| Page-cache budgets | Index `--page-cache-mem`; file `--page-cache-disk-mem`; hot `--page-cache-hot-mem`. Limit: files need `--page-cache-integrity-key` (single-link, root/serving uid, no group/other); `--page-cache-integrity-required` enforces it. |

| Bridge buffering | Bodies ≤ 256 KiB buffered, larger streamed (H1/H2/H3) |

| Request body budget | Process-wide byte budget with leases; usage, capacity and rejections exported as `httpjet_body_buffer_*` |

| Request decompression | 16 MiB decoded ceiling; 17 MiB codec workspace reservation for br/zstd; zstd window ≤ 2 24 |

| Multipart ranges | 8 ranges / 8 MiB of part bytes, else a full 200 |

| `.htaccess` chain depth | 64 directories, then a deny-all sentinel |

| sub_filter buffering | 4 MiB default (`subFilterMaxBody`); beyond it the stream passes through raw |

| WAF sidecar | Body inspected up to `--waf-body-max` (default 64 KiB, cap 1 MiB), total timeout default 100 ms (cap 30 s), concurrency default 128 (cap 4096), 4 KiB response head, 64 MiB process-wide serialization budget |

| Admin APIs | Read: 4 KiB/32 header fields, 4 connections, 5 s deadlines, 1 MiB response. Write: 8 KiB/32 fields, 1 MiB body, ≤128 vhosts, ≤64 XML nesting, 4 connections, one candidate build, 5 s lock / 10 s wait |

| Active health probes | Intervals/timeouts 1 s–1 h, rise/fall 1–100, process-wide cap of 16 concurrent probes |

| FastCGI | 65,535-byte records; separately bounded PARAMS aggregate, response head, STDERR, body buffering, pool size and deadlines |

| ACME | 1–100 identifiers, ≤128 live challenges, 1 MiB snapshots and CA bodies, 120 s per attempt |

| OCSP | ≤128 identities, ≤4 concurrent fetches, 64 KiB responses, 7-day staple validity cap |

| OpenTelemetry | 2048 queued spans + one 256-span batch, 1 s interval, 2 s export timeout, 3 s shutdown bound |

| Loopback-only endpoints | `/__hj_cache_purge`, `/__hj_cache_ready` (raw loopback peer), metrics `:9090`, admin listeners |

Size workers, file limits, budgets, cache, PHP and timeouts together.

## Reload boundary (summary)

SIGHUP and the API replace app state without dropping requests. Boot-owned resources stay **restart-required**. See Admin API & reload .

## Reproducible checks

           **verify the tree** · what CI runs
```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --locked -p httpjet --bin httpjet
cargo run --locked -p httpjet -- --root "$PWD/examples/litespeed" check --strict
cargo test --locked --workspace
```

Topic pages carry narrower acceptance commands. Tests use synthetic config and ephemeral loopback ports.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Configuration (https://httpjet.net/docs/configuration)
SUMMARY: Look up every setting in the XML reference.
==============================================================================

# Configuration reference

httpjet is configured by a **LiteSpeed-compatible XML tree** selected with `--root`: `conf/httpd_config.xml`, the per-vhost files it references, and `conf/mime.properties`. An existing LiteSpeed or OpenLiteSpeed tree works as-is. On that base httpjet layers its own opt-in directives — marked httpjet — which LiteSpeed ignores. Operational overrides live on the command line , not in the XML.

## The configuration tree

With no `--root`, httpjet uses `/usr/local/lsws`. You get LiteSpeed value semantics:

- Variables `$SERVER_ROOT`, `$HOSTNAME`, `$VH_ROOT`, `$VH_NAME` substitute. Limit: `$DOC_ROOT` and `$VH_DOMAIN` need vhost resolution.

- Sizes accept `K`/`M`/`G`/`B` suffixes. Limit: times use bare seconds.

- Bounded integers fall back to defaults when invalid. Limit: `setUIDMode`/`chrootMode` errors instead (2026-09-16).

- Booleans accept `1`, `2`, or `true`. Limit: symlink value `2` never follows.

- Unknown elements load silently. Limit: partial `allowOverride`, vhost `clientVerify`, rewrite maps, `phpIniOverride`, `enableHotlinkCtrl`, and `forceStrictOwnership` refuse the load.

           **layout** · a server root
```
/usr/local/lsws/
├── conf/
│   ├── httpd_config.xml          # server, tuning, security, listeners, extProcessors, vhost declarations
│   ├── mime.properties           # mime/type = ext1, ext2   (best-effort)
│   └── vhosts/example.test.xml   #  : docroot, contexts, rewrite, vhssl, cache, logging
└── logs/
```

> [Diagram: config-inheritance] Configuration cascade and parse-time memo classification. Server-wide defaults in httpd_config.xml cascade into each  , then into longest-prefix   overrides and the per-directory .htaccess chain, where static analysis computes the MemoClass eligibility verdict reported by httpjet check.

## Checking a configuration

           **check**
```
httpjet --root /abs/root check            # summary: listeners, vhost map, fast-memo verdicts, warnings
httpjet --root /abs/root check --strict   # same lint output; exits non-zero on lint errors (warnings never fail)
```

You run check under the service identity too. Readable-by-root does not prove readable at runtime. The write API runs the same normalization. It also refuses DTDs, nesting over 64 levels, over 128 vhosts, and XML over 1 MiB. Disk files cap at 16 MiB per file (`ConfigError::TooLarge`, 2026-10-06).

## Server and tuning

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `serverName` | `$HOSTNAME` | Server identity (else `localhost`). |

| `user` / `group` | `nobody` | Run-as credentials (the systemd unit usually sets these). |

| `indexFiles` | `index.html` | Directory-index candidates (vhost may override). |

| `useIpInProxyHeader` | `2` | Client-IP trust mode. Limit: 0 never, 1 always, 2 trusted peers, 3 as 2, 4 always. |

| ` ` | `0` | HTTP/3 master switch; also drives `Alt-Svc`. Needs the UDP port published. |

| ` maxConnections` | `65000` | Connection cap. |

| `connTimeout` / `keepAliveTimeout` | `60` / `5` s | Idle / keep-alive timeouts. |

| `maxKeepAliveReq` | `1000` | Requests per keep-alive connection (0 or 1 disables keep-alive, matching OpenLiteSpeed). |

| `maxReqURLLen` / `maxReqHeaderSize` | `8192` / `16380` | URL and header-block caps. |

| `maxReqBodySize` | `100M` | Server-wide request-body cap (413); per-context override below. |

| `perIpRate` · `perIpRateWindowSecs` httpjet | `0` · `1` | Per-client-IP request throttle (0 = off) and its fixed window. 429 on exceed; fail-open under state pressure. |

| `bandwidthLimit` httpjet | `0` | Per-connection egress throttle, bytes/s (0 = unlimited). H2 paces per connection; H3 unpaced. |

| `maxCachedFileSize` / `totalInMemCacheSize` | `4M` / `4G` | Small-file in-memory promotion threshold and budget (`CacheCaps`); the budget is clamped to 1 GiB. |

| `maxMMapFileSize` / `totalMMapCacheSize` | `256K` / `2G` | Sizes the static RAM store. Limit: per-file cap uses the larger value; budgets clamp to 1 GiB + 2 GiB. |

| `fileETag` | `28` | ETag bitmask (INODE|MTIME|SIZE → `"size-mtime-inode;;;"`); 0 = no ETag. |

| `enable{Gzip,Br,Zstd}Compress` (+`Dyn`) | on | Static/dynamic compression per codec; `zstdCompressLevel` 3, `brCompressLevel` 5. |

| ` enableExpires`, `expiresByType` | off | Expiry rules like `image/*=A604800`. Limit: authenticated responses default to `private, no-store`. |

| ` expireInSeconds` · `privateExpireInSeconds` · `cacheStatusCode` · `enablePostCache` | `900` · `0` · `200,301` · off | Default public/private TTLs and cacheable statuses. `cacheStorePath` is parsed but deliberately unused (see `--page-cache-store-path`). |

## Security directives

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| ` ` `allow`/`deny` | — | `ALL` or CIDR lists, most-specific wins. A trailing `T` on an allow rule marks a trusted proxy. |

| ` ` | — | Globs never served; a malformed glob is a hard start/reload error. |

| ` followSymbolLink` | off | Folded into each vhost's effective `allowSymbolLink`; `2` fails closed. |

| `geoipDBFile` · `geoAllow`/`geoDeny` · `asnAllow`/`asnDeny` httpjet | none | Offline CidrList source and label lists; deny-first, allow-only = whitelist, unknown label = build error. → |

| ` enable` · `uidMin` · `gidMin` | `0` · `100` · `100` | suEXEC master gate and floors; uid/gid 0 always rejected. |

| ` ` `enable`, `mount`, `pid`, `net`, `uts`, `ipc` | off | Namespace isolation for PHP workers; `pid` is accepted but not honored. |

| ` ` `CPUSoftLimit`/`CPUHardLimit` | — | Parsed for compatibility; ignored on persistent `lsphp` workers (`check` warns). |

| `lsrecaptcha`, `censorshipControl`, permission masks | — | not enforced — `check` warns. |

## Listeners and TLS

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `name`, `address` | `*:80` | Listener bind address. Limit: `unix:`/`uds:` serves HTTP only; TLS over UDS never serves. |

| `secure`, `keyFile`, `certFile`, `certChain` | off | TLS material; `certChain=1` appends `CACertFile` to the served chain. |

| `CACertFile` · `clientVerify` · `verifyDepth` | none · `0` · `1` | Client-certificate verification (0 none · 1 optional · 2 required · 3 optional without CA) against the listener CA. |

| `crlFile` httpjet | none | PEM CRL/bundle enforced by the client verifier. |

| `enableStapling` | `0` | Compatibility only; OCSP needs `--features ocsp` + `--ocsp-responder`. |

| `proxyProtocol` httpjet | `0` | PROXY v2/v1 required on *this* listener; fail-closed; never on a public bind. |

| `vhostMapList/vhostMap` `vhost`, `domain` | — | Maps host to vhost. Limit: exact, then parent, then `*`; globs never match. |

           **httpd_config.xml** · a TLS listener with h3
```
  1

     https
     *:443
     1
     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.test/privkey.pem
     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.test/fullchain.pem
     0
       example.test  example.test,www.example.test

```

## External processors

You define proxy, LSAPI, or FastCGI upstreams here. Limit: unknown legacy types proxy; `cgi` contexts never execute.

| Directive | Default | Meaning |

| `name`, `type` | required | `proxy` · `lsapi` · `fcgi`/`fastcgi` httpjet . |

| `address` (repeatable) | required | `ip:port`, `host:port`, `uds:///path`, `http://`, `https://`, and httpjet `h2://` (prior knowledge) / `h2s://` (TLS, ALPN fail-closed). Additional addresses form a group: ordered failover by default, load-balanced with the options below. |

| `loadBalancePolicy` httpjet | `primary-first` | `weighted-round-robin` · `weighted-least-active`. Invalid on non-proxy processors. |

| `addressWeights` httpjet | all 1 | One integer 1–1000 per address. |

| ` ` `mode` · `path` · `host` · `interval` · `timeout` · `rise` · `fall` · `expectedStatus` httpjet | `connect` · `/` · — · 10 · 2 · 2 · 3 · 200 | Active probes; intervals 1–3600 s, timeout ≤ interval, thresholds 1–100, status 200–599. → |

| `maxConns` | `100` | Pool cap (LSAPI: worker count source unless `--php-children` overrides). |

| `initTimeout` / `retryTimeout` / `pcKeepAliveTimeout` | `60` / `0` / `60` s | Connect timeout / bad-mark cooldown (retry dials fresh; a backend timeout is 504) / idle recycle. |

| `respBuffer` | `0` | Parsed; responses always stream (`check` warns if set). |

| `clientCertFile` / `clientKeyFile` httpjet | none | Upstream mTLS client identity for `https://`/`h2s://` targets; must lie within an admin resource root when submitted via the API. |

| `env` (repeatable) | — | `K=V` worker environment. Server-computed CGI names are protected. |

| `path`, `backlog`, `instances`, `autoStart`, `runOnStartUp` | — / `100` / `1` / `0` / `0` | LSAPI worker binary and supervision (`instances>1` warns: one fixed upstream). |

| *`phpConfig` additionally:* `phpHandler` (`command`, `suffixes`), `memSoftLimit`/`memHardLimit`, `maxProcessTime` (0 = unlimited; `--php-max-process-time-ms` overrides), `procSoftLimit`/`procHardLimit`, `extMaxIdleTime`, `backlog` default 1024, `pcKeepAliveTimeout` default 30 s (not 60), `detachedMode`. |

## Virtual hosts

You declare vhosts in `httpd_config.xml`. Limit: `restrained` confines to `vhRoot`; `enableScript=0` disables scripts.

| Vhost directive | Meaning |

| `docRoot`, `indexFiles`, `enableExpires`/`expiresByType` | Root and per-vhost overrides of the server settings. |

| ` ` `enable`, `autoLoadHtaccess`, `base`, `rules` | Inline rules run before the `.htaccess` chain. |

| ` ` `allowOverride`, `accessFileName` | Controls `.htaccess` loading. Limit: only `0` or `31` loads; partial masks refuse. |

| ` ` `keyFile`, `certFile`, `certChain`, `CACertFile` | The SNI identity for this vhost's domains (chain material, not a client-verify root). |

| ` ` `enableCache`, `enablePublicCache`, `enablePrivateCache` | Per-vhost page-cache gates (with `--page-cache-standard-vhosts` a missing block gets a default public policy). |

| ` ` `suffix`, `type`, `handler` | Suffix routing to `lsapi`/`php` handlers or a `cgi` handler bound to a FastCGI processor. |

| ` ` `uri`, `address` | WebSocket relay maps (plain TCP HTTP/1 upstreams). |

| ` ` `accessLog`/`errorLog` with `useServer=0`, `fileName`, `rollingSize`, `keepDays`, `logHeaders` httpjet | Per-vhost log files (default roll 50 MB, keep 30 days; `logHeaders` default 3 = combined, 7 = combined + Host). Log paths are boot-owned. |

| `setUIDMode` (0/1/2), `chrootMode` (0/1/2), `chrootPath`, `suexecUser`/`suexecGroup`, ` ` | Per-vhost PHP isolation (needs the server ` ` gate). Out-of-range modes are hard errors. → |

| ` ` | Vhost-scoped processors (distinct scope from server-level ones). |

## Contexts

Contexts map URI prefixes to terminals (`static`, `proxy`, `redirect`, `php`/`lsapi` via `handler`) and carry per-context overrides:

| Context directive | Default | Meaning |

| `type`, `uri`, `location`, `handler`, `enabled` | — | Kind, prefix, on-disk location (static), processor name (proxy/lsapi). |

| `extraHeaders` | — | Adds response headers. Limit: `Name: value` only; never on `proxy` contexts. |

| `addDefaultCharset` / `addDefaultCharsetCustomized` | off | Charset appended to text types. |

| `cachePolicy/*` | on (`enablePostCache` off) | `checkPublicCache`, `checkPrivateCache`, `respectCacheable`, `enableCache`, `enablePrivateCache`, `enablePostCache` — the six LSWS gates, enforced on both cache tiers. |

| `maxReqBodySize` httpjet | inherit | Per-context body cap (413) on every terminal. |

| `responseTimeout` httpjet | inherit | Upstream response-head deadline, seconds (proxy paths). |

| `bandwidthLimit` httpjet | `0` | Egress throttle overriding the server-wide rate. |

| `subFilter` (repeatable) · `subFilterOnce` · `subFilterTypes` · `subFilterMaxBody` httpjet | — · `0` · `text/html` · `4M` | Literal body substitution. Limit: missing `=>` disables the context filter. → |

           **vhost XML** · a proxied API prefix with overrides
```

     proxy
     /api/
     application
     2M
     15
     http://internal.example => https://example.test
     text/html,application/json

```

## Environment variables

See the CLI reference for the full list.

Common unit settings include `RUST_LOG` and `CF_SEND_ZSTD=1`.

You set variables in your unit drop-in.

==============================================================================
PAGE: TLS, ACME & OCSP (https://httpjet.net/docs/certificates)
SUMMARY: Set up certificates, ACME issuance, and OCSP.
==============================================================================

# TLS, ACME & OCSP

You configure certificates, client verification, and session resumption here. ACME and OCSP stapling are opt-in services on the same resolver.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

| Choice | Use it when. Gate: |

| File certificates | You already own PEM chains. Gate: none; reload via SIGHUP. |

| ACME ( below ) | You want issuance and renewal in-process. Gate: `--features acme` plus four CLI flags. |

| OCSP stapling ( below ) | Your CA still runs a responder. Gate: `--features ocsp` plus `--ocsp-responder`. |

ACME and OCSP are default-off at build and runtime. Both publish into the same generation-bound resolver slots as file certificates.

## TLS configuration

`hj-tls` builds one `rustls::ServerConfig` for TCP and QUIC via `build_server_config_alpn(cfg, listener, alpn)`. You land rotations on both transports at once.

| Listener XML | Meaning. Limit: |

| `secure`, `keyFile`, `certFile` | Listener default identity (PEM). Limit: `certChain=1` appends `CACertFile` as served chain. |

| Per-vhost ` ` | SNI identity for that vhost. Limit: chain material only, never a client-verify root; pair ECDSA+RSA for smaller modern chains. |

| `clientVerify` 0–3, `CACertFile`, `verifyDepth` | mTLS: 0 none, 1 optional, 2 required, 3 as 1. Limit: verifier uses the listener CA only; verdicts memoized off the hot path. |

| `crlFile` httpjet | PEM CRL or bundle for the webpki verifier. Limit: absent means no revocation checking; rotate via trust-generation reload. |

| `enableStapling` | Parsed for compatibility only. Limit: fetching needs the `ocsp` feature and `--ocsp-responder`; `check` says so. |

| `--ktls` (feature `ktls`) | Kernel TLS for TLS 1.3 H1 file egress. Limit: see the kTLS stub and File egress . |

### Handshake posture

- **SNI without cert-name-match.** SNI maps directly to configured material, mirroring OpenLiteSpeed. Limit: ACME identities are exact-SNI overlays; the no-SNI fallback stays.

- **TLS 1.3 suite.** TLS 1.3 offers exactly `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`; TLS 1.2 keeps its full set. Limit: rustls negotiates by client order; the pin moves transcripts to hardware SHA-NI.

- **Tickets.** Listeners without client verification (`clientVerify` 0) issue single-use, stateful TLS 1.3 tickets. Limit: `--tls-session-tickets` per full handshake (default 2; 0 shrinks the cache from 32,768 to 256 TLS 1.2 IDs); 0-RTT off everywhere.

- **Verified-client listeners.** `clientVerify` 1–3 issues no tickets and keeps no session cache. Limit: every connection full-handshakes and re-verifies; resumption stays 0 there.

- **Certified-peer idle window.** `--trusted-proxy-idle-secs` extends idle for verified-certificate connections. Limit: OCSP disables resumption; full handshakes fell 28%/s (about 30%/request x86, 78%/request ARM).

- **mTLS boundary.** On `clientVerify=2`, plaintext for an mTLS vhost is refused unless from loopback. Limit: `--no-mtls` relaxes this for local testing only.

- **Reload.** File certificates reload via `CertReloadHandle` on SIGHUP or the write API . Limit: a failed reload keeps prior certificates; kTLS templates apply to new handshakes only.

        !   Two CAs, two roles
A per-vhost `CACertFile` goes to clients as chain material. The listener `CACertFile` verifies client certificates; never merge the roles.

## ACME certificate automation --features acme

Build with `cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme`. You need all four required flags; one manager/account/identifier set runs per process, boot-frozen.

          HTTP-01  DNS-01 / wildcard  Local test CA

               **serve** · HTTP-01
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --acme-directory https://YOUR-CA/directory \
  --acme-domains example.test,www.example.test \
  --acme-store /abs/private/acme \      # pre-created, mode 0700, owned by the service uid
  --acme-accept-terms \
  --acme-bootstrap                      # only for first issuance without a configured certificate
```

You need public TCP port 80 and an enabled TLS listener. The route `/.well-known/acme-challenge/ ` runs before normalization, redirects, rewrites, auth, cache, and backends.

Only plaintext GET on the validated authority answers. Limit: 404 unknown, 405 other, `no-store`; tokens redacted; #259 bypass closed.

               **serve** · DNS-01
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --acme-directory https://YOUR-CA/directory \
  --acme-domains 'example.test,*.example.test' \   # quote the wildcard
  --acme-store /abs/private/acme --acme-accept-terms \
  --acme-dns-webhook https://YOUR-CONTROLLER/acme \
  --acme-dns-zones example.test \
  --acme-dns-token-file /abs/private/dns-controller.token   # regular file, 0600, 16..4096 printable chars
```

You need no port 80 and no HTTP exemption here. Run your own controller; no Cloudflare or provider integration ships.

A wildcard matches exactly one leftmost label. Limit: request the apex separately; scope the credential to the listed zones.

| Webhook operation | Contract. Limit: |

| `present` | POST JSON `{"version":1,"operation":"present","name":"_acme-challenge.example.test","value":" "}`, Bearer [REDACTED]. Limit: adds that value only, never replaces the RRset. |

| `ready` | Same `name`/`value` fields. Limit: reply `{"ok":true,"ready":true|false}`; false means not yet visible. |

| `cleanup` | Same fields; reply `{"ok":true}`. Limit: removes only that value; succeeds if already absent (apex/wildcard share one owner). |

All operations are idempotent, with a 5 s deadline per call. Limit: replies over 16 KiB, redirects, non-2xx, and unexpected fields are rejected; `ready:true` without real DNS visibility is invalid in production.

`--acme-test-mode` permits literal-loopback HTTP directories and alternate ports. Limit: it requires loopback serving addresses; `--acme-test-ca-root`, `--acme-test-issuer-root`, and `--acme-dns-test-root` replace roots without disabling verification (Pebble only).

               **acceptance** · Pebble v2.10.1
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-acme
cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme
python3 -B scripts/acme-pebble-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet \
  --pebble /path/to/pebble --dns /path/to/pebble-challtestsrv \
  --pebble-source /path/to/pebble-v2.10.1 --bootstrap [--dns01]
```

### Issuance, recovery and activation

> [Diagram: acme-http01] HTTP-01 issuance. Each durable step precedes its network step: account key before registration, certificate key and CSR before finalize, issued pair in the same atomic snapshot. Only a validated pair publishes.

- **Durable before network.** A lost `newOrder` response is ambiguous; a marker stops reissuance. Limit: restart once with `--acme-reconcile-order `; never delete the store.

- **Bounded CA traffic.** Only GET/HEAD/POST at the directory origin. Limit: no redirects/proxies; 1 MiB bodies; 5 s connect / 10 s request; 120 s per attempt; backoff plus `Retry-After`.

- **Private store.** Pre-create a 0700 directory owned by the effective uid. Limit: no-follow ancestors, exclusive lock, 0600 snapshots (pending→fsync→rename→dirsync, 1 MiB cap); pending files discarded.

- **Activation.** The validated `CertifiedKey` publishes as exact-SNI to TCP, kTLS, and QUIC. Limit: SIGHUP uses a separate slot; boot rejects an expired pair.

- **Bootstrap.** With `--acme-bootstrap`, the default identity starts absent. Limit: no self-signed placeholder; handshakes fail until issuance.

- **Renewal.** Renewal keeps one third of lifetime in reserve, plus jitter.

> [Diagram: acme-dns01] DNS-01 cleanup. Cleanup intent journals before any DNS mutation; cleanup replays after attempts, at shutdown and startup, and blocks new issuance until it succeeds. Changing endpoint or zone scope on a reused store fails closed.

Scope: DNS identifiers only (ASCII A-labels), one account/group per process, same-origin endpoints, no EAB, contact management, or ARI. Production at windowsforum.com still renews through certbot.

## OCSP stapling --features ocsp

Build with `--features ocsp` (OpenSSL 3.x headers and pkg-config at build; shared libraries at runtime). Pass `--ocsp-responder https://ocsp.example.net/status`, optionally `--ocsp-required`.

The CLI opt-in covers every certificate on your TLS listeners. Limit: `enableStapling` alone does nothing; one responder must serve every issuer.

        !   Not for Let's Encrypt
Let's Encrypt retired OCSP on 2025-08-06 and publishes CRLs instead. Do not enable this manager for current Let's Encrypt certificates.

> [Diagram: ocsp-policy] Status lifecycle. Fetching never happens during a handshake. Verified GOOD fills a generation-bound slot; verified REVOKED suppresses that leaf even across reload; failures preserve a still-valid staple or fall to policy.

- **Trust.** Each leaf includes its immediate issuer. Limit: issuer/authorized-signer signatures only; no AIA, redirects, encoded bodies, or bypass; SHA-256 CertIDs; RSA PKCS#1 v1.5, ECDSA SHA-256/384/512.

- **Freshness.** `thisUpdate`, `producedAt`, `nextUpdate` required. Limit: never past seven days from `thisUpdate`; wall and monotonic time both apply.

- **Transport.** Percent-encoded GET at ≤ 255 bytes, else binary POST. Limit: DNS pinned; private destinations rejected except loopback under `--ocsp-test-mode`.

- **Policy.** Optional (default) serves without a staple, unless Must-Staple. Limit: required rejects handshakes until valid, even at startup; memory-only, resets on restart.

           **acceptance** · real-server fixtures on isolated listeners
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-ocsp
cargo test --locked -p hj-tls --features ocsp ocsp
cargo build --locked -p httpjet --features acme,ocsp
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet            # required policy
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --optional
python3 -B scripts/ocsp-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --optional --must-staple
```

## Kernel TLS

kTLS now lives inside TLS configuration as one table row. See File egress for policy and receipts; this stub keeps old links working.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Security & access control (https://httpjet.net/docs/security)
SUMMARY: Control who can reach your sites.
==============================================================================

# Security & access control

Decide **who the client is** and **who may ask** here. The posture is **fail closed**: a control that cannot evaluate acts restrictive. One exception: the opt-in throttle fails open (see Throttle ).

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Client identity

Resolve one client IP at connection admission. Store it in `ReqCtx.client_ip`. Every later gate reads that value.

> [Diagram: client-ip] From socket peer to client identity. Forwarded headers are evidence, not identity: they count only from a peer an allow rule marks T; from anyone else they are attacker-controlled data and ignored. Every later gate — ACL, geo, throttle, mTLS exemption, logs, the cache key — reads the resolved value.

| `useIpInProxyHeader` | Forwarded headers are believed… |

| 0 | never |

| 1 / 4 | always. Limit: only safe when only your proxy can reach the listener. |

| 2 (default) | only from trusted peers (`allow … T`). Limit: `CF-Connecting-IP` counts on that path. |

| 3 | as 2, for IP purposes only |

The admin write API marks `useIpInProxyHeader` and ` ` **restart-required**. Trust never changes under a running generation.

## Network ACLs

**Summary:** CIDRs decide access most-specific-wins; static opens stay beneath the docroot.

Evaluate ` ` CIDRs most-specific-wins; trailing `T` marks a trusted proxy. Never serve ` ` globs; malformed globs hard-fail. Mode `2` fails closed to never-follow.

Open statics with `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH)` (plus `RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS` when denying symlinks). Refuse non-regular files. Without `openat2`, walk `O_NOFOLLOW` components beneath the docroot (v0.1.10).

## Per-client-IP throttle

Cap requests per client IP per fixed window with ` ` (or `--per-ip-rate`). Set the window with `perIpRateWindowSecs` (default 1 s). Excess requests get 429. Count once per request, in 64 shards with 4096 tracked IPs per shard.

        !   Off by default, and fail-open
Default 0 (disabled): a shared NAT egress aggregates many visitors behind one address. Under pressure the throttle evicts expired windows, then *admits untracked*. It degrades fairness, never availability. Watch `httpjet_throttle_{allowed,rejected}_total`.

## GeoIP / ASN rules

Get country/network membership from `hj-geo` (no runtime network access). Point ` ` at a CidrList file; ranges binary-search as merged intervals. Judge IPv4-mapped IPv6 in v4 space.

           **geo source** · CidrList format
```
# country
country US 203.0.113.0/24 198.51.100.0/24
country DE 2001:db8::/32
# asn
asn 13335 203.0.113.0/24
```

Resolve `geoAllow`/`geoDeny`/`asnAllow`/`asnDeny` at build: **deny first**; allow-alone is a **fail-closed whitelist**. Unknown labels or a missing database hard-fail. Judge the *resolved* IP in both funnels.

## PROXY protocol trust

Require a PROXY v2/v1 header on every connection to a `proxyProtocol=1` listener. Consume it before TLS or the h1/h2c sniff. The opt-in *is* the trust decision — never enable it on a public bind (`check` warns). Refuse loopback or unspecified source claims at the parser (2026-09-16). Details: Protocol stacks .

## TLS & mTLS

- **mTLS** — set `clientVerify` 1–3 for a webpki verifier on the *listener* CA; level 2 requires a client certificate. Limit: `--no-mtls` is local testing only; confirm flags with `systemctl show -p ExecStart`.

- **Revocation and resumption** — add `crlFile` for PEM CRL enforcement; absent means none. Limit: one TLS 1.3 suite, 0-RTT off, single-use tickets only without client verification, resumption off with OCSP.

- **One config, two transports** — a certificate, verifier or CRL change lands on TCP and QUIC together. Limit: see TLS, ACME & OCSP .

A plaintext request for an mTLS vhost is refused unless from loopback. TLS stream splitting was made memory-safe in the 2026-09-06 round.

## Request limits & resource fences

| Fence | Enforcement |

| Header, URL, connections, timeouts | From ` `. Limit: `maxReqURLLen`, `maxReqHeaderSize`, `maxConnections`, `connTimeout`, `keepAliveTimeout`, `maxKeepAliveReq`. |

| Body size | `maxReqBodySize`, per-context override. Limit: 413 on every terminal; reserve decoded growth first. |

| Body budget | Process-wide byte budget with owned leases. Limit: released on completion or teardown; see `httpjet_body_buffer_*`. |

| Request decompression | Gzip default; br/zstd opt-in. Limit: 16 MiB ceiling, 17 MiB workspace, zstd window ≤ 2 24 , one coding ( → ). |

| Egress bandwidth | Per-connection token bucket (`bandwidthLimit`). Limit: H2 paces per connection; H3 unpaced. |

| Ranges · sub_filter · `.htaccess` | 8 ranges / 8 MiB. Limit: 4 MiB then raw pass-through; 64 levels then deny-all. |

| H2 / H3 memory | Stream and connection limits, Bomb mitigation. Limit: leases release on reset/EOF/error. |

| Page cache | 100 MiB object cap; index/file/hot budgets; identity guard. Limit: integrity key validated like admin tokens; purge is loopback POST-only. |

| Reload safety | Broken SIGHUP config keeps the old generation. Limit: out-of-range isolation modes are hard errors. |

| Worker pinning | Core indices clamped to `CPU_SETSIZE`. Limit: no pin past the set size. |

Incomplete request reads stay bounded (2026-09-06). H2 frame/body deadlines apply on both loops. Judge integrity state by `httpjet_pagecache_integrity_active`; `--page-cache-integrity-required` makes an uninstallable key a boot failure.

## WAF inspection seam

httpjet embeds no rules engine. Enable `--waf-sidecar-addr` for a bounded call over a Unix socket (peer UID via `SO_PEERCRED` vs `--waf-sidecar-uid`) or loopback TCP. Run it before rewrite, cache and dispatch, so warm hits still get inspected. Default failure is **closed** (503); `--waf-fail-open` is explicit. A sidecar 403 always blocks. See Extending httpjet .

## The PHP jail

Configure suEXEC (` `, off by default; uid 0 always rejected), chroot (`chrootMode` 0–2) and namespaces (`pid` accepted, not honored). An unsafe jail disables PHP with 503 — never unjailed. Workers never run as root. See LSAPI & PHP .

## Control surfaces

**Summary:** every control surface requires loopback, a token, or both — check the guard before you expose one.

| Surface | Guard |

| `/__hj_cache_purge`, `/__hj_cache_ready` | Raw TCP peer must be loopback. Limit: POST-only purge (405 + `Allow`); ready takes GET/HEAD; a `unix:` listener opens both to local processes. |

| `--metrics-addr` (`/metrics`, `/cache-entries`, `/__mimalloc-stats`, `/__alloc-count`, `/debug/pprof/profile`) | Loopback-only by default. Limit: `/metrics` open on loopback; the rest need a Bearer token matching `--profile-token-file` (403 when unset). |

| `--admin-addr` (`/v1/status`) | Loopback TCP only. Limit: loopback Host required; Origin headers and bodies rejected. |

| `--admin-write-addr` (`/v1/revision`, `/v1/config[/validate]`) | Loopback + Bearer token from a 0400/0600 single-link file. Limit: constant-time compare, exact `If-Match`, explicit resource roots. |

| LSAPI control and generation files | Root-only control socket. Limit: web pools mmap the generation file read-only; parent must not be group-writable. |

| ACME store · DNS token · integrity key · admin token | Owner and mode checks on the descriptor. Limit: no symlink following, bounded reads. |

## Audit posture

| Date | Scope | Headline |

| 2026-08-30 | #362–#368 | No exploitable High. Limit: five low/informational fixes. |

| 2026-09-06 | Five findings | H2/H3 reservation leaks, gzip accounting, Basic-auth merging. Limit: plus authenticated-static caching and UA memo keys. |

| 2026-09-16 | Twelve fixes | Unreadable `.htaccess` fail-closed, PROXY loopback claims, `[P]` screening. Limit: plus CGI deny-list, never-root, single Content-Length. |

| 2026-10-06 | #560–#575 (0.0.4) | H3 budget at `Connected`, RFC 9112 intake, docroot-confined `AuthUserFile`. Limit: plus POST-only purge, fuzz targets, RustSec CI. |

| — | 0.0.5 (#579–#593) | 15 findings. |

| 2026-10-13 | 0.0.6 (#594–#611) | Truncated LSAPI/FastCGI aborts, HPACK over-cap stream error. Limit: plus H3 backpressure, OCSP SAN checks. |

| 2026-10-14..24 | 0.0.7–0.1.5, bug-bash 1–16, #1138 | OLS parity, APR1/MD5-crypt + auth rate limit, SHA-256 vary hashing. Limit: plus WAF peer-UID, rustls 0.23.46. |

| 2026-10-25 | 0.1.10 bug/perf bash | 23 issues, 22 fixed, one closed by decision. Limit: no-follow walk, H1 send deadlines, dropped-POST replay. |

| 2026-11-10..11 | 0.2.0 review of v0.1.10..v0.1.12 + the 2026-10-30 sweep (#1193–#1230) | 28 issues fixed, each with a regression test; two read-only reviews found no wrong-content path in the response memo or page cache. Limit: upstream WebSocket handshake validation, no credentials in capsule revalidation, every gzip member decoded, LSAPI packet order, error-log escaping, QUIC self-closing Initials (pre-handshake memory), shared cache bodies off the server-wide H3 budget, listener address checks, CPU steering gated on NIC queues. |

Gates re-run after each round: full suite (3,171 tests at 0.2.0; 3,068 at 0.1.10), fast-memo parity, cache xurl/scheme/xhost, h2spec 146/146.

        i   Reporting
Use private responsible disclosure per `SECURITY.md`, not a public issue. Findings reconcile against source and regression tests. Nothing here proves production exploitation, or absence of other vulnerabilities.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Operations (https://httpjet.net/docs/operations)
SUMMARY: Deploy, upgrade, roll back, and recover safely.
==============================================================================

# Operations & deployment

A fresh packaged installation runs a static service as a dedicated account. The reference configurations below also show optional socket activation, persistent PHP pools and container deployment for operators who need them.

## Installation

### Fresh installer

For a fresh Linux server, use the signed installer . It selects the native package or portable archive, starts the welcome page on ports 80 and 443, and creates a unique self-signed certificate. A browser warning is expected until a trusted certificate is configured. io_uring must be available.

### Source build

To build and deploy from source instead, install the binary at a stable path *outside* Cargo's `target/` so a later `cargo clean` cannot delete what a running unit depends on:

           source install
```
cargo build --locked --release -p httpjet
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/httpjet --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin httpjet
sudo install -d /usr/local/httpjet/bin /usr/local/httpjet/conf /usr/local/httpjet/logs
sudo install -m0755 target/release/httpjet /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet

# an existing LiteSpeed tree works as-is — validate it first, as root AND as the service user
sudo /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check --strict
sudo -u httpjet /usr/local/httpjet/bin/httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check --strict

# minimal loopback example unit (no TLS, no PHP, no cache); it runs /usr/bin/httpjet on /etc/httpjet/litespeed
sudo install -m0755 target/release/httpjet /usr/bin/httpjet
sudo install -d /etc/httpjet && sudo cp -a examples/litespeed /etc/httpjet/litespeed
sudo install -m0644 packaging/systemd/httpjet-example.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now httpjet-example
```

        !   Review before start
The example units bind loopback and use example document roots. Set listeners, domains, docroots, TLS material, writable paths and the service identity deliberately before enabling a public service. A permission-preparing `ExecStartPre` that runs as root and then drops to the unprivileged account is the reference shape.

## Advanced systemd socket activation

The following reference topology is optional. The fresh installer uses a single static service and does not set up these socket, PHP-pool or firewall units.

> [Diagram: systemd-units] Five core units (plus the optional edge firewall). The socket units own the listening fds; the boot gate keeps the public listeners closed until the PHP pool can answer; the web tier adopts the fds and dials the pool. Restarting the web tier or reloading the pool never closes a listener.

| Unit | Role |

| `httpjet.socket` | N× `:80` TCP, N× `:443` TCP, N× `:443` UDP with `ReusePort=yes`, `Backlog=8192`. The multiplicity reproduces the per-worker SO_REUSEPORT fan-out, so N must equal `serve --workers`. Static (not enabled under `sockets.target`); pulled in by the service after the gate to avoid a cold-boot ordering cycle. |

| `httpjet-boot-ready.service` | Boot-only oneshot gate, availability-first: the `Type=notify` LSAPI pool is the one hard dependency; databases/caches are ordered but not required — it waits up to 300 s, then proceeds with a loud warning so a cold boot with a slow database still serves static + warm cache + stale-if-error. Later backend maintenance cannot tear down the sockets. |

| `httpjet.service` | The web tier under a dedicated user. Limit: you check drop-ins before reasoning about flags. |

| `httpjet-lsphp.socket` | Owns the LSAPI Unix listener (mode 0600, backlog 8192, `RemoveOnStop`). Never restart it during a reload or supervisor deploy. |

| `httpjet-lsphp.service` | `httpjet lsphp …`, `Type=notify` (active only after a marker-attributed LSAPI response), `ExecReload=httpjet lsphp-reload …`, its own identity, `RuntimeDirectory=httpjet` for the control socket and generation file. |

| `httpjet-edge-firewall.service` | Optional oneshot edge firewall (`scripts/httpjet-edge-firewall.sh`) for origins without a cloud firewall: restricts new `:80`/`:443` connections to Cloudflare IPv4 + private ranges (keep its list in step with the XML `T` entries). |

**Hardening:** You apply `systemd/httpjet.service.d/zz-hardening.conf` as reference only. It sets `ProtectSystem=strict`, private tmp/devices, and empty capabilities. You enforce `@system-service` seccomp only after a clean soak. Measured score: 9.0 → 1.9.

        i   Scope of the zero-loss guarantee
Socket activation eliminates RSTs of *new and queued* connections across a deploy. Requests the old process has already accepted — h1/h2 mid-serve and especially h3/QUIC streams — still drain under `TimeoutStopSec`. "Never drops a connection" means never RSTs a new or queued one.

## The persistent PHP pool

Static and proxy deployments need no PHP. For LSAPI, run the pool as its own unit and point the web tier at it; the units above wire the socket, the root-only control socket and the 16-byte generation file. Routine opcache recycle is `systemctl reload httpjet-lsphp.service` — synchronous and candidate-first. Reserve a hard restart of the pool *service* for supervisor binary/unit changes; verify the listener inode is unchanged before and after. Reference: LSAPI & PHP .

           replace the supervisor without closing the listener
```
before=$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' /run/httpjet/php.sock)
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart httpjet-lsphp.service                 # the SERVICE only — never the .socket
test "$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' /run/httpjet/php.sock)" = "$before"
test "$(stat -Lc %s /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation)" = 16
ss -xlnH | awk '$5 == "/run/httpjet/php.sock" {print $4}'    # Send-Q should equal the XML backlog
```

## Safe change workflow

- **Edit in a reviewable change** Configuration tree or application content.

- **`check --strict`** The deploy gate. SIGHUP with a broken config keeps the old generation, but the check should catch it first.

- **Test in isolation** Alternate ports, a separate PHP socket, a separate cache store path, low worker/child counts. Kill test instances by exact PID; a leaked SO_REUSEPORT instance silently shares the port with independent cache and htaccess state.

- **Apply** `systemctl reload httpjet` (SIGHUP) for vhost/rewrite/access/expires/tuning/certificate changes; `systemctl restart httpjet` for the binary or boot-owned resources; the write API for validated in-memory replacement.

- **Verify on loopback, then watch** `curl -sk -H 'Host: …' https://127.0.0.1/…`, the journal, `httpjet_requests_total` and 5xx counters. Purge any outer cache if an incorrect cacheable response reached it.

## Binary deploy and rollback

> [Diagram: deploy-flow] The deploy gate chain. The repository's scripts/deploy-lscache.sh automates this for one deployment (strict check, co-listener guard, external-lsphp recurrence guard, health probe with automatic revert to the previous binary, capsule purge gate); the shape is what matters for any deployment.

- **Kill switch: cache**: Drop `--page-cache` from the unit (a drop-in override) and restart; the cache code is inert without the flag.

- **Kill switch: capsules**: Drop the `--xf-capsule*` flags and restart.

- **Kill switch: fast memo**: `--no-fast-memo` or `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0`.

- **Kill switch: WAF**: Remove `--waf-sidecar-addr` (the seam is completely inert without it).

- **Rollback**: Keep the previous binary beside the current one (`bin/httpjet.prev`); restore and restart. A rollback does not remove bad objects already stored in the origin cache (purge) or at the CDN edge (purge the zone).

- **Start limits**: `StartLimitBurst=5` per 60 s: more than five restarts a minute trips systemd and takes the service down until `systemctl reset-failed`. The persistence gate restarts the service — run it once.

The production build uses profile-guided optimization (`scripts/build-pgo.sh`: instrument → drive a representative loopback workload → rebuild). PGO scratch data is kept off tmpfs. Never benchmark a non-PGO binary against a PGO one.

## What SIGHUP reloads

Vhost maps, rewrites, document roots, contexts, access/expires/tuning settings, cache policy gates, and TLS certificates on an unchanged listener topology. Signal streams (`SIGHUP`, `SIGUSR1`, `SIGUSR2`) are registered immediately at runtime startup so a certbot or reload signal arriving during boot queues cleanly instead of terminating the process. A change that needs a restart (listener addresses, QUIC enablement, PHP topology, cache-store identity, privileges, log paths) is logged as "requires a restart — keeping current config" and nothing changes. A reload that would 404 a mapped vhost because its per-vhost file failed to load is refused. The dictionary registry is retained across SIGHUP (rotation needs a restart). Full semantics: Admin API & reload .

## Observability checklist

See Observability for metrics and logs.

You check loopback surfaces first.

You pair counters with a process monitor.

## Container deployment

For a ready-to-run Docker image on Linux or Docker Desktop with WSL 2, follow the Docker quickstart . It includes the seccomp profile required for io_uring and publishes HTTP on 8080 and HTTPS on 8443. Microsoft's separate WSL Containers runtime denied io_uring in the environment tested.

### Hardened OCI example

`packaging/oci/` is an adoption example, not a prescription. The image runs as numeric UID/GID `10001:10001`, binds unprivileged ports, needs no capabilities; the compose file adds a read-only root filesystem, drops every capability, sets `no-new-privileges`, and mounts a small `noexec,nosuid,nodev` `/tmp`. Because Moby's default seccomp allowlist omits io_uring, `seccomp-httpjet.json` is the pinned Moby default plus only `io_uring_setup`, `io_uring_enter` and `io_uring_register` (ptrace/`process_vm_*` gated on `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`).

| Path | Access | Purpose |

| `/run/httpjet-certs` | read-only | TLS certificate + key (no key ships in the image; generate one for `example.test`). |

| `/var/lib/httpjet` | read-write | Page-cache files and the integrity key. |

| `/etc/httpjet/litespeed/logs` | read-write | Access/error logs. |

| `/etc/httpjet/litespeed/{conf,example}` | image read-only | LiteSpeed XML and static content. |

| `/tmp` | bounded tmpfs | Temporary runtime files. |

           build, run, smoke
```
docker compose -f packaging/oci/compose.yaml up --build     # publishes 8080/tcp, 8443/tcp AND 8443/udp
docker run … --security-opt seccomp=/abs/path/seccomp-httpjet.json …   # a hand-written run must pass the profile explicitly
bash scripts/oci-smoke.sh                                    # read-only root, UID 10001, caps dropped, real HTTP/3 through the UDP port
```

A seccomp denial is a startup/test failure — do not work around it with `--privileged`, `--cap-add` or `seccomp=unconfined`; narrow the runtime policy or pick a supported host. Rootless engines may add memlock, UDP or io_uring restrictions of their own. The image health check calls `/__hj_cache_ready`, so readiness means the cache boot scan finished, not that a user URL was warmed.

## Release and upgrade discipline

A public release must provide portable x86_64 and aarch64 artifacts, checksums, signatures or attestations, an SBOM, the GPL-3.0 license text and a documented Linux/kernel/libc floor; architecture-tuned PGO helpers must not be uploaded as generic binaries (production builds and gathers PGO natively on each architecture). Upgrades preserve the tree, dictionaries and state; stage and validate the new binary before restart; keep a known-good binary. Dictionary rotation: write the new file atomically, validate, restart, expect old-generation cache entries to become safe misses. Dependency upgrades run through `scripts/update-deps.sh` and the full suite. See the changelog/release page for current dependency versions.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Observability (https://httpjet.net/docs/observability)
SUMMARY: Read metrics, logs, and request traces.
==============================================================================

# Observability

Everything httpjet tells you about itself: **Prometheus metrics** on a loopback listener, the **cache-entries** report, access and error **logs** in text or JSON with an optional syslog tap, per-request **correlation ids**, the telemetry TSV and PHP slow log, opt-in **OpenTelemetry** traces and metrics, and the profiling endpoints. All control surfaces are loopback-only by design.

## Prometheus metrics

`--metrics-addr` (default `127.0.0.1:9090`; empty disables) serves `/metrics` in Prometheus text format. You watch the families below first:

| Family | Meaning. Limit: |
| `httpjet_requests_total` | Served requests. Limit: pair with 5xx counters. |
| `httpjet_pagecache_*` | Cache activity. Limit: watch hit ratio first. |
| `httpjet_lsapi_*` | PHP pool health. Limit: watch TTFB next. |

| Metric | Type | Meaning |

| Requests & connections |

| httpjet_requests_total · httpjet_active_requests · httpjet_active_connections | counter / gauge | Served requests, requests in the response-head phase, open connections. |

| httpjet_requests_by_vhost · httpjet_responses_by_vhost · httpjet_request_duration_by_vhost_seconds | labeled | Per-vhost volume, status class and handle() wall time. |

| httpjet_status_{2xx,3xx,4xx,5xx} · httpjet_status_{400,403,404,410,414,429,500,502,503,504} | counter | Status classes and the interesting exact codes. |

| httpjet_proto_{h1,h2,h3} · httpjet_served_{static,php,proxy} | counter | Wire protocol and terminal mix. |

| httpjet_request_duration_seconds · httpjet_phase_{rewrite,cache_lookup,compress,upstream}_seconds | histogram | Total handle() time and sampled per-stage costs (upstream = proxy checkout → response head). |

| httpjet_tls_handshakes_{full,resumed}_total · httpjet_conn_{idle,peer}_closes_total | counter | Full vs resumed TLS handshakes; connection closes by idle timeout vs peer FIN/RST. |

| httpjet_h2_rapid_reset_goaways_total · httpjet_h2_send_stall_resets_total · httpjet_h3_send_stall_resets_total | counter | H2 connections closed with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM when cancellations outrun the time-refilled rapid-reset budget; H2 and H3 response streams reset on send stall. |

| httpjet_h2_conn_ends_total{reason} | counter | Every HTTP/2 connection of the io_uring transport, counted once under the first cause recorded for it: `idle` (our idle GOAWAY), `peer_eof`, `peer_goaway`, `protocol_error` (our error GOAWAY), `io_error`, `shutdown`, `other`. Behind a proxy that never resumes TLS, each ended connection costs a full handshake, so this shows who ends them. |

| httpjet_htaccess_parses_total | counter | Access files parsed by the current configuration generation's `.htaccess` cache, re-parses after an edit included. Parsing is single-flight per file and happens before the first connection is accepted. |

| httpjet_throttle_{allowed,rejected}_total | counter | Per-IP throttle decisions (0 when disabled). |

| httpjet_body_buffer_{bytes,capacity_bytes,rejected_total} | gauge / counter | The process-wide request-body budget. |

| Fast path & rewrite |

| httpjet_fast_memo_{hits,stores,ineligible}_total | counter | Finished-response memo activity; *ineligible* = the chain refused the store (see `httpjet check`). |

| httpjet_fast_cookie_{none,member_session,benign_only}_total · httpjet_fast_bridge_total{reason} | counter | Cookie shape of fast-path GET/HEADs and attribution of why a GET/HEAD fell off the on-core fast path into the tokio bridge. |

| httpjet_rewrite_outcome_{hits,misses,uncacheable}_total · httpjet_rewrite_ua_classify_entries | counter / gauge | Rewrite-outcome cache and UA-classification table size. |

| Page cache |

| httpjet_pagecache_{hits,misses,stores,purges,purges_received,store_purge_rejections,expired_misses}_total · httpjet_pagecache_hit_ratio · httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real | counter / gauge | Core activity; `_real` excludes loopback probes; `httpjet_cache_{hits,misses}_by_vhost{vhost}` split it per vhost and `httpjet_pagecache_evictions_total` counts size/TTL teardowns. Telemetry twins `httpjet_cache_{hits,misses,bypass,stale_serves,sie_serves,admitted,rejected}` and `httpjet_disp_*` (why a response was or wasn't stored) plus `httpjet_cache_admit_ratio`. |

| httpjet_pagecache_entries · _memory_bytes · _hot_bytes · _decoded_entries · _meta_{raw,compressed}_bytes · _tag_{keys,memberships,index_bytes} · _tag_purge_{tombstones,floor_milliseconds} | gauge | Exact RAM accounting of the index and tag indexes. |

| httpjet_pagecache_ghost_hits_total | counter | Misses on a key the file tier had evicted while its copy was still fresh: misses a larger `--page-cache-disk-mem` could have served. An estimate (a bounded sample of recent evictions; later tag purges are not subtracted). Compare with `httpjet_pagecache_disk_evictions_total` before resizing the tier. |

| httpjet_pagecache_disk_{bytes,max_bytes} · _disk_evictions_total · _disk_evict_age_{lt_1h,1h_6h,6h_24h,ge_24h}_total · _swept_expired_total | gauge / counter | File-tier footprint vs budget, LRU evictions by entry age, proactive expiry sweeps. |

| httpjet_pagecache_disk_{read,write,full}_errors_total · _missing_file_invalidations_total · _orphan_{reclaimed,deferred}_total · _meta_decode_errors_total · _key_id_collisions_total · _poisoned_locks_total | counter | Health: every one of these should be flat. Poisoned locks nonzero = indexes may be inconsistent. `httpjet_pagecache_integrity_active` = 1 once the file-tier integrity key is installed. |

| httpjet_pagecache_dict_recompress_total · _dict_recompress_bytes_total · httpjet_pagecache_refresh_inflight | counter / gauge | Store-time dictionary recompressions (bounded background pool); stale-while-revalidate refreshes in flight. |

| httpjet_pagecache_shared_path_{public_routes,canary_skipped}_total · _shared_paths_{matchers,canary_percent} | counter / gauge | Shared-paths routing. |
