| httpjet_xf_capsule_{hits,misses,stale_hits,dedicated_stores,canary_filtered}_total · _hits_by_class_total · _shell_age_secs | counter / summary | XenForo capsule tier. |

| httpjet_process_rss_bytes · httpjet_process_rss_anon_bytes · httpjet_pagecache_unaccounted_rss_anon_bytes | gauge | Process RSS and the part the cache accounting cannot explain. |

| LSAPI / PHP |

| httpjet_lsapi_{acquire,dispatch,ttfb}_seconds | histogram | Pool contention · backend call · request-committed-to-first-byte. |

| httpjet_lsapi_generation_advances_total · _stale_{idle,checked_out}_drops_total · _stale_worker_retire_{signals,failures}_total · _worker_attribution_failures_total · _eagain_{retries,terminal_exhaustions}_total · _reset_replays_total · _reset_replay_exhaustions_total | counter | External-pool generation lifecycle, backlog pressure, and fresh-dial replays of requests a retiring worker reset before any response byte. |

| Proxy |

| httpjet_proxy_peer_{healthy,probes_total,health_transitions_total,active_requests,selections_total,prehead_failures_total} · httpjet_proxy_failover_total | labeled | Per-peer (labels `scope`, `group`, `peer` = ordinal) health and selection; failovers served by a non-primary peer. |

| Logging, OTel, debug |

| httpjet_log_{access,error,vhost}_dropped_lines_total | counter | Access (unified + per-vhost), per-vhost error, and per-vhost writer log lines shed by the bounded writer queues (65,536 lines / 64 MiB per logger). |

| httpjet_otel_spans_{queue,dropped_total,exported_total,export_failed_total} · httpjet_otel_http_{exports,export_failures}_total | gauge / counter | Span queue depth and loss; collector HTTP outcomes (observable even when the collector is down). |

| httpjet_debug_cache_entries_{renders,throttled}_total | counter | Renders of the `/cache-entries` report and locally throttled requests for it. |

## The cache-entries report

You fetch `GET /cache-entries` on the metrics listener. It reports entries, bytes, and health. Limit: diagnostic routes require your Bearer [REDACTED]; missing tokens return 403.

## Logs

          Access log  Error log  Syslog tap  Per-vhost logs

The unified access log (path from the XML; combined format with a trailing `reqid=` token) writes from a dedicated non-blocking task with a bounded queue (65,536 lines and 64 MiB per logger; `httpjet_log_access_dropped_lines_total` counts sheds), opens and rotates without following symlinks (`O_NOFOLLOW`), rolls asynchronously at 50 MiB and prunes after 30 days (`HTTPJET_ACCESS_ROLLING_BYTES`, `HTTPJET_ACCESS_KEEP_DAYS`). `HTTPJET_ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT=json` emits one object per line with a fixed field order:

               access · json
```
{"ts":"17/Sep/2026:11:02:09 +0000","client_ip":"203.0.113.9","remote_user":null,"method":"GET","uri":"/threads/hello.123/","protocol":"HTTP/2.0","status":200,"bytes":41211,"referer":null,"user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 …","reqid":"3f9c2a7b81d04e55"}
```

Unix-socket peers render the literal host `unix:`. Cache disposition is in the response header (`x-litespeed-cache`), not the log line; join on `reqid`.

The rolling `httpjet_error.log` (and captured backend stderr) is text by default. `HTTPJET_ERROR_LOG_FORMAT=json` switches to JSON events with `schema_version 1`: `timestamp_unix_ms`, `level`, nullable `target`, `message`, and a `fields` object that keeps tracing WARN/ERROR fields named rather than flattened. JSON-only redaction replaces values of authorization/cookie/password/token/secret/key/credential-named fields and suppresses whole values that look like credential syntax or URL userinfo — a conservative heuristic, not a guarantee. Bounds: 32 fields, 1024-char values, 8192-char messages; inputs over 32 KiB become `[OVERSIZED]`. The stdout/journald tracing formatter (`RUST_LOG`) is unaffected.

`HTTPJET_SYSLOG_TARGET` mirrors every rendered access line as an RFC 5424 (or 3164) datagram from the writer task — request path untouched, file logging unaffected, send failures counted. The MSG part is the rendered line itself, so existing parsers keep working. Targets: `udp://host:514`, bare `host:port`, or a unix-dgram path like `/run/systemd/journal/syslog`. Facility/severity/hostname/app-name knobs are on the CLI page .

A vhost's ` ` block with `useServer=0` and a `fileName` gives it its own access and error files (rolling size and keep-days per file; `logHeaders` 7 = combined format plus the quoted `Host`). Log paths are boot-owned: they cannot be changed through the write API.

## Request ids

Every request gets a 64-bit correlation id (a per-process seed mixed into a lock-free counter — no syscall, no RNG on the hot path; a background stale-while-revalidate refresh inherits its parent's id) that appears in the access, error and PHP-slow logs. `--request-id-header` also echoes it as `X-Request-Id` so a client or CDN can join a response to the server-side records. Off by default.

## Telemetry TSV and the PHP slow log

- **`--telemetry-file logs/telemetry.tsv`**: Appends a cumulative snapshot row of the in-RAM aggregates every `--telemetry-flush-secs` (30): durability across restarts and a self-contained time series (~1 MB/day). The `:9090` endpoint works without it.

- **`--php-slow-log logs/php-slow.tsv`**: A TSV line for every LSAPI request whose render TTFB exceeds `--php-slow-threshold-ms` (50), plus a 1-in-128 sample of *all* PHP requests as the population baseline — the per-URL / user-class attribution behind `httpjet_lsapi_ttfb_seconds`. Rolls at 64 MiB, gzip archives, 7-day prune.

These files produced the 2026-08-30 sample on Performance : mean request 9.99 ms, of which 8.96 ms is inside PHP.

## OpenTelemetry --features otel

Build with `--features otel`, then set `HTTPJET_OTEL=1`; without it no provider or exporter is created, and requesting it in a binary without the feature fails startup. The official Rust SDK exports OTLP HTTP/protobuf to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` (complete URL). `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1` adds a 30-second periodic metrics reader to `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`.

> [Diagram: otel-spans] What gets exported. One root span per request at the dispatch boundary, backend client spans, internal stage spans on sampled requests, and a loss-accounted batch exporter. Spans carry status and bounded internal attributes only — no headers, bodies, URLs or error text.

- **Sampling and trust.** `HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` (default 0.01) ratio-samples roots; children follow. Inbound `traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` are discarded by default — clients cannot dictate parentage or force sampling. `HTTPJET_OTEL_TRUSTED_PARENTS` lists exact gateway IPs (direct peers on a known non-PROXY listener) allowed to supply a single version-00 traceparent; a listed gateway controls parentage *and sampling*, so it must strip public trace headers first. Do not list a CDN merely because it forwards client IPs.

- **Propagation.** Named configured proxy targets and WebSocket maps receive the generated traceparent; LSAPI receives it as `HTTP_TRACEPARENT`; ad-hoc targets get nothing.

- **Completion.** Spans end at local write completion. Limit: peer receipt stays unproven.

- **Bounds.** You queue 2048 spans in 256-span batches. Limit: saturation drops telemetry, never serving.

- **Metrics instruments.** `httpjet.pipeline.requests.completed` and `httpjet.pipeline.response_head.duration` (seconds, bounded status labels), plus `httpjet.otel.http.exports`.

           enable
```
HTTPJET_OTEL=1 HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS=1 HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO=0.05 \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/metrics \
httpjet --root /abs/root serve …
```

## The read-only status API

`--admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9091` exposes `GET /v1/status`: generation, configuration fingerprint, listener names, vhost names, upstream peer health/active/selection counters and page-cache aggregates — never paths, credentials or cached URLs. Full contract on Admin API & reload .

## Debugging a request

           tracing filters
```
RUST_LOG=debug,hj_rewrite=trace httpjet --root /abs/root serve --http-addr 127.0.0.1:8080 …
# where to look: vhost resolution (hj-core router) → rewrite outcome (hj-rewrite eval) →
#   cache lookup (httpjet lscache) → terminal (pipeline dispatch) → response (handler)
```

Production units run `RUST_LOG=httpjet=info`; anything you must see in the journal should log at WARN or above.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Admin API & reload (https://httpjet.net/docs/admin-api)
SUMMARY: Check status and reload configuration safely.
==============================================================================

# Admin API & reload

You change a running httpjet three ways: SIGHUP, read-only status API, transactional write API. One publication coordinator serves all writers. Each change publishes fully, or not at all.

| Way | Does | Limit |

| **SIGHUP** | Republish on-disk tree | Needs shell/systemd access |

| **Read API** | Status only | Changes nothing; loopback only |

| **Write API** | Publish memory bundle | Volatile; token required |

## SIGHUP

Run `systemctl reload httpjet` (or `kill -HUP`). Re-parse, build, publish via `config_transaction::Coordinator`. Builds precede certificate reload. Preserves `--no-mtls`, `--per-ip-rate`. Journal outcomes:

- **published**: New generation serving; in-flight requests finish on the old one; certificate handles reloaded for the unchanged listener topology.

- **requires a restart — keeping current config**: The diff touched a boot-owned resource (hot reload covers vhost/rewrite/access/expires/tuning, cache policy gates and TLS material).

- **reload would 404 mapped vhost(s)**: A per-vhost file failed to load; the old generation is kept rather than serving 404s.

- **reload rejected**: Parse or build error — nothing changes.

- **certificate reload failed**: Application state published; certificates whose reload failed are retained.

## Read-only status API

Opt in: `serve --admin-addr 127.0.0.1:9091`. Non-loopback rejected. Bind failure aborts startup. Separate from metrics. Changes nothing. No profiling or purge.

           **GET** /v1/status · schema_version 1
```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9091/v1/status | jq .
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "generation": 3,                       # process-local, starts at 1; rejected candidates stay invisible
  "config_fingerprint": "9f2c…",      # of the normalized model's Debug form — comparable within one binary version only
  "listeners": [{"name":"https","tls":true,"unix":false}],   # configured names + flags, NOT bound addresses
  "vhosts": ["example.test"],
  "upstreams": [{"scope":"server","group":"application","peer":0,"healthy":true,"active":2,"selections":1290}],
  "page_cache": {"entries": 41210, "memory_bytes": 60817408, "hits": 1904411, "misses": 88123},   # or null when off
  "truncated": false
}
```

Returns no values, paths, credentials, headers, keys, URLs. Limits: names 256 chars, rows 256, response 1 MiB (503 beyond). GET only, exact path (405/404 otherwise). Host: loopback or `localhost`. Rejects Origin, bodies. Sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, closes connections. Caps: 4 KiB / 32 fields, four tasks, 5 s deadlines. Local users trusted. Never proxy it.

## Transactional configuration API

Writes need separate opt-in. Read listener never enables them. Set all three:

           **serve** · enabling writes
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … \
  --admin-write-addr 127.0.0.1:9092 \
  --admin-token-file /operator/private/token \       # 64 lowercase hex chars (32 random bytes), mode 0400/0600, one hard link, root or service uid
  --admin-resource-root /operator/content \          # repeatable; up to 32 existing directories; "/" is refused
  --admin-resource-root /etc/letsencrypt/live
```

> [Diagram: reload-transaction] Validate, then publish with an exact precondition. Every write carries If-Match with the revision it read; a stale revision or an out-of-band publication (SIGHUP included) loses with a conflict rather than silently rebuilding against newer state. Publication is volatile: the on-disk XML is never rewritten and a restart returns to it.

### Endpoints and contract

| Request | Behavior |

| `GET /v1/revision` | The current revision: a random 128-bit process incarnation plus a monotonic generation, so a restart can never revive an earlier process's revision. |

| `POST /v1/config/validate` | Builds the candidate, returns a redacted verdict, publishes and persists nothing. |

| `PUT /v1/config` | Builds, rechecks the exact revision under the publication boundary, publishes, transfers health-check ownership, notifies bridge admission. Returns the next revision and `persistence: volatile`. An interrupted response after publication does not roll back — re-read the revision to reconcile. |

Frame each write exactly:

- `Authorization: Bearer `: missing/duplicate/malformed → 401, body unread, constant-time compare, token never logged.

- Exact quoted `If-Match`: missing → 428, stale → conflict.

- `Content-Type: application/json`, one `Content-Length` ≤ 1 MiB, headers ≤ 8 KiB / 32, deadline 5 s.

- Host: bound loopback, or `localhost: `. Rejected: encodings, Origin, Expect, Upgrade, Trailer.

- One request per connection, never pipelined. Max four connections, one build. Lock ≤ 5 s, candidate ≤ 10 s. Late builds never publish.

           **body** · the in-memory bundle (exactly three fields)
```
{
  "server_xml": " … ",
  "vhosts": [ {"name": "example.test", "xml": " … "} ],
  "mime": "text/html = html, htm\n"
}
```

`hj-config::parse_bundle` normalizes bundles. Never reads `configFile` paths. Limits: 1 MiB, ≤128 vhosts, one root, no DTD, ≤64 nesting. Bad declarations fail. Errors carry no submitted data. Root from startup.

### What a transaction may change

Boundary, stated once for this page: reloadable publishes live, boot-owned returns `restart_required`, nothing half-applies.

#### Reloadable (application)

- Listener→vhost mappings on the unchanged listener set
- Rewrites, document roots, contexts, static locations
- Reloadable request settings, cache policy gates, expires
- Proxy and FastCGI processors, and proxy groups (health schedulers restart cleanly)
- GeoIP database and upstream client-cert files — inside a resource root

#### Constrained trust (TCP transaction)

- Listener identity/routing, PROXY-protocol policy, TLS certificate/key/CA/CRL material — through prepared same-socket TCP successors
- An existing `--http-uds` endpoint is handed off
- An already-enabled QUIC endpoint adopts the new TLS/mTLS policy for future handshakes without rebinding UDP
- UDS ext-processor addresses authorized against resource roots

#### restart_required

- Listener addresses, count, order, secure/plain roles; QUIC enablement; UDS topology
- PHP topology and pools (LSAPI processors)
- Cache-store identity and boot-time cache caps/policy
- User/group, namespace and isolation settings, per-vhost log resources
- `useIpInProxyHeader` and the whole ` ` block

**Resource policy.** Keep candidate files inside an `--admin-resource-root`: docroots, contexts, GeoIP, certs, TLS paths. Rejects traversal, relative, missing, escaping links. Authorization, not sandbox. Failures return categories only.

**Cache namespaces.** First publication creates an epoch. Keys use epoch + generation. Old renders cannot overwrite. Old roots cannot replay. See Page cache → generations .

**Shutdown.** Coordinator closes first. Candidates get `Closed`. Listener drops tasks. Blocking work resists forced stop. Deadline bounds waiting only.

## The reload boundary in depth

Live state: one generation — application state plus listener generations. Each listener pins bind, PROXY, TLS, identity, drain control. Connections pin trust at acceptance (`ServingView` via `CoreHandler`). Compatible reloads stay visible live. Incompatible trust retires the group: H2 GOAWAY, H1 close-after-response, H3 bounded drain. Old connections never reach new routes.

         Owner table: resource, owner, replacement rule

| Resource | Owner | Replacement rule |

| TCP addresses, workers, fds | listener plan + `uring` groups | Same-socket successors behind barrier; identities verified. |

| UDS path, permissions | listener adoption | Distinct owned path; never unlink inherited sockets. |

| TLS acceptor, mTLS, PROXY | per-core TLS bridge | Pinned per connection, per generation. |

| Certificates / SNI map | `CertReloadHandle` | One validated snapshot per generation; swaps not atomic. |

| QUIC endpoint / UDP fds | `QuicResources` | Stable UDP; policy handle for future handshakes. |

| kTLS template | TLS worker | New handshakes only; keys connection-owned. |

| ACME overlays, OCSP slots | feature runtimes | Generation-owned targets; leases retained. |

| PHP supervisor / external worker registry | startup | Restart-required. |

| Log writers, budgets, metrics, admission | process-owned Arcs | Retained; reservations preserved. |

| User/group, privileges, namespaces | startup | Never runtime-acquired; rejected first. |

TCP trust order: authenticate → check revision → diff (retain unchanged) → acquire owned candidates → start behind barrier (readiness ≠ permission) → validate (failure drops all) → recheck + publish atomically → activate/stop acceptors → retire old, bounded, outside lock.

## Reproducible checks

           **tests** · isolated loopback listeners and temporary trees
```
cargo test --locked -p httpjet admin
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet                       # served-file replacement, validate-only non-mutation, stale writes, SIGHUP restoration, restart incarnation
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --memo-parity         # 48-cell memo parity across a publication
python3 -B scripts/admin-runtime-test.py --binary target/debug/httpjet --persistent-cache    # authenticated on-disk containers, hits across publication, boot-scan restoration
```

SUMMARY: See how the server fits together.
==============================================================================

# Architecture

httpjet is a Cargo workspace with **one binary crate** and **nineteen `hj-*` library crates**. Roughly 3,200 test functions span the workspace (3,171 green at v0.2.0).

## Workspace shape

The graph is acyclic and `hj-config` sits at the root. `hj-core` is the small frozen seam for every handler. Two crates, `hj-acme` and `hj-ocsp`, link only behind build features. The binary is the only crate that sees everything. Transports, protocols, gateways and the cache evolve behind `hj-core`. Request-aware page-cache glue also lives in the binary.

           Browse workspace on GitHub ↗
           1 binary + 19 libraries
           Rust 1.99.1 · edition 2024 · v0.2.0
           Acyclic; hj-config at the root
           ≈3,000 test functions
           Vendored forks: monoio, monoio-rustls (real writev), dashmap, pprof

## Crate dependency graph

`hj-config` parses LiteSpeed XML into one normalized model. `hj-core` re-exports that model for every downstream crate.

- hj-config XML tree → model · parse_bundle hj-core the frozen contract · ReqCtx · Router · budgets handlers & transports (depend on hj-core) hj-tls hj-h2 hj-lsapi hj-fastcgi hj-static hj-compress hj-proxy hj-acl hj-extension hj-http (ServeConfig) hj-pagecache (uses hj-cache) hj-cache sharded byte-LRU hj-acme · hj-ocsp --features acme / ocsp no direct hj-core dep hj-rewrite hj-log hj-geo hj-cache httpjet uring transport · pipeline · lscache glue · admin config_transaction · resource_generation · waf · otel hj-config → hj-core → handlers and transports → the httpjet binary. ## Crate map Crate Role hj-core The frozen handler seam. Limit: changing its types requires updating every dependent. hj-config LiteSpeed XML to one normalized model. Limit: defaults fail closed. hj-tls One rustls config for TCP and QUIC. Limit: SNI uses no cert-name-match, like OLS. hj-acme feature HTTP-01 and DNS-01 issuance and renewal. Limit: links only behind `acme`. hj-ocsp feature Bounded OCSP fetch and validation. Limit: needs OpenSSL 3.x and the `ocsp` feature. hj-http Shared connection-tuning from ` `. Limit: it holds no transport. hj-h2 The native HTTP/2 server and HPACK codec. Limit: one task serves each connection. hj-lsapi LSAPI codec, pool and `lsphp` supervisor. Limit: the jail fails closed. hj-fastcgi FastCGI codec, pool and handler. Limit: use only explicit `fcgi`/`fastcgi` processors. hj-static Static files with ranges and conditionals. Limit: opens stay beneath the docroot. hj-cache Shared sharded byte-LRU primitive. Limit: sizing comes from `CacheCaps`. hj-pagecache The origin page store. Limit: request-aware glue lives in the binary. hj-compress gzip, brotli and zstd response encoding. Limit: negotiation follows server priority. hj-rewrite mod_rewrite and `.htaccess` evaluation. Limit: lookahead uses `fancy-regex` fallback. hj-proxy Reverse proxy, WebSocket and SSE relay. Limit: upstreams use h1, `h2://` or `h2s://`. hj-acl ACLs, real-IP, throttle and geo rules. Limit: geo resolves to CIDR sets at build. hj-geo Offline GeoIP and ASN sources. Limit: it makes no runtime fetches. hj-log Non-blocking access and error logging. Limit: the syslog tap is optional. hj-extension Compile-time handlers and transforms. Limit: the shipped registry is empty. httpjet The binary with transport and pipeline. Limit: it alone sees every crate. Path: see the note below this table. Path: transport lives in `crates/httpjet/src/uring/`. Path: pipeline lives in `crates/httpjet/src/pipeline/`. Path: cache glue lives in `crates/httpjet/src/lscache/`. Path: HTTP/2 lives in `crates/hj-h2/src/server/`. Path: rewrite lives in `crates/hj-rewrite/src/`. Path: LSAPI lives in `crates/hj-lsapi/src/`. ## Transport paths The pure io_uring transport is the only serving transport. You get no runtime switch and no `URING=0` rollback build. One monoio runtime runs per listener fd. It pins to its core when workers equal CPU count. Use `--no-core-pinning` to disable pinning. > [Diagram: transport] One transport, three protocols, one pipeline. Cheap work stays on the monoio core: the H1 codec, the native h2 task, the QUIC driver, and the on-core fast path (finished-response memo, static files, page-cache hits). Anything else crosses uring::bridge into the tokio runtime that owns ServerState, the LSAPI pool, the page cache and reload state, then returns to the monoio core for framing and writes. Bodies ≤ 256 KiB are buffered; larger ones stream on H1, H2 and H3 alike. `--uring-ring coop` is the default since 2026-11-07. It measured +28% RPS and -27% CPU per cookieless H2 cache hit on x86. `legacy` uses flagless rings. `defer` measured ~-2% on the GCE guest. Ring size stays at the default. Ring memory is memlock-charged. Multishot accept is on by default. Use `--no-multishot-accept` for one SQE per connection. Bodies ≤ 256 KiB are buffered. Larger bodies stream on H1, H2 and H3. ## The frozen contract — hj-core This is the seam that lets handlers compose without knowing the transport. Changing these signatures means updating every dependent, so they are treated as frozen: **hj-core** · the seam ``` enum Body { Empty, Full(Bytes), Stream(BoxBody), File(FileBody) } type Request = http::Request ; type Response = http::Response ; // every terminal handler (StaticFiles, Lsapi, FastCgi, ProxyHandler) trait Handler { async fn handle(&self, &mut ReqCtx, Request) -> Result ; } // every post-handler munger (promote → expires → sub_filter → compress → deny-CDN-cache → Alt-Svc) trait ResponseTransform { async fn transform(&self, &ReqCtx, &mut Response); } ``` `FileBody` can pin an open inode across cache swaps. `ReqCtx` carries `server`/`vhost` and client state. It also carries `is_tls`, `protocol` and `trusted_proxy`. Its `env` vec holds rewrite `[E=]` sets and CGI overrides. `Router::resolve(listener, key)` maps SNI/Host to a vhost. i Extending Register new handlers in `pipeline/mod.rs::dispatch()`. Register new transforms in `state.rs::build_transforms`. Out-of-tree code uses the extension registry . ## The request pipeline `pipeline::handle()` is the integration point. It resolves the vhost first. It then applies trust, ACL, geo and throttle checks. It runs optional WAF and extension pre-handlers. It then calls `dispatch()` and applies transforms. It finally writes logs, metrics and spans. `dispatch()` mirrors OpenLiteSpeed ordering. It inserts page-cache seams after rewrite and access resolve. The pinned `LsapiScript` extension keeps the resolved script separate. It pushes `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` into `ctx.env` for front controllers. Terminals use an explicit `if/return` chain, not a uniform registry. A failed proxy context falls through to static. A script with no pool **hard-fails 503**. It must never fall through to source. ! Load-bearing detail A rewrite to `index.php` keeps the original `REQUEST_URI`. The cache must key by that original URI. Never key by the rewrite-resolved path. Cache seams stay inert without `--page-cache`. `lscache::cache_lookup` runs before any backend. `lscache::cache_store` runs after `finalize_response`. ## Module organization See the Path note under Crate map . ## Configuration generations Live state publishes as immutable *generations* behind an `ArcSwap`. A SIGHUP or API transaction builds a complete candidate first. It validates the candidate before publishing. In-flight requests finish on their pinned generation. > [Diagram: generations] Candidate → published → retired. A rejected candidate never touches the serving generation. Trust changes (TLS material, mTLS policy, PROXY protocol) retire the old listener group and drain its connections under their pinned policy; boot-owned resources (listener topology, PHP pools, cache stores, privileges) are restart_required. The full ownership inventory and the transactional replacement sequence are on Admin API & reload . ## Code conventions **Formatting:** rustfmt-clean (default settings, edition 2024); `cargo fmt --all --check` is a CI gate.

- **Errors:** `thiserror` types at system boundaries; internal invariant violations panic with a message rather than pretending to recover.

- **unsafe:** Keep `unsafe` rare and never in HPACK. Document the safety invariant above each block.

- **Async:** tokio tasks for independent work, `FuturesUnordered` for multiplexing with coordinated shutdown, no per-stream spawn on hot paths.

- **Hashing:** Use `rustc-hash` only for trusted or hard-capped keys. Limit: the `.htaccess` memo caps at 16 shards × 512 entries, keys ≤ 1 KiB. Untrusted unbounded maps keep SipHash.

- **Allocator:** Use mimalloc globally with threshold-gated trim (`--mimalloc-trim-*`). Limit: production sets `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0`, so you pool transient buffers in `hj_core::recycle`.

> [Diagram: recycle-pools] Zero-fault buffer and task recycling (v0.1.2–v0.1.5). Under MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0, unpooled transient allocations in sparse size classes fault back in on every request. hj_core::recycle pools H2 stream futures, bridge futures, tiered body buffers (frozen into ref-counted Bytes via Bytes::from_owner and returned when the last slice drops), LSAPI read/BEGIN buffers, and per-core 64 KiB TLS record buffers.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Protocol stacks (https://httpjet.net/docs/protocols)
SUMMARY: How HTTP versions and listeners work.
==============================================================================

# Protocol stacks

You get HTTP/1.1, native HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 over QUIC here. One unconditional io_uring / monoio transport serves all three.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

All serving lives in the binary's `uring/` module. You select the protocol at the connection boundary.

| Signal | Stack. Limit: |

| TLS ALPN `h2` | Native `hj-h2`. Limit: TLS only. |

| TLS ALPN other / none | Custom monoio + `httparse` HTTP/1.1. Limit: http/1.1 or none. |

| Cleartext 24-byte h2 preface | Native `hj-h2` h2c. Limit: prior knowledge, no upgrade. |

| Cleartext other bytes | HTTP/1.1. Limit: sniff is non-destructive. |

| UDP on the HTTPS port | HTTP/3, `quinn-proto` on io_uring. Limit: see HTTP/3 . |

> [Diagram: connection-lifecycle] A TCP connection's life. PROXY stripping (if opted in) precedes TLS or the cleartext sniff. ALPN picks the TLS stack; the 24-byte preface picks the cleartext one. H2 drains with GOAWAY on shutdown.

## HTTP/1.1 & h2c detection

You get strict RFC 9112 framing here. Cleartext h2c needs no upgrade handshake.

| Rule | Behaviour. Limit: |

| Framing | Single `Content-Length` only. Limit: conflicting lengths rejected. |

| Reads and bodies | Bounded incomplete reads; chunked bodies decoded. Limit: deadlines extend only on progress, to an absolute ceiling. |

| Keep-alive | Keep-alive and pipelining supported. Limit: `maxKeepAliveReq` 0 or 1 disables keep-alive, matching OpenLiteSpeed. |

| Request target | Origin-form, plus `*` for OPTIONS. Limit: http/https absolute-form reduces to origin-form; its authority replaces `Host`. |

| `CONNECT` / authority-form / raw `#` | `CONNECT` answers 405. Limit: authority-form and raw `#` answer 400. |

| `Host` | HTTP/1.1 requires `Host`; HTTP/1.0 may omit it. Limit: must be UTF-8 and pass the h2/h3 `:authority` validation. |

| Line endings | Bare LF ends no header line. Limit: rejected 400 before the head materializes. |

| Refusals | Lingering close drains unread request bytes. Limit: the peer reads the error status cleanly. |

| Egress | Large responses stream from the bridge. Limit: minimum send-progress rate applies; see below. |

These rules date from the 2026-10-06 review. You detect h2c non-destructively: observed bytes pass to the winning stack.

            **uring** · ALPN + cleartext routing

```
// over TLS: ALPN decides the TCP stack
match alpn {
    b"h2"       => hj_h2::server::serve_local_with_prefix(io, prefix, service, cfg).await,
    _           => handle_h1_bridged(io, prefix, service).await,   // http/1.1 or none
}

// cleartext: sniff the 24-byte preface, pass the observed bytes along
match sniff_cleartext(&mut stream).await? {
    Proto::Http2(prefix) => hj_h2::server::serve_local_with_prefix(stream, prefix, service, cfg).await,
    Proto::Http1(prefix) => handle_h1_bridged(stream, prefix, service).await,
}
```

- **103 Early Hints.** You emit interim `103` from the shared preload/preconnect `Link` matcher. Limit: batched with the final head when ready; `101` upgrades bypass it; canonical/alternate links excluded.

- **Ranges.** You parse, clamp, and coalesce RFC 9110 multi-range sets. Limit: `multipart/byteranges`, capped at 8 ranges / 8 MiB part bytes, full-200 fallback; invalid component poisons the header (200); unsatisfiable set is 416.

- **Request decompression.** You decode gzip by default. Limit: brotli/zstd need `--request-decompression-extra`; bounded and buffered; see Compression .

- **Bandwidth pacing.** You pace `Body::Full` as 64 KiB slices and streams per chunk. Limit: per-connection token bucket, burst 2× rate, when `bandwidthLimit` is set; a matched context overrides the server-wide rate.

- **Send progress.** You end a response under 16 KiB delivered per `connTimeout` window. Limit: applies to every response write, sendfile included.

## Native HTTP/2

`hj-h2` serves ALPN `h2` and cleartext h2c here. You optimize one connection's multiplexing for few, long-lived CDN connections.

- TLS conn ALPN h2 / h2c ONE connection task FuturesUnordered⟨stream⟩ stream 1 · handler stream 2 · handler … stream N HPACK enc / dec send flow control · deadlines one vectored writev / wake wire zero-copy Bytes bridge dispatch → shared pipeline → monoio writes One connection task multiplexes every stream. It emits a single vectored write per wake. **One task per connection.** Streams multiplex through `FuturesUnordered`. Limit: 100 streams cost one task.

- **Flow control.** Per-stream and connection windows apply. Limit: frame, header-block, and body deadlines run on the monoio loop.

- **Stalled streams.** Under 16 KiB per `connTimeout` window earns `RST_STREAM(CANCEL)`. Limit: withheld flow-control credit only.

- **Streaming bodies.** LSAPI, proxy, SSE, and file bodies stream unbuffered. Limit: spans stay open through final flush.

- **Writes.** One vectored write per wake; large bodies stay zero-copy `Bytes`. Limit: vendored `monoio-rustls` adds `writev`, one flush write, per-core pooled buffers.

- **Validation.** RFC 9113 inbound, GOAWAY drain. Limit: stray `CONTINUATION` and stream-id reuse are connection errors.

- **Oversize heads.** Over-cap block gets bodiless 431; over-cap body gets 413. Limit: then `RST_STREAM(NO_ERROR)`; suppressed decode keeps HPACK in sync.

- **Refusals.** Budget-refused streams get `RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM)`. Limit: rapid-reset budget 200, refilled 10/s; past it, GOAWAY(ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM).

- **Abuse bounds.** HTTP/2 Bomb (CVE-2026-49975) and no-progress stay bounded. Limit: see rapid-reset budget.

- **Pacing.** Per-connection at OutQueue flush. Limit: server-wide rate only; H3 unpaced.

        ⎁   Measured
You pass **146 of 146** h2spec 2.6.0 cases over TLS. Limit: three consecutive runs is the gate; h2c records 145/146, with generic §3.5/2 structurally unsatisfiable on the sniffing port.
 scripts/h2spec_check.sh · scripts/ci-h2spec.py
        i   HPACK
RFC 7541 HPACK lives in the `hpack` submodule of `hj-h2`, zero-allocation and pure safe Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]`). Huffman codes to 11 bits resolve from a 4 KiB root table. Three 32-entry sub-tables cover 12–16-bit codes (0.1.7; replaced 256 KiB flat; cold decode 16.6 → 4.6 µs). The encoder remembers eight long literals (257+ bytes) per thread (0.1.10; 4.73 → 1.34 µs per block). Decoder and round-trip are fuzz targets . See the HPACK stub .

## HPACK

HPACK now lives inside Native HTTP/2 as a three-line summary. You keep this stub so existing links keep working.

## HTTP/3 & QUIC

`uring/h3.rs` runs `quinn-proto` state over io_uring UDP here. You bridge requests into the same pipeline.

- **Intake and parsing.** You use `quinn-udp` metadata (GSO/GRO, live GSO cap) and parse streams incrementally. Limit: QUIC DATAGRAM disabled; QPACK head bytes charge `total_req_bytes` and the body budget.

- **Bodies and stalls.** Small, cached, and sub-threshold bodies go whole; large, SSE, and proxy bodies stream HEADERS-first. Limit: backpressured DATA; send-stalled streams reset; retained memory bounded per connection (2026-09-06).

- **Budget.** Charge at `Connected`, after validation. Limit: spoofed Initials cannot hold budget; full budget closes `H3_EXCESSIVE_LOAD`.

- **Handshake slots.** One of 256 per-core slots per unvalidated connection. Limit: above 64 per core, stateless **Retry**; token-bearing Initials pass; handshakes close after 10 s.

- **Discovery and trust.** Advertise via **Alt-Svc** (last TLS transform); pin trust/mTLS at acceptance. Limit: migration disabled; reloads affect future handshakes only.

> [Diagram: h3-admission] HTTP/3 UDP intake. Unvalidated Initials pass per-core slot caps (256 max, Retry above 64) before charging maxConnections at Connected. QPACK heads charge total_req_bytes and BodyBufferBudget.

        !   Publish UDP too
You must publish the same numeric HTTPS port over TCP and UDP. Publishing `8443/tcp` alone gives you no HTTP/3.

## Connection front doors

Two per-listener features sit before protocol detection. Both are httpjet-native, with no LiteSpeed listener equivalent.

### PROXY protocol v2 / v1

Set ` 1 ` and you require a PROXY header on every connection. You install the claimed address before TLS or the H1/h2c sniff.

- Missing header closes the connection. Limit: fail-closed both ways.

- Loopback or unspecified sources are refused at the parser (2026-09-16). Limit: they would otherwise forge mTLS exemption and the loopback purge gate.

        !   The listener opt-in is the trust decision
Never enable this on an internet-facing bind. Anyone can forge their client address there; `check` warns on wildcard or public binds.

### HTTP over Unix sockets

Use `unix:/path/sock` (or `uds:`), or `--http-uds`, for plain HTTP over a Unix socket. You serve H1 and h2c prior knowledge on one accept core.

- Socket mode is 0660, owner and group read/write. Limit: SO_REUSEPORT does not exist for AF_UNIX; socket-activated fds are adopted by path.

- A stale file is unlinked only after `connect(2)` proves it dead. Limit: cleanup binds to the owned directory and socket identity.

- Peers have no address. Limit: ACLs, the per-IP throttle, and `REMOTE_ADDR` see fabricated loopback; the log renders `unix:`.

- TLS over UDS is unsupported. Limit: `check` lints it.

## File egress: sendfile & kTLS

An uncached `Body::File` keeps its pinned inode and byte range across the bridge. You send it with bounded nonblocking `sendfile(2)` on plain TCP HTTP/1.

- Unsupported pairs resume at the exact offset via positional io_uring reads. Limit: short files or aborts close, never a wrong `Content-Length`.

- Stalled sendfile backs off 100 µs → 12.8 ms. Limit: 16 KiB per `connTimeout` progress rule still applies.

- `--features ktls` extends this to TLS 1.3 H1 after the rustls handshake. Limit: queued peer KeyUpdate applies before next writes, fencing TX rekey.

- Policy `--ktls=auto|on|off`; `auto` (default in feature builds) checks the IPv4 default-route NIC via ethtool. Limit: enables only with active `tls-hw-tx-offload` on a non-virtual NIC; else logs one reason, stays rustls.

- TLS 1.2, H2, H3, and UDS keep userspace paths.

        ⎁   Measured
Plaintext sendfile: 5,000 × 1 MiB at c=50 → **4,852 req/s**, 10.08 ms mean, zero failures. Software kTLS on a virtual GVE NIC: **2,999.7 req/s off vs 2,944.9 on**.
 loopback · 2026-09-09 · `bench-results/httpjet-sendfile-*.csv`, `httpjet-ktls-sendfile-*.csv`

## TLS in one paragraph

`hj-tls` builds one `rustls::ServerConfig` for TCP and QUIC, on aws-lc-rs. You map SNI directly to configured chains (no cert-name-match, like OLS), with dual ECDSA+RSA chains per name.

Client verification uses the listener CA only, with CRL enforcement. Read TLS, ACME & OCSP for resumption (`--tls-session-tickets`, default 2; 0-RTT off) and reload.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Rewrite & .htaccess (https://httpjet.net/docs/rewrite)
SUMMARY: How .htaccess rules rewrite and protect requests.
==============================================================================

# Rewrite engine & .htaccess

`hj-rewrite` is httpjet's Apache **mod_rewrite** / `.htaccess` engine. It depends only on `hj-compress`, so `.htaccess` and XML expiry share one `A/M` time grammar.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

Run inline ` ` rules first, then the `.htaccess` chain (OpenLiteSpeed order). `evaluate()` returns one outcome per pass: `Rewritten`, `Redirect`, `Proxy`, `Forbidden`, `Gone` or `Unchanged`.

> [Diagram: rewrite-eval] One evaluation pass. A rewrite that crosses into another directory reloads the destination chain and evaluates again; a terminal flag stops the walk; an exhausted chain returns Unchanged and dispatch falls through to suffix routing.

## Per-directory loading

`HtaccessCache` loads each directory's file (`accessFileName`, default `.htaccess`; bare names only). **mtime invalidation** re-stats at most once a second, so edits land within a second. The parsed form holds directives, regexes, scopes, the auth map and the memo verdict. The chain caps at **64** levels, then a deny-all sentinel applies.

Since 2026-09-16 an unreadable, unparseable or over-16 MiB `.htaccess` fails closed to that sentinel. Non-UTF-8 bytes decode lossily. Set ` 0` to disable the chain; `autoLoadHtaccess` alone loads without overrides. Each generation owns its caches, so reloads never revive stale results.

## The dense-DFA prefilter

See Matching . The prefilter now lives there.

## Matching

Compile eligible patterns once into **one dense DFA** (`regex_automata::dfa::dense`). Search it once to learn which rules could match. Run only those rules for real. A dense DFA holds no lazy state, so the search is **cacheless**. You pay no per-search allocation and no cross-thread pool lock.

           **hot path** · prefilter, then evaluate
```
let hits = prefilter.search(path);          // which rules *could* match — one DFA pass
for rule in hits {
    if let Some(m) = rule.regex.find(path) { return rule.apply(m); }   // substitute + flags
}
Outcome::Unchanged
```

Each flagged rule runs through `CompiledRegex`. Prefer `regex_automata::meta::Regex` (per-pattern thread-local cache). Fall back to `fancy-regex` only where the linear engine cannot express a construct. Accepted patterns match identically under both.

| Pattern shape | Engine | Why |

| Anchors, classes, alternation, repetition | `regex_automata::meta` | Linear time. Limit: per-pattern thread-local cache, no shared lock. |

| Lookahead `(?=…)` / `(?!…)`, lookbehind | `fancy-regex` | Not a finite automaton. Limit: backtracking only here. |

| In-pattern backreference `\1` | `fancy-regex` | Requires backtracking. Limit: backtracking only here. |

| Pure lookahead conjunction `^(?=.*A)(?=.*B)…` | `regex_automata::meta` per part | One linear search per part. Limit: `fancy-regex` only for captures (0.1.10: 29 → 1 µs). |

A regex error at match time **fails closed toward the rule's polarity**. A failing deny counts as matched; a failing allow is withheld (hardened 2026-09-06).

## Rewrite-outcome cache & UA classification

See Two caches . Outcome caching now lives there.

## Two caches

**Outcome cache.** Memoize the rewrite decision for path-cacheable chains (`--rewrite-outcome-ttl-ms`, default 1000 ms; 0 disables). Key on vhost, scheme, method, host, path, query and keyable headers. Count with `httpjet_rewrite_outcome_{hits,misses,uncacheable}_total`.

**UA classification.** Enable `--rewrite-ua-classify` (default off) to key UA chains by RewriteCond bitmap, when analysis proves that dependence. Since 2026-09-06 header collection continues past it, so Origin/Accept chains still key correctly (`httpjet_rewrite_ua_classify_entries`).

**Finished-response memo.** Serve repeat cookieless static GETs without the pipeline (default on; `--no-fast-memo` / `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0`). Per thread, 1 s TTL, 64 MiB/worker. Store only 200 full bodies without `Set-Cookie`, after one full pass per key.

Eligibility is a **parse-time verdict** (`MemoClass`, fail-closed) that `httpjet check` prints per vhost. Note: `%{TIME*}` evaluates to the empty string, and chains reading it are ineligible for this memo.

> [Diagram: memo-eligibility] Memo eligibility. A chain that reads anything the memo key cannot carry — client/server addresses, protocol, IP/env/host access operands, REDIRECT_STATUS, %{HTTP_COOKIE}, %{TIME*} — is ineligible and pays the full pipeline every time. Eligible chains memoize with a VARY-SET of every header the chain reads (raw Origin, UA bitmap …), so an 800-line forum chain still memoizes.

        ⎁   Measured
Same-binary A/B on the forum's 806-line chain (`/robots.txt`, c=100): **h2 137k → 248k req/s (+81%)**, **h1 107k → 153k (+43%)**. Gate `scripts/fast_memo_parity_test.sh` diffs UA × Origin × Accept-Encoding × scheme (192 cells, zero differences).
 PGO · 2026-08-28 · parity re-run 2026-09-16

Interactive · `.htaccess` & `fast_memo` readiness inspector

         Paste or edit an `.htaccess` snippet to inspect `MemoClass` eligibility, `VARY-SET` headers, regex engine split, and directive support:
           RewriteEngine On
SetEnvIfNoCase User-Agent "SemrushBot|AhrefsBot|MJ12bot" bad_bot=1
RewriteCond %{ENV:bad_bot} =1
RewriteRule ^ - [F,L]

Header always set Access-Control-Allow-Origin "https://windowsforum.com" env=CORS_OK
RewriteCond %{HTTP:Origin} ^https://(www\.)?windowsforum\.com$ [NC]
RewriteRule ^ - [E=CORS_OK:1]

RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -f [OR]
RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} -d
RewriteRule ^ - [L]
RewriteRule ^ index.php [L]

Mirrors the parse-time `MemoClass` analysis printed by `httpjet --root /usr/local/lsws check`.

## SetEnvIf & lazy headers

Evaluate `SetEnvIf`/`SetEnvIfNoCase` with **lazy header access**: materialize only referenced headers, compare case-insensitively. No match costs nothing. Since 2026-09-16 you cannot set server-computed CGI names (`REMOTE_ADDR`, `HTTPS`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, …) this way.

           **.htaccess** · SetEnvIf
```
SetEnvIfNoCase User-Agent "bot|crawler" is_bot=1
SetEnvIf Request_URI "\.(?:png|jpg|css|js)$" is_asset=1
RewriteCond %{ENV:is_bot} =1
RewriteRule ^/expensive/ - [E=no-cache:1]      # [E=no-cache] also bypasses the page cache
```

## Front-controller routing

XenForo and WordPress rewrite every URL to `/index.php`. Keep the **original `REQUEST_URI`**; pin `SCRIPT_FILENAME` via `LsapiScript` and `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` via env. Hence the page-cache original-URI key .

## Access control

` `/` `/` `/` `/` ` carry `Order`/`Allow from`/`Deny from`/`Require`, ANDed across blocks. A ` ` deny covers everything beneath it. Only `Require all granted` grants; other predicates (`ip`, `host`, `env`, `expr`, `method`, …) **fail closed to deny** (403). Directory patterns accept mapped or docroot-relative paths.

## HTTP Basic auth

Protect a subtree with `AuthType Basic` + `AuthName` + `AuthUserFile` + `Require valid-user | user …`:

- Resolve requirements in scope order. Limit: metadata-only sections cannot erase inherited requirements; explicit `Require` replaces them.

- Enforce before cache lookup, on original/rewritten/index/script targets. Limit: valid credentials set `REMOTE_USER`; failures return 401.

- Fail closed on unsupported auth. Limit: exact usernames stay preserved.

           **.htaccess** · a protected subtree
```
AuthType Basic
AuthName "Staging"
AuthUserFile /srv/example.test/conf/htpasswd
Require valid-user
```

Accepted htpasswd hashes — verify each in constant time:

- **bcrypt** (`$2y$`/`$2b$`/`$2a$`, `htpasswd -B`). Limit: cost capped at 14; higher is refused before hashing.

- **APR1-MD5** (`$apr1$`), **MD5-crypt** (`$1$`) and `{SHA}`.

- Plaintext, DES, `$5$` and `$6$` `crypt()`. Limit: these verify *false* with a parse-time warning.

An unknown user pays dummy bcrypt/MD5 work at the file's recorded cost. Charge Basic-auth attempts per client before hashing. Refuse repeated `Authorization` headers.

Resolve `AuthUserFile` **inside the docroot**, or under `--auth-user-file-roots`. Check the descriptor's real path; cap reads at 1 MiB. An unreadable or out-of-root file returns 500, never a silent 401; `check` warns. Authenticated statics get `Cache-Control: private, no-store` without an explicit policy (#414).

Note: the 2026-09-06 review split parsed policy from the effective realm; the rules above carry its outcome.

## Directives reference

| Directive | Status | Notes |

| RewriteEngine · RewriteBase | supported | Toggle and base-path resolution. |

| RewriteCond · RewriteRule | supported | - Flags: `L END R R=code F G P PT E= N NC QSA QSD NE C S=n B B=chars BNE= BNP BCTLS UnsafeAllow3F`; `OR` on conditions. - File tests: `-f/-F -d -e -l/-L/-h -s -x` (`-U` always matches). - Variables: `REQUEST_URI REQUEST_FILENAME REQUEST_METHOD REQUEST_SCHEME QUERY_STRING THE_REQUEST HTTPS HTTP_HOST HTTP_USER_AGENT HTTP_COOKIE HTTP_REFERER HTTP_ACCEPT REMOTE_ADDR REMOTE_PORT SERVER_ADDR SERVER_NAME SERVER_PORT SERVER_PROTOCOL DOCUMENT_ROOT SCRIPT_FILENAME`, `%{HTTP:Name}`, `%{ENV:NAME}`, `%{LA-U:…}`/`%{LA-F:…}`. - `%{TIME*}` yields the empty string. - `RewriteMap`, `${map:key}`, `T=`/`H=` fail closed at parse time. Limit: other flags (e.g. `DPI`, `CO=`) are ignored. |

| SetEnvIf · SetEnvIfNoCase | supported | Lazy header access. Limit: server-computed CGI names stay protected. |

| Order · Allow from · Deny from | supported | Apache accumulation per scope. Limit: `env=`, host and CIDR operands make the chain memo-ineligible. |

| Require | partial | `all granted`, `valid-user`, `user …`. Limit: everything else fails closed to deny. |

| AuthType · AuthName · AuthUserFile | supported | Basic only. Limit: bcrypt, APR1 (`$apr1$`), MD5-crypt (`$1$`) and `{SHA}` only. |

| Header set / add / append / merge / unset | supported | - Guards: `always`/`onsuccess`, `env=`/`env=!`, `%{NAME}e`. - Scopes merge directory, then ` `, then ` `. Limit: applied in `finalize`; CR/LF rejected. |

| Header echo | partial | Parses without error. Limit: emits nothing. |

| Header edit / edit* / note / setifempty / echo · RequestHeader * | ignored | Line ignored. Limit: see `docs/header-directive-compatibility.md` for the exact boundary. |

| Header condition expr= / value expr= | partial | Only `%{REQUEST_URI} =~ / !~` conjunctions evaluate. Limit: value expressions are not implemented. |

| ErrorDocument | supported | Path, inline and external forms. Limit: never clobbers an app's own JSON error body. |

| DirectoryIndex | supported | Including the `Disabled` form. |

| SetHandler · AddHandler · AddType · ForceType · RemoveHandler · RemoveType | supported | `application/x-httpd-php` forces PHP. Limit: other handlers and `Remove*` record a non-PHP reset; `AddType`/`ForceType` override `Content-Type`. |

| CacheLookup · CacheEnable · CacheDisable · CacheKeyModify | supported | LSCache directives for the page cache . Limit: `CacheKeyModify` strips query parameters from the key. |

| php_value · php_admin_value · php_flag · php_admin_flag | supported | Per-request PHP ini overrides. Limit: LSAPI special-env path only. |

|             | partial | Common scopes honored. Limit: ` ` only for the modeled REQUEST_URI shape; ` ` bodies evaluate. |

| FileETag · H2EarlyHints · esi · AddOutputFilterByType · AllowOverride · Options | no-op | Recognized and dropped. |

| ExpiresActive · ExpiresDefault · ExpiresByType | supported | Scoped across directory, ` ` and ` `. Limit: shares the `A/M` grammar; overrides vhost XML ` ` when active. |

Unrecognized directives are ignored, so vendor files stay loadable.

See Configuration → Contexts . Per-context overrides and `sub_filter` now live there.

           **tests**

==============================================================================
PAGE: Page cache (https://httpjet.net/docs/page-cache)
SUMMARY: How full pages are cached and cleared.

# The origin page cache

Use this opt-in full-response cache to serve stored pages without the backend. It speaks the LiteSpeed protocol — `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control`, `X-LiteSpeed-Tag`, `X-LiteSpeed-Vary`, `X-LiteSpeed-Purge` — so LSCache-tuned sites need no app change.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

`hj-pagecache` is the store: sharded LRU, W-TinyLFU admission, key/vary/tag indexes and the HJPC file tier. The `lscache/` glue runs `cache_lookup` before any backend, and `cache_store` after `finalize_response`. Both stay inert without `--page-cache`.

           Off by default · app opt-in per response
           Keyed by the ORIGINAL URI · identity-guarded
           Public · private · shared-path tiers
           RAM index · hot tier · tmpfs file tier
           Tag purge · stale-while-revalidate · stale-if-error · single flight
           Per-vhost dictionaries · survives restarts

        i   Two memos, kept apart
Static files use a separate default-on per-worker memo (1 s TTL) — see Rewrite → Two caches . It never serves page-cache entries. Since 0.1.11 the page cache has its own default-on response memo, fenced by freshness, Age and purge epochs (`--no-page-cache-response-memo` disables it). With the default `coop` ring it measured +27.6% RPS / −26.7% CPU per cookieless H2 hit — see Performance → 0.1.11 .

## Opt-in by the app

Store only when the app says so. Gate lookups with ` `, `CacheLookup` and `[E=no-cache]`; gate storage with the response header. `respectCacheable`/`enablePostCache` parse but do not enforce.

           **app → httpjet** · the cache protocol headers
```
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public,max-age=3600            # public entry, one hour
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: private,max-age=120            # per-session entry (needs --page-cache-private; TTL capped 300 s)
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public,max-age=60,stale-while-revalidate=600,stale-if-error=3600
X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: no-cache                       # never store this response
X-LiteSpeed-Tag: T1234,forum7                             # purge tags
X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=xf_style_id                      # vary the public entry on a declared cookie value
X-LiteSpeed-Purge: tag=T1234                              # drop every entry carrying this tag (also: * for all)
```

**Standards mode.** List vhosts in `--page-cache-standard-vhosts` for OLS `checkPublicCache` shape: plain `Cache-Control: public` opts in. All other guards still apply.

        !   Backends cannot self-purge
Strip `X-LiteSpeed-*` from proxied upstream responses. Only LSAPI/PHP responses and loopback purge callers shape cache behavior.

## The lookup path

> [Diagram: cache-lookup] Lookup, tier routing and freshness. Member-cookie requests route to the private tier (or, for allow-listed visitor-invariant endpoints, to the shared public tier); the key is derived from the original URI; a found entry serves only if its stored identity matches; stale entries within their windows serve immediately with a background refresh; concurrent misses collapse onto one render.

Route member requests to the private tier; allow-listed invariant endpoints go shared-public instead. Key on the *original* URI. Serve only on identity match. Serve stale in-window with background refresh; collapse concurrent misses.

## Keys, tiers and the identity guard

key & tier explorer — change the request and the app's header

           method  GET  HEAD  POST
           scheme  https  http
           host
           path
           query
           vary cookie xf_style_id

             request carries the member cookie (xf_user)
             --page-cache-private on
             path matches --page-cache-shared-paths
             the .htaccess chain reads Origin

          X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control on the response

Illustrative composition, not the byte layout. The real key is a compact id plus the stored identity; the guard makes any id collision a miss.

        !   Invariant 1 · key by the original URI
Key on `orig_path`/`orig_query`, never the rewrite-resolved path. XenForo rewrites every page to `/index.php`; resolved-path keying once served one page to everyone.

Every entry records its host and raw request path. Serve only when both match; a collision degrades to a miss (`httpjet_pagecache_key_id_collisions_total`), never wrong content. Add three key dimensions: **per-URL cookie vary** (`X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=NAME`, plus `--page-cache-vary-cookies`; header vary hashes with SHA-256), **Origin** when the chain reads it (2026-09-16), and **epoch + generation** from the first API publication . Only the canonical Host spelling reads or populates an entry. An absent Origin keeps the historic base key.

| Tier | Routed when | Keyed by | Notes |

| **Public** | No member cookie | vhost · scheme · host · original path?query · vary cookies (· Origin) | Strip `Set-Cookie` and `X-LiteSpeed-*`. Limit: a private-cookie response never stores. |

| **Private** | Member marker (`xf_user`, or bare `xf_session`, 2026-10-04) + `--page-cache-private` | public key + session-cookie value | Never touches public entries. Limit: TTL capped at 300 s. |

| **Shared paths** | Member cookie + `--page-cache-shared-paths` match, within canary % | public key | Visitor-invariant HMAC image endpoints only. Limit: never HTML; malformed specs abort startup. |

| **Bypass** | Non-GET/HEAD, `[E=no-cache]`, no header, member without private tier | — | Counted as `httpjet_cache_bypass`. |

## The store path and admission

> [Diagram: cache-store] Store gates. After the app opts in, the response still has to pass the status list, the private-cookie guard, the proxied-header strip, the self-redirect guard, the purge-race check and the object cap, and then earn admission. Only then is the stored copy written — into RAM, or at birth into an immutable tmpfs file.

Pass the status list, private-cookie guard and proxied-header strip first. Pass the self-redirect guard, purge-race check and object cap next. Earn W-TinyLFU admission last. Write the stored copy only then — into RAM, or at birth into an immutable tmpfs file.

### W-TinyLFU admission

> [Diagram: admission] A fixed-memory frequency sketch rejects one-hit wonders: at the default threshold of 2 a URL is stored on its second sighting. One request is ONE sighting — the on-core fast path probes uncounted and records only a hit it serves. Size weighting adds +1 per 256 KiB. With dictionaries making storage cheap, --page-cache-admit-threshold 1 caches on first sight. Tune by httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real and httpjet_cache_admit_ratio.

Reject one-hit wonders with a fixed-memory frequency sketch. At threshold 2 (default) you store on the second sighting; one request counts as one sighting. Size weighting adds +1 per 256 KiB. Set `--page-cache-admit-threshold 1` to cache on first sight. Tune by `httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real` and `httpjet_cache_admit_ratio`.

Decline a cacheable 3xx whose `Location` is the request's own URL (hosts normalized without port). Re-check that guard at serve time; the XF add-on refuses at a third layer. De-cache cacheable redirects from the CDN via the deny-CDN-cache transform.

## Storage tiers & the file tier

> [Diagram: cache-tiers] Dual-cap tier model. The RAM index describes every entry; with a file tier, bodies live as immutable HJPC files and are charged metadata-only against --page-cache-mem while their footprint counts against --page-cache-disk-mem. A small hot tier fronts the files. Every teardown path (evict, expire, purge, replace) is synchronous under the shard lock; only the unlink(2) syscall is deferred to just after the lock is released.

Default to in-RAM only; restarts flush it. Set `--page-cache-store-path /dev/shm/jetcache` (or `default`/`jetcache`) for a **tmpfs-primary** tier. `PageStore::store` offloads every body to an immutable file at birth, off the heap. HJPC containers authenticate with `--page-cache-integrity-key`. The LiteSpeed `cacheStorePath` parses but stays unused.

- **Survives restarts.** A boot scan (up to 8 threads) rebuilds the index — ~300k entries in seconds. Limit: `/__hj_cache_ready` returns 503 while scanning, then 200 + `x-hj-cache-ready: 1` + `x-hj-cache-loaded: N`.

- **Reclaim invariant.** Live entries resolve to live bodies. Limit: a missing file fails closed to a miss and counts `disk_read_err`.

- **Durable purges.** Purges unlink eagerly and keep a purge-all stamp. Limit: a restart cannot resurrect purged entries.

- **Dictionaries compress at store.** A background task dict-recompresses the identity birth copy (~3.5–9× smaller), never inline. Limit: incompressible types never encode; vhosts in `--page-cache-egress-at-rest-vhosts` skip this job (0.1.6).

budget calculator — how many pages fit?

           --page-cache-mem (MiB)
           --page-cache-disk-mem (MiB)
           --page-cache-hot-mem (MiB)
           typical page (KB, identity)
           dictionary ratio ×

Rules of thumb only (≈6 KB metadata per entry, ratio 3.5–9× on forum HTML). tmpfs *is* RAM. Production: disk-mem 2 GiB (x86) and 5.5 GiB (ARM), hot-mem 384 MiB on both.

| Flag | Default | Meaning |

| `--page-cache-mem` | 128 MiB | RAM index budget. Limit: file-tier bodies charge metadata-only here. |

| `--page-cache-disk-mem` | 2 GiB | tmpfs footprint cap. Limit: 0 falls back to `--page-cache-mem`. |

| `--page-cache-hot-mem` | 192 MiB | Hot bodies in RAM before files. Limit: cold hits pay one tmpfs read + decode. |

| `--page-cache-store-path` | *none* | Enables the file tier. Limit: deploy gate `ALLOW_PAGE_CACHE_FILE_TIER=1`. |

| `--page-cache-dict-vhost` / `--page-cache-dict` / `--page-cache-dict-level` | — | Per-vhost / fallback dictionaries; level 1–19 (default 12). Limit: rotation needs a restart. |

| `--page-cache-vary-default` | *empty* | `name=value` keyed as absent. Limit: e.g. `xf_style_id=50`. |

| `--page-cache-opt-in-status` / `--page-cache-303-prefixes` | *empty* | Cache 303/404/410 on explicit public opt-in only. Limit: TTL ≤ 300 s, no stale; default caches 200/301. |

| `--page-cache-stream-fill-vhosts` | *empty* | Stream length-less public 200 misses frame by frame. Limit: errors and over-cap bodies never store. |

| `--page-cache-egress-at-rest-vhosts` | *empty* | Keep dictionary-less zstd at rest; skip re-encode. Limit: stored copy stays larger; capsules keep the dictionary path. |

        !   Dictionaries can retain content
Train only on public, logged-out pages of one vhost. Served bytes are never dictionary-encoded. A missing compatible dictionary is a miss, never undecodable output.

## Variants, compression and egress

See Compression → cache interaction . Variant and egress rules now live there.

## Purge

Invalidate by tag. Emit `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: tag=T1234` (or `*`) on a response — every header line counts (0.0.5) — or POST the loopback endpoint. Reject a store that started before a purge and finished after it (`httpjet_pagecache_store_purge_rejections_total`).

           **purge** · loopback-only endpoint
```
curl -s -X POST -H 'x-litespeed-purge: tag=T1234' -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_purge   # 204
curl -s -X POST -H 'x-litespeed-purge: *' http://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_purge                                          # everything
```

Gate the endpoint on a **raw loopback TCP source** — no secret, no per-URL purge. CDN-relayed or LAN requests get 404. The endpoint answers **POST only** (2026-10-07); other methods get 405 + `Allow`. The former `--cache-peer` fan-out and `--cache-purge-secret-file` are gone.

## Stale policies & single flight

| Mechanism | Flags | Behavior |

| stale-while-revalidate | `--page-cache-stale-default-secs` (0), `--page-cache-stale-max-secs` (86400) | Serve stale now; refresh in background via full dispatch. Limit: an `X-LiteSpeed` opt-in never merges standard `Cache-Control` stale values (2026-10-04). |

| stale-if-error | `--page-cache-stale-if-error-default-secs` (0), `--page-cache-stale-if-error-max-secs` (86400) | Serve the retained entry on backend 5xx as `hit,stale-if-error`. Limit: `public,max-age=30` egress, Age reset; production sets 30 s. |

| single flight | built in | Collapse concurrent misses onto one leader via `Notify`. Limit: followers wait instead of rendering. |

## XenForo public-shell capsules application-specific

Enable `--xf-capsule` (requires `--page-cache`) for a public HTML *shell* on member requests; the add-on fills member bits client-side. Empty `--xf-capsule-vhosts` disables every vhost. Cover routes with `--xf-capsule-paths` or `all-get-classified`. Set `--xf-capsule-stale-secs` (production 3600). Since 2026-10-04 members use the *public* entry; `--xf-capsule-dedicated-store` (default off) restores a dedicated copy.

> [Diagram: xf-capsule] Guest vs logged-in member routing across the four cache surfaces. Guests use the public tier directly; logged-in members route visitor-invariant HMAC image paths (--page-cache-shared-paths) to the public tier, eligible forum routes (--xf-capsule) to the anonymized public HTML shell, and remaining opt-in pages to the per-session --page-cache-private tier.

## Generation-scoped namespaces

Derive an *epoch* from the process-bound revision at first API publication. Key all entries by epoch + generation (including SIGHUP). In-flight renders finish in their own namespace; restarts return to the on-disk namespace. Obsolete entries age out normally.

## Microcaching today, and what is missing

Roadmap note: short TTLs already work today (`public,max-age=2` gets every guard; `scripts/microcache_policy_example.sh` proves it). A first-class route-level policy does not exist yet. The proposed ` ` contract sits in `docs/microcache-policy.md`; the parser still ignores it.

## Observing the cache

           **observe** · headers, entries, metrics
```
$ curl -sI -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/ | grep -i x-litespeed-cache
x-litespeed-cache: miss            # ran the backend; stored if admitted
$ curl -sI -H 'Host: example.test' http://127.0.0.1:8080/ | grep -i x-litespeed-cache
x-litespeed-cache: hit             # served from cache (also: hit,stale-if-error)

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /etc/httpjet/profile.token)" http://127.0.0.1:9090/cache-entries   # totals, per-URL-class counts, top-N by size, ram/disk line, health line
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/metrics | grep -E '^httpjet_(pagecache|cache)_'
$ curl -sk https://127.0.0.1/__hj_cache_ready -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'   # 200 once the boot scan finished
```

Judge health by `httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real` and `httpjet_pagecache_{hits,misses,stores,purges,evictions}_total` (per-vhost split, 2026-10-04). Never judge by raw file count. Full list: Observability .

## Deploy gates

Pass these loopback scripts before shipping `--page-cache`:

- **`cache_xurl_test.sh`** Three distinct URLs keep their own content — the front-controller poisoning class.

- **`cache_scheme_test.sh`** An HTTP-origin canonical 301 must not poison the HTTPS entry — the "Too Many Redirects" loop.

- **`cache_xhost_test.sh`** Foreign-host isolation.

- **`cache_private_test.sh`** Private-tier session isolation, plus the shared-paths case when configured.

- **`cache_persist_test.sh`** With a file tier: waits on `/__hj_cache_ready` and asserts the boot scan restored entries. It restarts the service — run once (five restarts a minute trip systemd's start limit).

- **`cache_sie_test.sh` · `cache_capsule_purge_test.sh`** Stale-if-error (freezes its own lsphp tree mid-test, the production outage shape) and the capsule purge invariant.

        !   A cache bug outlives a rollback
A wrong response cached at the CDN edge stays there for its edge TTL. If bad content shipped: confirm the origin is correct on loopback, then purge the CDN zone — a binary rollback does not remove objects already stored upstream.
