PAGE: LSAPI & PHP (https://httpjet.net/docs/lsapi)
SUMMARY: How httpjet runs PHP through lsphp.
==============================================================================

# LSAPI & PHP

You speak native LSAPI to an operator-configured `lsphp` here — no FastCGI shim. Run the persistent external pool in production so web restarts keep PHP warm.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Overview

Suffix routing to PHP (` `, an `lsapi` `extProcessor`, or `SetHandler application/x-httpd-php`) talks LSAPI directly. PHP stays optional for static, proxy, and FastCGI deployments.

- client HTTP/1·2·3 HTTP httpjet LSAPI handler · CGI env LSAPI · UDS lsphp pool — capped by --php-children / maxConns php #1 php #2 … php #N streamed response · php-slow log · lsapi_ttfb histogram Native LSAPI over a Unix socket. You own the pool (spawn) or run it separately (external, the production shape). Native LSAPI · vendored `lsapidef.h` Operator-supplied `lsphp` Generation-tracked UDS pool Candidate-first zero-downtime reload Fail-closed jail ## Zero-downtime deploys: the external pool Spawn mode cold-starts opcache on every web deploy. You avoid that with `httpjet lsphp` as its own unit (`httpjet-lsphp.service`, `Type=notify`, socket-activated). ### Web tier deploy `systemctl restart httpjet`
- systemd holds the :80/:443 fds — no RST for new or queued connections
- PHP workers and opcache stay warm

### PHP recycle

- `systemctl reload httpjet-lsphp` → `httpjet lsphp-reload`
- candidate-first: a new family must answer a real, marker-attributed LSAPI request before promotion
- the systemd-owned listener is never closed; queued dials survive

> [Diagram: lsphp-reload] Candidate-first reload. Promotion follows a marker-attributed response, then the shared 16-byte epoch advances. Web pools drop idle sockets and retire in-flight stale workers after their responses, via pre-pinned pidfds.

           external pool wiring (see  Operations  for the units)
```
# the PHP half — its own unit, its own identity
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp --php-socket /run/httpjet/php.sock --php-children 256 \
  --control-socket /run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock \
  --generation-file /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation

# the serving half — dial, never spawn; restart freely
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … --lsphp-external /run/httpjet/php.sock \
  --lsphp-generation-file /run/httpjet/lsphp.generation

# opcache/PHP recycle without dropping the listener
httpjet lsphp-reload --control-socket /run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock --timeout-secs 90
```

        !   Generation file and socket are trust anchors
The 16-byte file (epoch + promoted-family marker fingerprint) identifies your pool. Supplying `--lsphp-generation-file` aborts startup if it is missing or malformed; its parent must not be group/other-writable, and test pools default files beside their own socket.

Never restart `httpjet-lsphp.socket` during a reload: it preserves the listener inode and 8192-deep queue. Restart only `httpjet-lsphp.service` (it reapplies the XML backlog via `listen(2)`); verify socket inode, 16-byte file, and `ss -xln` Send-Q = 8192 (`LIVE=1 scripts/lsphp-reload-test.sh`).

## The UDS connection pool

Requests reach `lsphp` over a Unix socket behind a generation-epoch pool. In external mode you map the 16-byte generation file read-only; in owned mode the epoch stays process-local.

- **Idle reuse.** Idle connections reuse newest-first and expire oldest-first (0.1.10). Limit: post-surge traffic avoids workers marked to retire.

- **Reset replay.** A GET/HEAD reset before any response byte replays up to twice, on fresh dials after 25 ms (0.1.9). Limit: since 0.1.10, any method dropped unread replays if bodiless or fully read (non-multipart POST to 64 KiB).

- **Dial retries.** Refused or missing-socket dials retry within `retryTimeout`, capped at 15 s. Limit: fresh-dial `EAGAIN` under backlog retries too; accepted connections keep TCP keepalive.

- **Attribution.** Each connection's worker is found via `UNIX_DIAG` peer-inode plus `/proc`, then pinned by pidfd. Limit: stale workers retire via that pidfd after responding; failures count, never guess.

- **Request bodies.** Chunked or no-`Content-Length` uploads collect first, because LSAPI needs `m_reqBodyLen`. Limit: `collect_to_cap` returns 413 the instant `maxReqBodySize` would pass; bytes charge the process-wide budget until completion or teardown (2026-09-06). See the bodies stub .

| Metric | Meaning. Limit: |

| `httpjet_lsapi_generation_advances_total` | Epoch advances observed. Limit: this web process only. |

| `httpjet_lsapi_stale_idle_drops_total` / `_stale_checked_out_drops_total` | Idle sockets discarded / checked-out sockets refused re-pooling. Limit: after an advance. |

| `httpjet_lsapi_stale_worker_retire_signals_total` / `_failures_total` | Stale workers retired via pidfd / signals failed. Limit: after their responses completed. |

| `httpjet_lsapi_worker_attribution_failures_total` | Workers you could not pin. Limit: counted, never guessed. |

| `httpjet_lsapi_acquire_seconds` · `_dispatch_seconds` · `_ttfb_seconds` | Pool contention · backend time · first byte. Limit: TTFB covers pickup plus render start. |

| `httpjet_lsapi_reset_replays_total` / `_reset_replay_exhaustions_total`, `httpjet_lsapi_eagain_*` | Reset replays / exhausted replays, backlog retries. Limit: see replay rules above. |

        ⎁   Measured
PHP/LSAPI over HTTP/1.1: **~44.8k req/s vs LiteSpeed's ~38.5k at c=40** (LiteSpeed best ~41.2k at c=60). In production, PHP render is ~90% of wall time; pool acquire is p99.9  loopback · PGO · 2026-06 · production telemetry 2026-08-30

## The lsphp supervisor

In spawn mode (`serve` without `--lsphp-external`) you supervise `lsphp` yourself. Start with the external pool above for production; read this for spawn-mode limits.

- **Spawn.** The listen socket passes on fd 0; socket-activation listeners stay out of children via `FD_CLOEXEC` and `close_range(..., CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`. Limit: `setsid()` detaches; `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` ties workers to the parent; `pre_exec` uses async-signal-safe calls only.

- **Tracking.** The supervisor is a subreaper for adopted PHP zombies. Limit: each generation family tracks by injected `LSAPI_Z_HTTPJET_GENERATION_MARKER` plus pidfds.

- **Cap.** Config `LSAPI_CHILDREN` is stripped, so `--php-children` / `maxConns` alone caps workers. Limit: values below 2 normalize to 2.

- **Refusals (2026-09-16).** Workers never run as root, even if suEXEC computes uid/gid 0. Limit: a setuid `lsphp` binary is also refused.

- **Deadline.** `--php-max-process-time-ms` gives a total per-request deadline; exceeded means 504. Limit: spawn mode also kills/restarts the worker; external mode has no web-process monitor, so keep it conservative.

        !   Packaging boundary
httpjet ships no PHP runtime; you manage the executable, extensions, `php.ini`, opcache, and writable paths. The repo's hardening runbook (`systemd/httpjet-lsphp.service.d/hardening.conf`, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=no` for opcache JIT) is validated live but off by default.

## The LSAPI wire codec

`proto/{frame,builder}` implements the vendored php-src `lsapidef.h` constants (BSD-3-Clause) byte-for-byte. Remember one rule: each length prefix includes the trailing NUL.

           **proto** · the NUL-inclusive length prefix
```
// each env/header field:  [u16 BE = byte_len + 1] [bytes…] [0x00]
const MAX_FIELD: usize = (u16::MAX as usize) - 1;   // 65534
```

- Fields cap at `u16::MAX − 1` bytes. Limit: longer fields would wrap and desync every later frame, so the handler answers 431 first.

- Bodies scan for an embedded `BEGIN_REQUEST` signature before sending; negative env counts fail at the builder. Limit: the response-header parser is fuzz target `lsapi_resp_header`, one of eight.

- A worker dying before `LSAPI_RESP_END` aborts the body, never truncates silently. Limit: use the shipped `packaging/lsphp/lsapilib-hardening.patch` for upstream `lsapilib.c`; tracing reaches PHP as `HTTP_TRACEPARENT` with OpenTelemetry on.

## The CGI environment

The builder keeps what was requested apart from what runs. `LsapiScript` pins `SCRIPT_FILENAME` while the original `REQUEST_URI` survives, so front-controller routing stays correct.

| Variable | Meaning. Limit: |

| `REQUEST_URI` | Original request URI. Limit: preserved through rewrites. |

| `SCRIPT_FILENAME` / `SCRIPT_NAME` | Resolved on-disk script / URI-space name. Limit: `SCRIPT_NAME`/`QUERY_STRING` upsert via `ctx.env`. |

| `REMOTE_ADDR`, `SERVER_NAME`, `HTTPS`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, `PHP_VALUE`, `PHP_ADMIN_VALUE`, … | Server-computed or special-env only. Limit: since 2026-09-16, `[E=…]`/`SetEnv`/processor `env` naming one is denied (shared with FastCGI). |

| `HTTP_*` | Validated request headers (2026-10-06 rule for CGI, LSAPI, FastCGI). Limit: `Proxy` and underscore names never pass; forwarding-authority names pass only from a trusted, certificate-presenting proxy. |

| `HTTP_*` via LSAPI block | Since 0.1.8, lsphp builds these from the header block. Limit: env table also carries only `Host`, `Content-Type`/`Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, names over 250 bytes, and repeats; `HJ_LSAPI_FULL_HEADER_ENV=1` restores all (FastCGI keeps all). |

| `REMOTE_USER` | Set by successful Basic auth . Limit: realm-authenticated requests only. |

| Special-env section | `php_value` / `php_admin_value` / `php_flag` / `php_admin_flag` from `.htaccess`. Limit: carried on the special-env wire path; plain `lsphp` ignores regular CGI `PHP_VALUE`. |

## The jail

You fence PHP with suEXEC (` `, `uidMin`/`gidMin` floors), chroot (`chrootMode` 0–2, per-vhost `chrootPath`), and optional namespaces. Namespaces cover `mount`, `net`, `uts`, `ipc`; `pid` is accepted but not honored.

- suEXEC off, non-root process, or no per-vhost isolation gives the all-None default `"php"` pool. Limit: single-pool behaviour preserved byte-for-byte.

- An unsafe configured jail disables PHP for that vhost with 503. Limit: uid 0, below-floor uid, bad chroot, out-of-range modes (2026-09-16), or credential-less chroot (0.0.5); never unjailed or static.

        !   Source-disclosure guard
An unavailable pool returns 503, always. Falling through to static would serve raw `.php` source; shared-pool vhosts share worker credentials, so isolation is your suEXEC decision.

## Request bodies

Request bodies now live inside The UDS connection pool . This stub keeps existing links working.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Proxy & gateways (https://httpjet.net/docs/gateways)
SUMMARY: Proxy traffic to other servers and services.
==============================================================================

# Proxy & gateways

You hand requests to other processes here: reverse proxy, WebSocket and SSE relay, and FastCGI. LSAPI/PHP has its own page .

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## How a request reaches a backend

Three routes select a gateway, in dispatch order. Script suffixes route to LSAPI or FastCGI instead.

- Rewrite `[P]` target. Limit: deferred until after the page-cache lookup, so it can still cache.

- WebSocket map (` `). Limit: only when the request carries an upgrade.

- Proxy ` ` whose prefix matches and whose `handler` names a `proxy` extProcessor. Limit: missing, unknown, or non-`proxy` handlers give 503, never static fallthrough.

| Target form | Protocol. Limit: |

| `host:port`, `ip:port`, `uds:///path`, `http://…` | HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive pools. Limit: pool keys are scheme-scoped. |

| `https://…` | HTTP/1.1 over TLS, certificate verified. Limit: optional client cert via `clientCertFile`/`clientKeyFile`. |

| `h2://host:port` httpjet | HTTP/2 prior knowledge (cleartext). Limit: multiplexes on one backend connection. |

| `h2s://host[:443]` httpjet | HTTP/2 over TLS. Limit: ALPN fail-closed; h2 requests re-absolutized for `:scheme`/`:authority`. |

Proxied responses may not assert `X-LiteSpeed-Purge`/`-Cache-Control`/`-Tag`/`-Vary`; you strip them. Named upstreams receive a W3C `traceparent` when tracing is on.

        !   [P] targets are screened

- Since 2026-09-16, a `[P]` URL resolving to any non-public-unicast address is refused. Limit: loopback, unspecified, link-local, RFC 1918, CGNAT, multicast, and documentation ranges count; `/etc/hosts` pins cannot bypass DNS screening.

- Only an exact operator-configured extProcessor or WebSocket-map address exempts a screened target. Limit: Unix-socket `[P]` targets are always refused; concurrent DNS lookups stay bounded.

- When the request can choose the upstream host via substitution, you withhold client credentials. Limit: `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, and `Cookie` are withheld when scheme/authority comes from `$N`/`%N`/`%{…}`.

## Upstream groups & selection

Several ` ` children make a group. Without options you keep ordered primary/failover with a passive breaker: 3 consecutive dial failures mark a peer bad, one success clears it.

           **httpd_config.xml** · a weighted group with active probes
```

   application
   proxy
   127.0.0.1:9001
   127.0.0.1:9002
   weighted-round-robin

   2,1

     GET

/ready application.internal 10 2 2 3 200 ``` > [Diagram: proxy-selection] Selection. Eligibility intersects active health and the passive breaker; policy picks among eligible peers. A pre-head dial failure marks the peer and moves on; sent bodies never replay. > [Diagram: upstream-health] Peer states. A peer starts cold until rise successes; fall failures take it down; probes restore it. All-ineligible gives 503. - **Policies:** `primary-first` (default), `weighted-round-robin` (smooth WRR), `weighted-least-active` (active ÷ weight, WRR tie-break). Limit: invalid policies, weights, or health settings fail config loading. - **Probes:** `connect` tests transport; `GET`/`HEAD` validate TLS, bound the head, compare status exactly, follow no redirects, and consume no body. Limit: no cookies, authorization, or body; 16 concurrent probes process-wide; pool permits untouched. - **Groups share one protocol.** Keep credentials, paths, and queries out of group authorities. Limit: a `Host` override never overrides TLS identity. - **Reloads:** candidates start no probes; publication starts the new scheduler and retires the old. Limit: unchanged identities keep state; changed endpoints, weights, policies, or TLS identities start fresh. - **Reservations** survive the response head. Limit: streams and WebSocket relays release the active count on completion, error, or drop. Metrics carry scope, group, and ordinal labels only: `httpjet_proxy_peer_{healthy,probes_total,health_transitions_total,active_requests,selections_total,prehead_failures_total}`, `httpjet_proxy_failover_total`, `httpjet_phase_upstream_seconds`. See the status API .

## Streaming, SSE and timeouts

Upstream responses never buffer (`respBuffer` parses but always streams; `check` warns). SSE stays real-time through compression and H1, H2, and H3.

| Timeout | Meaning. Limit: |

| Backend connect | `initTimeout` bounds the connect. Limit: see your processor configuration. |

| Response head | Processor default bounds the head. Limit: a context `responseTimeout` overrides it. |

| Backend timeout | An exceeded backend deadline answers 504. Limit: request bodies still stream to h1/h2 upstreams. |

| Request body size | A context `maxReqBodySize` is enforced before dispatch. Limit: before any backend work. |

## WebSocket relay

A ` ` map (`uri` → `address`) or a `ws://` rewrite `[P]` performs the HTTP/1 backend handshake, then relays raw frames. An upgrade reaching an ordinary proxy ` ` without a map gets 426.

- Upstreams are plain TCP HTTP/1 only. Limit: no TLS, H2, or Unix-socket targets.

- Maps carry a stable `websocket: ` identity, vhost-scoped, for trace propagation. Limit: the client span covers the handshake, not the unbounded relay.

- TCP keepalive stays on. Limit: a vanished peer cannot pin fds and permits forever.

## FastCGI gateway opt-in

Declare ` fcgi ` or `fastcgi` for `ExtKind::FastCgi` — never a silent proxy/LSAPI conversion. Only an explicit `cgi` handler naming it dispatches; httpjet spawns nothing, connecting to your supervised TCP/Unix endpoint.

           **vhost XML** · FastCGI suffix routing
```

   my_fcgi
   fcgi
   uds:///run/my-app/fcgi.sock
   32
   5

30 fcgi cgi my_fcgi ``` > [Diagram: fastcgi-flow] One request through hj-fastcgi. The gateway takes an already-validated script target and never derives an executable from the URI. Only a clean, exact END_REQUEST makes a connection reusable; multiplexing is disabled. - **Wire bounds:** FastCGI version 1, nonzero request id, known record types, 65,535-byte records. Limit: PARAMS rejected before allocation past field or aggregate caps. - **Pool:** all sockets, including idle and dialing, cap under one acquisition deadline. Limit: poison/drop releases capacity immediately; clean idle sockets expire oldest-first. - **CGI variables** are server-derived; headers become validated `HTTP_*`. Limit: processor `env` cannot override `SCRIPT_FILENAME`, `DOCUMENT_ROOT`, `REMOTE_ADDR`, `SERVER_NAME`, `CONTENT_LENGTH`, `HTTP_AUTHORIZATION`, etc. (same deny-list as LSAPI `[E=]`). - **Bodies** buffer under the shared budget for an exact STDIN length. Limit: underflow/overflow, framing errors, and cancellation poison the connection. - **Responses:** strict CRLF head, repeated end-to-end headers kept, one valid `Status`, CGI `Location` default, folding rejected. Limit: hop-by-hop and `X-LiteSpeed-*` stripped; missing `END_REQUEST` aborts; STDERR is capped and escaped into the error log only. Known follow-ups: CGI context-directory routing (today suffix mappings only), a codec fragmentation corpus, and a real-application interoperability fixture.

## Conventional CGI and uWSGI not routable

Generic CGI and uWSGI stay disabled until a demonstrated workload exists; see Capabilities . Existing `type=cgi`, `rails`, `appserver`, and unknown types never activate them, and `check --strict` warns on CGI contexts.

Proposed identities are `type=cgi-exec` and `type=uwsgi`. Their contracts require fixed non-root identities, strict limits, and (for CGI) direct `execve` with inode pinning; uWSGI would use modifier-0 packets only, no multiplexing or reuse.

## Reproducible checks

           **tests** · loopback fixtures only
```
cargo test --locked -p hj-config -p hj-proxy
cargo test --locked -p hj-proxy --test upstream_groups     # h1/h2 weighted distribution, cold start, down/recovery, all-down 503
cargo test -p hj-fastcgi                                    # synthetic loopback responder + clean-connection reuse
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet
```

To return a group to legacy selection, remove `loadBalancePolicy`, `addressWeights` and `healthCheck` and reload; removing only the health check keeps the configured policy.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Compression (https://httpjet.net/docs/compression)
SUMMARY: How responses shrink for faster delivery.
==============================================================================

# Compression

`hj-compress` encodes responses with gzip, brotli and zstd. You get **gzip on by default; br/zstd are opt-in**. Server priority picks the codec, bounded by the client's `Accept-Encoding`.

        resolve    acl    rewrite    cache    dispatch    finalize    store

## Codecs and negotiation

| Codec | Backend | Default level | XML switches |

| zstd | `zstd` | 3 (1–22) | `enableZstdCompress`, `enableDynZstdCompress`, `zstdCompressLevel` |

| brotli | `brotli` | 5 (0–11). Limit: without `brCompressLevel`, `enableBrCompress` level 1–6 sets it, 0 disables. | `enableBrCompress`, `enableDynBrCompress`, `brCompressLevel` |

| gzip | `flate2` | 6 (1–9) | `enableGzipCompress`, `enableDynGzipCompress`, `gzipCompressLevel` |

> [Diagram: compression-negotiation] Choosing an encoder. Bodies of 200 bytes or fewer are never compressed (OpenLiteSpeed parity), the compressible-type set matches LiteSpeed's compressibleTypes, already-encoded and 206 responses are skipped, and every encoded response carries Vary: Accept-Encoding.

**What gets compressed** — check each item:

- Bodies over 200 bytes. Limit: 200 bytes or fewer never compress.

- Types in LiteSpeed's `compressibleTypes`. Limit: other types pass through.

- Unencoded, non-206 responses. Limit: already-encoded and 206 responses skip.

- Buffered bodies in one shot. Limit: streamed bodies stay streaming.

- Every encoded response. Limit: it carries `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.

zstd uses a per-thread `ZSTD_CCTX` pool and pooled buffers (`hj_core::recycle::BODY_BUFS`). Streamed bodies (`Body::Stream`) wrap in a lazy `CompressStream`, so SSE stays real-time.

## Trusted-proxy zstd egress

`--cf-send-zstd` (or `CF_SEND_ZSTD=1`) forces zstd to a *trusted-proxy* peer, ignoring forwarded `Accept-Encoding`. Cloudflare re-encodes per browser at its edge, so browser bytes stay unchanged (cheapest-to-produce form; officially unsupported CDN↔origin). Off by default; enabled in production. It never applies to untrusted clients.

## Precompressed siblings

Serve an existing `.br`/`.gz` sibling directly (`gzip_static`/`brotli_static`, brotli preferred), with matching `Content-Encoding`/`Vary`. Ranged requests skip the swap. A missing sibling costs one stat, then on-the-fly compression.

## Interaction with the page cache

The page cache keeps identity bytes plus one best variant (server priority). Other clients get a per-serve re-encode. Dictionaries never reach the wire; hits decode to identity first.

## Request decompression

You decode one supported `Content-Encoding` after full body framing. Decoding runs before rewrite, cache, WAF, proxy and dispatch. One decoder serves HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, h2c and HTTP/3. Gzip is on by default; brotli and zstd are opt-in:

           **serve** · opt-in codings
```
httpjet --root /abs/root serve … --request-decompression-extra br,zstd     # accepts br, brotli, zstd; "gzip" is rejected as redundant
```

> [Diagram: request-decompression] Bounded, buffered, fail-safe. Only exactly one coding is decoded; malformed streams and the 16 MiB ceiling forward the original representation unchanged (the destination applies its own policy); the codec workspace and both body forms are charged to the shared budget first.

- A successful decode removes `Content-Encoding`. It replaces `Content-Length` with the decoded length before any handler runs.

- Decoded output may not exceed `maxReqBodySize` (413). Limit: the absolute decoder ceiling is 16 MiB.

- At the 16 MiB ceiling, you forward the encoded body unchanged. Limit: you never expose a truncated body.

- Brotli large-window extensions stay disabled. Limit: zstd frames cap at a 2 24 -byte window; `deflate` never decodes.

- Brotli/zstd reserve 17 MiB for decoder tables first. Limit: if workspace plus both body forms cannot reserve, you get 503.

**Limits.** Response-side decoding caps `windowLogMax` and bounds decoded size. A hostile or corrupt frame fails the decode instead of ballooning memory. Compare representative hits and misses before trading CPU for bytes. Production samples this phase as `httpjet_phase_compress_seconds`.

           **tests**
```
cargo test --locked -p httpjet uring::request_body --no-fail-fast     # all three codecs, bombs, malformed input, stacked encodings, workspace exhaustion
```

## Decode safety

See Request decompression → Limits . Response-side caps now live there.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Extending httpjet (https://httpjet.net/docs/extensions)
SUMMARY: Add trusted code and sidecar checks.
==============================================================================

# Extending httpjet

Extend httpjet two ways: linked Rust crates, or a WAF sidecar. No dynamic plugin ABI exists. No in-process sandbox exists. This page states that once.

Rust offers no stable trait-object ABI across shared libraries. Native modules would share allocator, signals, threads anyway. No workload needs untrusted in-process code. No WASM runtime ships. Route untrusted inspection via the sidecar. Future untrusted designs must define capabilities, memory, fuel, deadlines, cancellation, body access, state, network access, versioning, fail semantics first.

| Need | Hooks | Sidecar |

| Custom headers/policy | Yes. Limit: rebuild + restart. | No. Limit: inspection only. |

| Blocking rules | Yes, in Rust. Limit: in-process. | Yes. Limit: external engine. |

| Independent deploy | No. Limit: linked build. | Yes. Limit: call per request. |

| Untrusted code | No. Limit: trusted only. | Outside process. Limit: bounded document. |

## Compile-time extensions

Assemble `hj-extension::ExtensionRegistry` at `crates/httpjet/src/extensions.rs`. Shipped binary registers nothing. Facility stays inert without your build. Contract: source-level, over frozen `hj-core` types. No stable native ABI.

           **extensions.rs** · registration
```
pub(crate) fn compiled_registry() -> hj_extension::ExtensionRegistry {
    let mut registry = hj_extension::ExtensionRegistry::new();
    registry.register_pre_handler("company.request-policy", company_policy::hook()).expect("unique");
    registry.register_response_transform("company.headers", company_headers::transform()).expect("unique");
    registry
}
```

Registration order = execution order. Names: unique, 1–64 bytes, lowercase ASCII, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`. Logged once at boot. Changes need rebuild + restart. SIGHUP carries registry forward. Settings belong to your crate. No XML reinterpretation. No runtime loader.

> [Diagram: extension-hooks] Where hooks run. Pre-handlers run after trust and access resolution but before everything that could serve a byte; response transforms run after dispatch (and after page-cache storage) but before httpjet's own transforms, so an extension changes egress, not the canonical cached object, and is re-applied on hits.

### Pre-handler contract

`PreHandler` gets immutable `ReqCtx` plus `RequestView`. View exposes method, URI, headers only. No body, no mutable parts. Return `Continue` (next hook, then dispatch), `Respond(response)` (skip dispatch; transforms/metrics/logging still run), or `Err(HandlerError)` (fail closed, log failure). Never sees reserved routes (ACME, cache endpoints) or earlier rejections.

**Any pre-handler disables the fast path.** Memo/cache/static fast path cannot run async hooks. Response-only extensions keep it.

### Response-transform contract

`ResponseTransform`s run in order, on full-pipeline and on-core responses. Run before host transforms: promotion, expires, sub_filter, compression, redirect guard, Alt-Svc. See origin form, pre-compression. Cannot bypass final header policy. No error return. Keep work bounded. Fail setup at registration.

        !   In-process means full authority
Extension code runs with httpjet's memory and filesystem authority. A panic, deadlock, unbounded allocation or blocking call affects the server. Only trusted, reviewed crates belong in the registry.

## WAF sidecar

httpjet embeds no rules engine. Ignored `lsrecaptcha`/`censorshipControl` stay inactive. Enable `--waf-sidecar-addr` for loopback inspection instead. Transport: Unix socket (`unix:/path`, peer UID via `SO_PEERCRED` vs `--waf-sidecar-uid`) or loopback TCP (`ip:port`). Fits Coraza/OWASP CRS adapters. httpjet claims no CRS compatibility. Adapter owns engine translation.

           **serve** · sidecar flags
```
--waf-sidecar-addr unix:/run/waf/inspect.sock   # or loopback 127.0.0.1:19090; absent = seam inert
--waf-sidecar-uid 0                   # uid a unix: sidecar must run as (default: root or serving uid)
--waf-sidecar-path /inspect           # absolute, no control characters
--waf-timeout-ms 100                  # total deadline: admission + allowance + connect + write + parse (≤ 30 s)
--waf-body-max 65536                  # bodies at or below this are sent as body_hex (≤ 1 MiB)
--waf-concurrency 128                 # ≤ 4096
--waf-fail-open                       # weaker policy: continue on sidecar failure (every bypass is logged; 403 still blocks)
```

> [Diagram: waf-sidecar] One inspection per request. Inspection runs after URI decoding/normalization and body-limit enforcement but before rewrite, cache lookup and any backend — background cache refreshes go through the same dispatch and are inspected too. Only two replies are valid; everything else is a sidecar failure.

### Document

Sends `version: 1`, method, normalized path, query, vhost, client IP, protocol, TLS state, all headers. Headers and body use lowercase hex. Hex stays lossless, injection-safe. Adapters reject unsupported versions.

### Bodies

≤ `--waf-body-max`: `body_hex`, restored byte-identically. Larger: `body_omitted: true`, sidecar decides explicitly. Global request limit stays authoritative.

### Limits

Concurrency cap plus shared 64 MiB serialization budget. Each inspection reserves byte-weighted allowance before copying. Waiting counts inside deadline, follows fail policy. Stalled calls cannot multiply heap.

### Transport

One close-delimited HTTP/1.1 POST per inspection. Never reused. Response head ≤ 4 KiB. Only 204/403 valid. Failures: duplicate/nonzero Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, malformed status, EOF, other statuses.

           **tests**
```
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet pipeline::e2e::waf_runs_before_static_cache_and_can_block_a_previously_allowed_path
cargo test -p httpjet --bin httpjet pipeline::e2e::waf_sidecar_failure_policy_is_closed_unless_explicitly_opened
cargo test -p hj-extension
```

## Why there is no dynamic or sandboxed plugin ABI

See lede note. Choice stated once there. Untrusted inspection: WAF sidecar .

==============================================================================
PAGE: CLI reference (https://httpjet.net/docs/cli)
SUMMARY: Every command, flag, and environment variable.
==============================================================================

# CLI reference

One binary, four subcommands. You set persistent policy in XML. You set operational overrides on the command line. This page is generated from `httpjet serve --help` of the current release.

## Subcommands

           **httpjet** [--root DIR] <subcommand>
```
httpjet --root /abs/root check [--strict]     # parse + summary + lint; --strict exits non-zero on lint errors (deploy gate)
httpjet --root /abs/root serve [flags…]       # bind the configured listeners and serve
httpjet --root /abs/root lsphp [flags…]       # run a standalone persistent lsphp pool (the PHP half of a zero-downtime deploy)
httpjet lsphp-reload [flags…]                 # ask a running pool to replace its worker generation without closing the listener
httpjet --version                             # httpjet 0.2.0
```

| Subcommand · flag | Default | Meaning |

| `--root ` (global) | `/usr/local/lsws` | Server root containing `conf/httpd_config.xml`. Use an absolute path. |

| `check --strict` | off | Hard-error on shared docroots, missing docroots, mapped vhosts whose config did not load, and an unloadable first TLS listener; warn (never fail) on vhosts without an exact `vhostMap` domain, apex-without-www, wildcard map patterns, TLS over UDS, PROXY protocol on public binds, inert LiteSpeed elements, generic CGI contexts, unsupported auth forms. Geo rules without a db fail `check` even without `--strict`. Plain `check` prints the same lint lines, `vhost-map-fingerprint` and fast-memo verdicts; `--strict` only makes errors exit non-zero. |

| `lsphp --php-socket` | `/tmp/php8-httpjet.sock` | Socket lsphp listens on — the path `serve --lsphp-external` dials. A systemd-activated fd at the same path is adopted. |

| `lsphp --php-children` | `0` | 0 = honor the XML `PHP_LSAPI_CHILDREN`/`maxConns`; >0 overrides; values below 2 normalize to 2. |

| `lsphp --control-socket` | ` .control` | Root-only control socket used by `lsphp-reload`. Defaults beside the pool socket so a test pool can never answer the production control path. |

| `lsphp --generation-file` | ` .generation` | The 16-byte epoch + marker file external web pools map. Defaults beside the pool socket so a test pool can never advance the production epoch. |

| `lsphp-reload --control-socket` | `/run/httpjet/lsphp-control.sock` | Control socket of the running supervisor. |

| `lsphp-reload --timeout-secs` | `90` | Maximum wait for candidate readiness and old-generation drain. |

## serve flags

**Most operators need these:** `--http-addr`, `--https-addr`, `--workers`, `--root`, `--page-cache`, `--php-socket`, `--lsphp-external`, `--no-mtls`, `--metrics-addr`, and `--no-php`. You set the rest only for specific needs.

Type to filter; click a group to narrow. Defaults are the binary's; *(empty)* means an empty string disables the feature.

| Flag | Default | Meaning |

| Listeners & transport |

| --http-addr   | 127.0.0.1:8080 | Address for the plain-HTTP listener |

| --https-addr   | 127.0.0.1:4443 | Address for the TLS listener. Empty to disable |

| --workers   | — | Number of accept-loop workers (SO_REUSEPORT sockets). Defaults to CPUs |

| --no-core-pinning | off | Do not pin the per-core io_uring transport threads to their CPU cores. Pinning is automatic (and only) when the worker count equals the number of CPUs the process may run on (its affinity mask); this flag is the kill switch if pinned placement worsens tail latency |

| --uring-ring   | coop | Sets io_uring ring mode: `coop`, `legacy`, or `defer`. Measured: see Performance . |

| --no-cpu-steering | off | Kill switch for listener CPU steering. Pinned TCP workers normally ask the kernel (SO_INCOMING_CPU) for the connections whose SYN arrived on their CPU, so RSS/RPS placement and the serving core coincide Steering is also skipped automatically unless every device-backed NIC that is up has at least as many receive queues (or RPS CPUs) as there are workers; the startup log says so. |

| --ready-file   | — | Atomically publish this process's PID after worker activation. The absolute path must be fresh and its parent directory owned by root or this account |

| --h3-engine   | legacy | HTTP/3 request engine. The accelerated engine tries the shared on-core cache path before dispatching misses through the io_uring bridge Values: `legacy`, `accelerated`, `auto`. |

| --h3-gso-segments   | 10 | Maximum HTTP/3 datagrams in one GSO transmit. The experimental value 20 retains the same 20-datagram flush budget; the default remains 10 Values: `10`, `20`. |

| --h3-send-batch   | 1 | Maximum UDP messages per send syscall; 1 retains the scalar path Values: `1`, `4`, `8`, `16`. |

| --h3-ack-eliciting-threshold   | 0 | Ask HTTP/3 peers that support QUIC ACK_FREQUENCY to acknowledge every N ack-eliciting packets instead of every second one. 0 (default) asks nothing |

| --h3-max-ack-delay-us   | 1000 | The max_ack_delay requested along with --h3-ack-eliciting-threshold |

| --no-multishot-accept | off | Disable multishot accept: submit one accept SQE per connection (the pre-multishot behavior) instead of one armed SQE per listener |

| --http-uds   | — | Additionally serve plain HTTP on this unix domain socket (H1 + h2c prior knowledge, one accept core). Peers have no address: ACLs and logs see fabricated loopback and the access log renders `unix:` — the socket file's mode/owner is the real access boundary. A socket-activated fd at the same path (socket unit) is adopted for zero-downtime restarts |

| --ktls [ ] | auto | Controls kernel TLS: `auto`, `on`, or `off`. Limit: TLS 1.3 only; validate first. |

| Security & limits |

| --no-mtls | off | Local testing / explicit rollback only: drop the mandatory Cloudflare client-cert requirement so TLS content can be tested locally without a Cloudflare-issued client cert. Without this flag, clientVerify=2 validates every presented certificate during TLS. A peer that presents none completes the handshake, then the request pipeline rejects it before dispatch (except the loopback exemption) |

| --per-ip-rate   | — | Per-client-IP request throttle: max requests per client IP per second. 0 (default) = disabled — overrides the ` ` tuning field when set. Protects the origin from single-source floods; a shared NAT egress aggregates many visitors, so size accordingly |

| --request-decompression-extra   | (empty) | Additional request Content-Encoding values to decode before dispatch. Gzip remains enabled for compatibility; Brotli and zstd are opt-in. Accepted comma-separated values: br,zstd |

| --trusted-proxy-idle-secs   | 0 | Idle window in seconds for connections whose peer presented a VERIFIED client certificate (in prod, only Cloudflare's authenticated-origin-pull cert). CF never resumes TLS to the origin, so closing a connection it would have reused costs a full TCP + TLS + mTLS handshake. 0 keeps the normal 90 s floor for everyone; uncertified peers always keep it |

| --trusted-proxy-idle-max-conns   | 6000 | Above this many open connections, certified connections fall back to the normal idle floor (bounds idle state during a connection surge) |

| --tls-session-tickets   | 2 | TLS 1.3 session tickets issued per full handshake (rustls default 2). 0 stops minting them and shrinks the session cache to TLS 1.2 session IDs: Cloudflare's origin pull never resumes (`httpjet_tls_handshakes_resumed_total` stays 0), so the tickets only cost two records per handshake plus a cached copy of its client-cert chain |

| --auth-user-file-roots   | (empty) | Extra directories (comma-separated) where a `.htaccess` AuthUserFile may live, besides the vhost docroot |

| PHP / LSAPI |

| --no-php | off | Do not spawn lsphp; PHP requests fall back to static serving |

| --php-children   | 0 | LSAPI worker children for the lsphp pool. 0 (default) = honor the lsws config's `PHP_LSAPI_CHILDREN` / `maxConns` (true drop-in). A value > 0 is an explicit override (e.g. to cap concurrency on a shared box); values below 2 are normalized to 2 for persistent supervision |

| --php-socket   | /tmp/php8-httpjet.sock | Socket path for httpjet's OWN lsphp pool — deliberately separate from the production php8.sock so the two never contend |

| --lsphp-external   | — | EXTERNAL lsphp: connect to an lsphp master already listening on this socket (run by a separate `httpjet lsphp` process) instead of spawning one. Lets the web tier restart for a zero-downtime binary deploy without cold- starting PHP. Overrides --php-socket. Mutually exclusive with spawning |

| --lsphp-generation-file   | — | Shared lsphp generation epoch used to invalidate pooled external connections after a supervisor reload or restart. When supplied with --lsphp-external, startup fails if the 16-byte mapping cannot be opened |

| --php-max-process-time-ms   | — | Sets the PHP processing deadline. Limit: external pools return 504 only; workers stay wedged. |

| Page cache — you enable the tier, then size storage, then tune admission and vary rules. Most sites need only `--page-cache` plus memory sizing. |

| --page-cache | off | Enable the LSCache-equivalent origin full-page cache (OFF by default; opt-in / R&D). Per-vhost ` ` + `.htaccess CacheLookup` still gate each request, and the app must opt responses in via `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control`. With this flag absent the cache is inert |

| --page-cache-mem   | 134217728 | RAM budget (bytes) for the in-process index: entry metadata + precompressed variants + any in-RAM body. With --page-cache-store-path, persisted (tmpfs) bodies do NOT count here — they are bounded by --page-cache-disk-mem instead — so this should be sized for metadata, not body bytes. Without a file tier it is the whole body budget, as before. Default 128 MiB |

| --page-cache-disk-mem   | 2147483648 | tmpfs file-tier footprint budget (bytes) for --page-cache-store-path: the disk LRU evicts the least-recently-served entry once charged file footprint under the store path exceeds this. tmpfs IS RAM, so size it against the box's headroom (with dict compression a 2 GiB cap holds the compressed equivalent of ~7–18 GiB of pages). 0 ⇒ fall back to --page-cache-mem. Ignored without a file tier. Default 2 GiB |

| --page-cache-store-path   | none | Directory for the PERSISTENT tmpfs file tier. The default is "none": bodies stay in the in-process RAM cache and flush on restart. Pass an explicit directory such as /dev/shm/jetcache to opt into the LiteSpeed-Enterprise-style store where bodies live as files and the cache survives restarts via a boot-time warm scan. The LiteSpeed config's cacheStorePath is intentionally NOT used |

| --page-cache-integrity-key   | /usr/local/httpjet/conf/.jetcache.key | Integrity key used for persistent cache containers |

| --page-cache-integrity-required | off | Refuse to start the file tier when the integrity key cannot be installed, instead of running with untagged containers |

| --page-cache-hot-mem   | 201326592 | Byte cap of the in-RAM hot tier in front of the file store (zero-syscall zero-copy serves for the hottest bodies). Only meaningful with --page-cache-store-path. Default 192 MiB |

| --page-cache-dict   | (empty) | Sets the shared zstd dictionary path. Limit: absent stores plain identity. |

| --page-cache-dict-vhost   | (empty) | Comma-separated `vhost=path` pairs: a PER-VHOST zstd dictionary, trained on that vhost's own content (train one local corpus per vhost). A shared dictionary trained on one site's boilerplate does little for a differently templated site, so each vhost compresses against its own. A vhost not listed here falls back to --page-cache-dict if set, else stores identity (today's behaviour). Example: `forum.example=conf/pagecache-forum.dict,moon.example=conf/pagecache-moon.dict` |

| --page-cache-dict-level   | (empty) | Comma-separated `vhost=level` pairs overriding the internal zstd level (1-19, default 12) of that vhost's dictionary. A vhost whose compressed bodies round to the same 4 KiB tmpfs pages at a cheaper level gains nothing from 12 (one production vhost costs 5× less at level 3 with no footprint change). A malformed pair aborts startup |

| --page-cache-vary-default   | (empty) | Comma-separated `name=value` pairs: a vary cookie carrying this value is keyed like no cookie (the app treats the default the same way). E.g. `xf_style_id=50` |

| --page-cache-opt-in-status   | (empty) | Comma-separated extra statuses (from 303, 404, 410) cached only when the app sends an explicit `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: public`, with the TTL capped at 300 s and no stale windows. Empty = off (only 200/301 are cached) |

| --page-cache-303-prefixes   | (empty) | Comma-separated request-path prefixes under which an opted-in 303 may be stored (e.g. `/whats-new/`). A 303 anywhere else is never stored |

| --page-cache-stream-fill-vhosts   | (empty) | Comma-separated vhost names whose cacheable page-cache misses WITHOUT a Content-Length (progressive template output) are sent to the client as the backend writes them and stored once the backend finishes, instead of being buffered whole first. Only identity-encoded public 200s; a body that errors, is cut short or grows past the object cap is served but never stored. Empty = off |

| --page-cache-egress-at-rest-vhosts   | (empty) | Keeps plain zstd storage for listed vhosts. Limit: buffered misses only; storage grows. |

| --page-cache-admit-threshold   | 2 | Sets the W-TinyLFU admission bar. Limit: size adds +1 per 256 KiB. |

| --page-cache-vary-cookies   | xf_style_variation,xf_style_id,xf_language_id | Comma-separated public-vary cookie names: a cacheable public response may declare `X-LiteSpeed-Vary: cookie=NAME,...` and the entry is keyed by these cookies' values (shared, non-sensitive prefs). Default matches the XenForo style/language set |

| --page-cache-private-cookies   | xf_session,xf_user | Comma-separated cookie names that forbid public caching if a public response tries to Set-Cookie them (session guard). Default: XenForo |

| --page-cache-private | off | Enable the per-session PRIVATE cache tier: an `X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: private[,max-age=N]` response from a logged-in request is stored keyed by the session cookie and served only to that same session. OFF by default — without the flag a private opt-in bypasses exactly as before |

| --page-cache-private-session-cookie   | xf_session | Request cookie whose VALUE keys a private entry's owner (the session) |

| --page-cache-private-user-cookie   | xf_user | Request cookie whose PRESENCE routes a request to the private tier (the logged-in marker; XenForo's remember cookie) |

| --page-cache-shared-paths   | (empty) | Lists visitor-invariant endpoints members may share publicly. Limit: list identical bytes only, never HTML. |

| --page-cache-shared-paths-canary-percent   | 100 | Deterministic percentage (0-100) of member requests matching --page-cache-shared-paths that actually route to the public tier; the rest keep today's private-tier behavior. Sticky per member (bucketed by a hash of the user/session cookie value, exactly like --xf-capsule-member-canary-percent), so one member never flickers between tiers. 100 = all matching requests |

| --page-cache-standard-vhosts   | (empty) | Puts listed vhosts in standards mode. Limit: unlisted vhosts stay X-LiteSpeed-only. |

| --page-cache-stale-default-secs   | 0 | Stale-while-revalidate window (seconds) applied when the app declares none. 0 = off (serve only fresh unless the app sets stale-while-revalidate / max-stale) |

| --page-cache-stale-max-secs   | 86400 | Hard cap (seconds) on the stale-while-revalidate window honored from the app |

| --page-cache-stale-if-error-max-secs   | 86400 | Hard cap (seconds) on the stale-if-error window honored from the app |

| --page-cache-stale-if-error-default-secs   | 0 | Stale-if-error window (seconds) applied when the app declares none: how long past freshness a public entry stays servable as a backend-5xx fallback (a brief lsphp/DB outage serves slightly-stale pages instead of error pages). 0 = off (the prior behavior: only an app-declared stale-if-error window arms the fallback) |

| XenForo capsules |

| --xf-capsule | off | Enable XenForo public-shell capsules. Requires --page-cache; otherwise inert |

| --xf-capsule-vhosts   | (empty) | Comma-separated resolved vhost names allowed to serve capsules. Empty DISABLES the capsule tier for every vhost (#239 fail-closed default) |

| --xf-capsule-paths   | /,/forums/,/threads/,/whats-new/,/help/ | Comma-separated request-path prefixes eligible for capsule lookup/store |

| --xf-capsule-safe-get-mode   | prefixes | Capsule route coverage. `prefixes` honors --xf-capsule-paths; `all-get-classified` uses a conservative unsafe-route classifier Values: `prefixes, all-get-classified`. |

| --xf-capsule-stale-secs   | 86400 | Stale-while-revalidate window for capsule shell entries. This is applied to public-shell capsule stores even if the app declares a smaller window |

| --xf-capsule-canary-percent   | 100 | Deterministic percentage of eligible requests that may be served a capsule hit |

| --xf-capsule-members | off | Allow explicitly-marked member-cookie requests to receive public-shell capsules |

| --xf-capsule-member-canary-percent   | 0 | Deterministic percentage of eligible member-cookie requests that may receive capsules |

| Performance knobs |

| --no-fast-memo | off | Disable the finished-response memo on the on-core static fast path (default ON; per-thread, 1 s TTL, byte-identity-gated — see `pipeline::fast_memo`). Env `HJ_FAST_MEMO=0` is equivalent |

| --no-page-cache-response-memo | off | Disable the per-worker memo of finalized public page-cache hits (default ON since 0.1.11, with `--page-cache`; cookieless GET only; entries keep exact freshness/Age/purge fences and share the fast-memo budget). The old `--page-cache-response-memo` opt-in still parses for existing units |

| --fast-early-bridge   | off | Bridge a cookieless request to the full pipeline before the on-core prefix when nothing on-core can serve it: the page cache cannot answer the path and the static branch would decline. `off` (default) is today's path; `shadow` only counts what `on` would do (`httpjet_fast_early_predicted_total`, `httpjet_fast_early_forfeit_total`). Env `HJ_FAST_EARLY_BRIDGE` is equivalent and takes precedence. Values: `off, shadow, on`. |

| --cf-send-zstd | off | Sends zstd to trusted Cloudflare peers. Limit: never applies to direct clients. |

| --rewrite-outcome-ttl-ms   | 1000 | TTL in milliseconds for the rewrite-outcome cache (memoized rewrite decisions for `path_cacheable` chains, keyed by vhost/scheme/ method/host/path/query + any keyable header vars). 0 disables the cache entirely. The default (1000 ms) matches the historical hard-coded TTL — it bounds `-f`/`-d` filesystem staleness exactly like the StatCache and lets `.htaccess` edits take effect within ~1 s |

| --rewrite-ua-classify | off | Key UA-reading rewrite chains by the bitmap of matching User-Agent RewriteConds instead of the raw UA string, when parse-time analysis proves the outcome depends on the UA only through those match results. Collapses real-world UA diversity (near-zero hit rate on raw UAs) onto a handful of outcome-cache entries. Default OFF — enabling is a deploy-time decision |

| Memory |

| --mimalloc-trim-secs   | 120 | Interval (seconds) for the background mimalloc OS-trim that calls mi_collect(force) to hand retained/cold arena pages back to the OS (counters the swap retention seen in prod after a burst). 0 = disable |

| --mimalloc-trim-threshold-mib   | 768 | Only run the mimalloc trim (periodic and after a connection close) when process RSS+swap (read from /proc/self/status) is at least this many MiB; 0 = always. Lets a healthy process skip the collect entirely. Default 768: above a cache-less steady state (~360 MiB). Size it above the deployment's healthy peak (a large page cache holds 1-2 GiB) so only genuine post-burst arena retention trips the safety-net reclaim |

| Observability |

| --metrics-addr   | 127.0.0.1:9090 | Loopback-only Prometheus metrics endpoint address. Empty to disable. Exposes the page-cache hit/miss ratio (the key operational number once --page-cache is live) plus request/connection counters |

| --telemetry-file   | (empty) | Append a cumulative per-request telemetry snapshot row to this file every --telemetry-flush-secs: durability across restarts + a self-contained time-series for the two-node A/B. Empty = no disk flush (the in-RAM aggregates + the :9090 endpoint still work). e.g. logs/telemetry.tsv |

| --telemetry-flush-secs   | 30 | Snapshot flush interval in seconds (only used when --telemetry-file is set). Fixed RAM; ~1 MB/day on disk at the default |

| --php-slow-log   | (empty) | Per-request PHP render log: a TSV line for every LSAPI request whose render TTFB exceeds --php-slow-threshold-ms, plus a 1-in-128 sample of ALL PHP requests as the population baseline — the per-URL / user-class attribution behind the lsapi_ttfb histogram. Rolls at 64 MiB, gzip archives, 7-day prune. Empty = disabled. e.g. logs/php-slow.tsv |

| --php-slow-threshold-ms   | 50 | "Slow" threshold in milliseconds for --php-slow-log |

| --request-id-header | off | Echo the per-request correlation id (also in the access/error/php-slow logs) as an `X-Request-Id` response header, so a client/CDN can join a response to the server-side logs. Off by default |

| --profile-token   | (empty) | Bearer secret required for profiling and sensitive metrics diagnostics. Empty disables those routes; ordinary metrics scraping stays available. Visible in /proc/*/cmdline; prefer `--profile-token-file` |

| --profile-token-file   | — | File holding the --profile-token secret (single-link regular file owned by root or the serving user, no group/other permissions). Conflicts with `--profile-token`. |

| Admin API |

| --admin-addr   | — | Opt-in read-only operational JSON endpoint (loopback TCP only) |

| --admin-write-addr   | — | Authenticated application-config writes on a separate loopback listener |

| --admin-token-file   | — | Private file containing a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal bearer token |

| --admin-resource-root   | — | Allowed existing filesystem root for submitted resources; repeatable |

| WAF sidecar |

| --waf-sidecar-addr   | — | Opt-in HTTP request-inspection sidecar: `unix:/path` (its listener's uid is verified) or a loopback `ip:port` (unauthenticated). The sidecar must return 204 to allow or 403 to block; absent keeps the WAF seam inert |

| --waf-sidecar-uid   | — | The uid a `unix:` sidecar must run as. Default: root or this process's uid |

| --waf-sidecar-path   | /inspect | Sets the sidecar inspection path. |

| --waf-timeout-ms   | 100 | Sets the sidecar timeout in milliseconds. |

| --waf-body-max   | 65536 | Caps inspected body bytes. |

| --waf-concurrency   | 128 | Caps concurrent sidecar inspections. |

| --waf-fail-open | off | Continue when the configured WAF sidecar is unavailable or malformed. Default is fail-closed (503); this weaker policy requires explicit opt-in |

| ACME (--features acme) |

| --acme-directory   | — | ACME directory URL (HTTPS). Requires --acme-domains, --acme-store and --acme-accept-terms; nothing runs without all four. |

| --acme-domains   | — | Comma-separated DNS identifiers (1–100, ASCII A-labels). Wildcards need DNS-01. Quote a wildcard in the shell. |

| --acme-store   | — | Pre-provisioned private directory, mode 0700, owned by the service uid; holds atomic account/order/certificate snapshots and the DNS cleanup journal. |

| --acme-accept-terms | off | Explicit agreement to the CA terms of service. |

| --acme-bootstrap | off | Start with no listener default certificate; TLS handshakes fail until issuance succeeds. No self-signed placeholder. |

| --acme-reconcile-order   | — | One-shot recovery of an ambiguous newOrder from the same account's CA records. |

| --acme-dns-webhook   | — | Provider-neutral DNS controller endpoint (selects DNS-01). Requires --acme-dns-zones. |

| --acme-dns-zones   | — | Zone allowlist for TXT operations. |

| --acme-dns-token-file   | — | Bearer token for the controller: regular single-link file, mode 0600, 16–4096 printable characters. |

| --acme-test-mode | off | Loopback CA HTTP and alternate loopback validation ports for fixtures only; serving addresses must be loopback. |

| --acme-test-ca-root · --acme-test-issuer-root · --acme-dns-test-root   | — | Replace trust roots for the test CA / issuance / DNS controller without disabling verification (test mode only). |

| OCSP (--features ocsp) |

| --ocsp-responder   | — | Explicit HTTP(S) responder for every enabled certificate issuer. Applies regardless of the XML enableStapling boolean; disables TLS resumption. |

| --ocsp-required | off | Refuse new TLS handshakes without a fresh authenticated GOOD response (also implied by Must-Staple). |

| --ocsp-test-mode | off | Permit a literal-loopback responder, with loopback serving addresses only. |

| --xf-capsule-dedicated-store | off | Also store every capsule-capable page under a DEDICATED (admission-exempt) key. Off by default since 2026-10-04: members are served from the shell-capable PUBLIC entry, which keeps one copy per page and lets the admission gate govern every store |

        !   Removed flags
`--cache-peer` / `--cache-peer-fill*` (cross-node cache peers) and `--cache-purge-secret-file` are gone; the purge endpoint is loopback-gated. `--io-uring` / `--io-uring-h3` were removed when the io_uring transport became unconditional (the tokio/epoll adapters were deleted with them).

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |

| `HTTPJET_ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT` | combined | `json` selects JSON access lines (fixed field order: `ts, client_ip, remote_user, method, uri, protocol, status, bytes, referer, user_agent, reqid`). |

| `HTTPJET_ERROR_LOG_FORMAT` | text | `json` selects JSON error events (`schema_version 1`, credential redaction, bounded fields). Independent of the access format; does not change the stdout/journald tracing formatter. Restart to change; rotate first to avoid mixed files. |

| `HTTPJET_ACCESS_ROLLING_BYTES` / `HTTPJET_ACCESS_KEEP_DAYS` | 50 MB / 30 | Unified access-log rolling size and retention. |

| `HTTPJET_LOG_DIR` | unset | Redirect every opened log file (unified and per-vhost) into this directory so isolated test or PGO runs never touch production log paths. |

| `HTTPJET_URING_NO_IOWAIT` | unset | `1` passes `IORING_ENTER_NO_IOWAIT` on blocking ring waits when the kernel advertises `IORING_FEAT_NO_IOWAIT`, so network-wait time on io_uring rings is not accounted as system iowait. |

| `HTTPJET_SYSLOG_TARGET` | unset | Mirror every rendered access line to syslog: `udp://host:514`, bare `host:port`, or a unix-dgram path such as `/run/systemd/journal/syslog`. Sent from the writer task; failures counted, never fatal. |

| `HTTPJET_SYSLOG_FACILITY` · `_SEVERITY` · `_RFC` · `_HOSTNAME` · `_APP_NAME` | `daemon` · `info` · `5424` · server name · `httpjet` | Syslog framing (`3164` for the BSD format). |

| `CF_SEND_ZSTD` | unset | `1` ≡ `--cf-send-zstd`. |

| `HJ_FAST_MEMO` | `1` | `0` ≡ `--no-fast-memo`. |

| `HJ_FAST_EARLY_BRIDGE` | unset | `off` · `shadow` · `on` ≡ `--fast-early-bridge`; takes precedence over the flag when set. |

| `HJ_LSAPI_FULL_HEADER_ENV` | unset | `1` also sends every request header's `HTTP_*` copy in the LSAPI env table (kill switch for the 0.1.8 dedupe; lsphp's `$_SERVER` is unchanged either way). Read once. |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL` · `HTTPJET_OTEL_METRICS` | unset | `1` enables OTLP tracing / metrics (`--features otel`; startup fails if the feature is absent). |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` | `0.01` | Root-span ratio sampler, 0–1. |

| `HTTPJET_OTEL_TRUSTED_PARENTS` | empty | Comma-separated exact gateway IPs (≤128) allowed to supply a W3C `traceparent`; everyone else starts a new root. |

| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` · `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT` (+ SDK header settings) | — | Complete collector URLs, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces`. |

| `RUST_LOG` | `info` | Tracing filter for the error log / journal, e.g. `RUST_LOG=debug,hj_rewrite=trace`. |

| `HJ_ROOT`, `HJ_URING_*`, `HJ_PEBBLE_*`, `HTTPJET_*_TEST_CHILD` | — | Test-harness variables only. |

## Exit behavior and signals

- **SIGHUP**: Reload configuration and certificates through the publication coordinator; a bad config keeps the current generation (see Admin API & reload ).

- **SIGUSR1**: Reopen the unified and per-vhost access/error logs and the PHP slow log (logrotate).

- **SIGUSR2**: Toggle httpjet's own log level to `debug` and back to the boot `RUST_LOG` filter.

- **SIGTERM / SIGINT**: Graceful shutdown: stop accepting, GOAWAY h2, drain in-flight connections for up to 15 s (inside the reference unit's `TimeoutStopSec=20`), close the admin coordinator, flush logs and telemetry, bounded OTel shutdown.

- **Argument validation**: Public admin binds, missing companion options (`--admin-token-file`, `--admin-resource-root`, ACME requirements), malformed `--page-cache-shared-paths` or `--page-cache-vary-default` / `--page-cache-dict-level` pairs, an unopenable generation file, or a rejected WAF configuration fail startup before any socket is bound; `--page-cache-integrity-required` additionally refuses to start the file tier when the integrity key cannot be installed.

- **Socket activation**: Inherited fds are classified by port (TCP for the HTTP/HTTPS listeners, UDP for QUIC) or exact path (Unix socket); one io_uring core serves each inherited TCP fd, so the socket unit's fd count, not `--workers`, sets the core count.

==============================================================================
PAGE: Performance (https://httpjet.net/docs/performance)
SUMMARY: Measured speed and how it was measured.
==============================================================================

# Performance

httpjet is fast — and these docs are strict about *where* the time goes. Every figure names its regime, because a **loopback benchmark** (synthetic, on-box, PGO build) is not the same thing as **production telemetry** (real CDN-fronted traffic). The short version: on a Cloudflare-fronted PHP site, almost all wall time is PHP, and httpjet's own CPU is a rounding error.

        1,183 k rps   h2 static empty, c=50, dedicated load-generator VM, median of 3 (0.1.12, 2026-11-08)
        44.8 k rps   PHP/LSAPI over HTTP/1.1, PGO loopback
        40 ×   cache hit vs the same page through PHP
        0.2 %   httpjet's request phases, June 2026 production telemetry
        1.55 IPC   h2 hit path at saturation, June 2026 (hardware counters)
        0.0002 flt   v0.1.5 h2 static minor page faults/req
        0 / 80   metric rows worse, 0.1.10 vs 0.1.5 (controlled A/B)
        +27.6 %   h2 page-cache hit RPS, 0.1.11 defaults (coop ring + response memo, x86 ABBA)

## Read the regime, not just the number

           loopback benchmark · synthetic, on-box, PGO
           production telemetry · real CF-fronted traffic
           hardware counters · perf at saturation

Loopback removes network, handshakes, CDN. It isolates server code for comparison only. **No loopback figure here is a production number.** Telemetry measures user time instead: backend- and edge-dominated. Same server: ~908k req/s synthetic, ~0.2% of June 2026 user latency. Different questions.

## Performance across builds — interactive presentation

You find every campaign below with regime, commit, and receipt name. The curve covers Phase 1–7 (`0.0.1`, June 2026) through `0.2.0`. CSV receipts stay outside the public export at github.com/faratech/httpjet .

Compare v0.0.1–v0.2.0 in the **Release Speed Curve**. Every release was re-measured on 2026-11-11 under identical conditions on a dedicated lab VM — no production host was loaded. Per-round data: release-sweep-2026-11-11.tsv ; raw `h2load` logs, server logs and the bench driver: release-sweep-2026-11-11/ . (Earlier sweeps stay archived: 2026-11-08 and 2026-10-26 .) Then step through **17 build slides**, **Workload Trajectories**, **Build-vs-Build Diff**.

        ⎁   One test, every version
To keep this page simple, every version-to-version number comes from **one run under one set of conditions**: a dedicated lab VM (c4-highmem-8, the production machine type), loopback only, server pinned to 4 cores, `h2load` on the other 4, each release PGO-built from its tag the same way, same flags, same eight workloads, 3 rounds each, median shown. Before benching, every binary also had to pass the **same functional checks** (start, static file, `.htaccess` page, PHP page, cache hit, empty and 64 KiB files, config lint): lab-checks-2026-11-08.tsv . Numbers from *other* regimes — the dedicated-client server comparison, production telemetry, the dated build-history slides — are always labelled with their own conditions and are never mixed into the curve.

## Where the time actually goes

> [Benchmark Chart: attribution — Where a production request spends its time (live sample · 2026-08-30 · mean request 9.99 ms)]

        ⎁   Measured
Across millions of production requests, the `lsphp` render is **86.5–98.8% of request wall time**. In the June 2026 telemetry httpjet's own request phases were about **0.2%** — roughly **138 µs per request** (rewrite, cache lookup, compression); a synthetic cache hit costs ~38 µs of CPU including TLS, HTTP/2, rewrite, cache lookup and access logging. The 2026-08-30 sample: mean request 9.99 ms, 8.96 ms of it LSAPI TTFB, rewrite 5.4 µs, cache lookup 3.2 µs; pool acquire p99.9  production telemetry · --telemetry-file + --php-slow-log

Halving httpjet CPU shaves ~0.1% off latency here. Cache hits remove ~99% instead. Investment follows that asymmetry: cache, PHP/opcache, cacheable fraction.

**At the instruction floor.** Saturated h2 hits show **IPC 1.55**, **0.31% branch-miss**, **1.6 L1d misses per 100 instructions**. Instructions per request bottleneck, not locality. Futex (~85% of syscall time) was idle parking, not contention. Box sat ~50% idle at ceiling.

Responses: global **mimalloc**, **on-core fast path** plus memo. October 2026 campaign (`0.0.9`–`0.1.5`): skip double lookup for 404/PHP GETs (−14.5% cookied CPU); memoize `.htaccess` matches (`access_decision_for_request` 13% → 2.7%); `--trusted-proxy-idle-secs 1800` (handshakes −30% x86, −78% ARM); `--page-cache-dict-level` (ARM encode ~50% → 11%); pool buffers via `hj_core::recycle::BODY_BUFS` under `MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0`.

## Loopback throughput

August 2026 **three-way** (httpjet/OpenLiteSpeed/nginx): dedicated client, 2026-08-27, two interleaved pairs per cell, busy host. Heavy-`.htaccess`: loopback PGO, 2026-08-28. June PGO stays PHP-path reference (commercial-LiteSpeed baseline).

> [Benchmark Chart: h2-static — HTTP/2 static throughput by concurrency (dedicated load-generator client · 2026-08-27 · empty bodies · mean of 2 interleaved pairs · req/s)]

One h2 connection hits ~58k req/s at c=1 alone. Throughput keeps rising with concurrency. It never collapses here. The June collapse past c=50 reflected that build only. HTTP/1.1 empty bodies reach ~202k at c=1000. OpenLiteSpeed reaches ~183k there.

> [Benchmark Chart: heavy-rewrite — Heavy .htaccess static (806-line chain, /robots.txt) (PGO three-way · 2026-08-28 · c=100 · req/s)]

> [Benchmark Chart: memo-ab — Fast-path memo, same binary A/B (forum chain · /robots.txt · c=100 · req/s)]

> [Benchmark Chart: php-h1 — PHP over LSAPI, HTTP/1.1 (loopback · PGO build · 2026-06 · req/s)]

## Release 0.1.10: controlled A/B against 0.1.5

The `0.1.10` release (October 26, 2026) closed the five-round review. It found **23 issues, fixed 22, and closed 1 by decision**. The full workspace suite (3,068 tests) stayed green. Both builds ran back to back here. Each used its production flags. The run covered **16 workloads, 5 blocks, in both run orders**. Result: **0 of 80 metric rows were worse**. Every figure below shows relative A/B change only.

| Workload | Throughput | p50 | p99 | CPU / request | RSS |

| Page-cache miss → store | **+16%** | −8% | −9% | **−61%** | −10% |

| Warmer burst (fresh TLS connections) | +1% | −2% | −4% | **−38%** | −8% |

| Open-loop realistic mix (fixed offered rate) | fixed rate | +2% | **−29%** | −17% | – |

| Uncached PHP | +6% | −5% | −6% | −6% | −8% |

| Cookied page-cache serve | +1% | −1% | −3% | −6% | −8% |

| Beacon POST to PHP | +3% | −5% | +4% | −5% | −8% |

| h2 cache hits | +2% | +1% | +20% (noisy metric) | −3% | −8% |

| Static 1 KiB / 64 KiB, heavy `.htaccess`, h1 and h2 | −4% to +1% | −2% to +1% | −2% to +11% | +0.8% to +1.8% (within noise) | −8% to −9% |

| New TLS 1.2 / 1.3 connections | same | same | same | same | −9% |

        ⎁   Honest caveats
Static-file CPU per request is up 1–2%, which is within the measurement noise. The h2 cache-hit p99 row (+20%) is a high-variance metric on a loop that finishes in a couple of milliseconds. The largest page-cache miss and warmer gains come mostly from the egress-at-rest work that shipped in `0.1.7`, which `0.1.5` predates.

Vs `0.1.9` alone, CPU/request: PHP **−4.7%**, beacon **−4.3%**, cookied serves **−4.2%**, h2 hits **−1.8%**. HPACK encode **4.73 µs → 1.34 µs** (Huffman + memo). Cookie `SetEnvIf` **29 µs → 1 µs** (linear lookahead).

Also fixes sandbox 404s: `RestrictSUIDSGID=yes` makes `openat2` return `ENOSYS`. No-follow walk now resolves docroots. Transient unit: `0.1.9` 404, `0.1.10` 200.

## Release 0.1.11: two defaults flipped on

`0.1.11` (November 7, 2026) defaults two optimizations on: `coop` ring (`--uring-ring coop`; `legacy`/`defer` selectable) and response memo for public hits (off: `--no-page-cache-response-memo`; old opt-in still parses). ARM already ran both. x86 ran neither.

Alt-port ABBA, x86, one build, flags on/off, both orders, dominant production shape:

| Workload | Throughput | p50 | p99 | CPU / request | RSS |

| Cookieless H2 page-cache hits | **+27.6%** | **−36%** | **−32%** | **−26.7%** | +~2 MB |

| Cookied page-cache hits | – | – | – | −4.4% | – |

| Static 1 KiB | neutral (within noise) |

        ⎁   Honest caveats
~908k h2 static figure unchanged. aarch64 `coop` alone neutral vs `legacy`. Memo retains cookieless public GETs only, exact freshness/Age/purge fences. Gates pre-flip: 40 memo tests, purge-revocation test, 24 H1/H2 + 4 H3 real-hit arms.

Also removes Beeper/eBPF experiment code. Adopts ARM canary for voidrune. Clears H1/H3 panic-ratchet sites. Packaging fixes (musl, H3 stack, Gentoo `DIGESTS`) change no serving behavior.

Memo alone, instructions/request, frozen non-PGO binary, SINGULARITY loopback, 1 KiB hits, 500k/arm, off/on/on/off:

| Protocol | Memo off (instr/req) | Memo on (instr/req) | Change |

| H1 plaintext | 60,337 | 30,811 | **−48.9%** |

| H1 TLS | 72,720 | 40,561 | **−44.2%** |

| H2 plaintext | 65,975 | 36,621 | **−44.5%** |

| H2 TLS | 72,742 | 41,532 | **−42.9%** |

| H3 | 98,293 | 68,024 | **−30.8%** |

Instructions show less native cache-hit work here. They count user-mode PMU over warmup plus measurement. They show no whole-machine CPU saving. Throughput and tails mixed under compiler load. The shipped claim therefore rests on the x86 ABBA. Source: `docs/pagecache-response-memo-experiment.md` in the source tree.

## Release 0.2.0: security audit fixes and cold-start latency

`0.2.0` (November 11, 2026) is the result of a security and robustness review of everything added since 0.1.10. It fixes 20+ issues, each with a regression test, and changes one startup behaviour you can measure: the `.htaccess` chain is parsed once, before the first connection, and its rewrite prefilter is built off the request path. Before, every serving thread parsed the same 900-line file after each restart, reload or edit, and requests stalled for the parse (about 0.5 s of CPU).

- **Cold start:** slowest request of a 64-way burst right after boot **508 ms → 3 ms**; `httpjet check --strict` on the production config **1.5 s → 0.07 s**. Gate: `scripts/cold_start_latency_test.sh`.

- **Security and correctness:** upstream WebSocket handshake validation; no credentials in capsule revalidation; every gzip member of a backend response decoded; out-of-order LSAPI packets refused; control characters escaped in the text error log; a QUIC Initial that closes itself no longer leaves a connection behind for 60 s; shared cache bodies no longer drain the server-wide HTTP/3 body budget; listener CPU steering only where the NIC has a receive queue per worker.

- **Observability:** `httpjet_h2_conn_ends_total{reason}`, `httpjet_pagecache_ghost_hits_total`, `httpjet_htaccess_parses_total`.

- **Verification:** 3,171 workspace tests, h2spec 146/146 over TLS, memo parity 192 cells with zero diffs, HPACK and HTTP/1 fuzzers clean for 14 million runs. No flags change; the wire is unchanged.

Same-host loopback on the production x86_64 host (PGO, 8 cores, live traffic shared), 2026-11-11, standard suites. nginx 1.30 and OpenLiteSpeed ran the same docroot on alternate ports:

| Workload (c50 unless noted) | httpjet 0.2.0 | nginx | OpenLiteSpeed |

| HTTP/2 static 1 KiB | **423,164 req/s** | 153,485 req/s | 356,373 req/s |

| HTTP/1.1 static 1 KiB | 172,387 req/s | 110,481 req/s | **176,827 req/s** |

| HTTP/2 static 64 KiB | **60,314 req/s** | 28,667 req/s | — |

| Heavy `.htaccess` vhost, HTTP/2 (c100) | **310,055 req/s** | 155,196 req/s | 263,947 req/s |

| Heavy `.htaccess` vhost, HTTP/1.1 (c100) | 146,047 req/s | 118,156 req/s | **180,919 req/s** |

| Warm page-cache hit, HTTP/2 (c32/m32) | **123,591 req/s** | — | — |

| Warm page-cache hit, HTTP/1.1 (c100) | **90,566 req/s** | — | — |

Lab VM, 2026-11-11 (loopback, server on 4 cores, loadgen on 4, every release PGO-built from its tag, 3 rotated rounds, median). Use it to compare httpjet releases against each other: 0.2.0 vs 0.1.12 measured in the same run, H2 1 KiB **591.8k → 625.5k**, H1 1 KiB **273.3k → 311.2k**, heavy `.htaccess` H2 **402.9k → 515.3k**, PHP/LSAPI **27.8k → 32.3k**, page-cache hit **410.5k → 544.5k**, H2 empty **563.1k → 717.2k**; H2 64 KiB is flat (92.4k → 89.7k). Raw logs and the per-round TSV: release-sweep-2026-11-11/ . In the same lab nginx reached 196k (H2 1 KiB) against httpjet 0.2.0's 656k.

> [Benchmark Chart: lab-threeway — Lab three-way, same-host loopback (httpjet vs nginx vs OpenLiteSpeed) (dedicated lab VM c4-highmem-8 · server cores 0-3 / loadgen cores 4-7 · h2load c=32 x10 (64 KiB: n=20k) · median of 3 rounds · 2026-11-11 · req/s)]

        ⎁   Honest caveats
The production-host rows share a machine with live traffic, and the same servers swing ±10–20% between runs there: nginx's H2 1 KiB moved from 180,940 (2026-11-08) to 153,485 (this run) with no change on its side. Read them as the shape of the comparison, not as a precise delta against 0.1.12. The lab table, where both builds ran back to back on an idle VM, is the version-to-version comparison. The 0.1.12 dedicated load-generator table below was not re-run for 0.2.0 and still describes 0.1.12. The cache rows used a non-forum `/help/` page through the real origin cache (metrics endpoint not verified in this run; each page was primed and confirmed as `x-litespeed-cache: hit`). Raw CSVs for this run are on the benchmark page .

## Release 0.1.12: hot-path allocation and contention reductions

`0.1.12` (November 8, 2026) cuts hot-path allocation/contention: borrowed routing (`Router::resolve_ref`), single-pass header scan, HPACK name reuse, batched IDs, cached dates, sharded counters, diskstore/metablob refinements, lighter logging. No flags change. Wire unchanged. Parity gate: 192 cells, zero diffs.

Loopback, production x86_64 host, PGO, 8 cores, live traffic shared, 2026-11-08, standard suites:

| Workload (c50 unless noted) | httpjet 0.1.12 | nginx | OpenLiteSpeed |

| HTTP/2 static 1 KiB | **371,540 req/s** | 180,940 req/s | 399,505 req/s |

| HTTP/1.1 static 1 KiB | **195,446 req/s** | 117,979 req/s | 201,306 req/s |

| HTTP/2 static 64 KiB | **68,689 req/s** | 35,063 req/s | — |

| Heavy `.htaccess` vhost, HTTP/2 (c100) | **271,118 req/s** | 131,955 req/s | 333,519 req/s |

| Warm page-cache hit, HTTP/2 (c32/m32) | **110,158 req/s** | — | — |

| Warm page-cache hit, HTTP/1.1 (c100) | **80,025 req/s** | — | — |

Re-run 2026-11-08: `h2load` + `wrk` check, **dedicated load-generator VM** (c4-highcpu-8, same zone), full unpinned host over VPC, production PGO, median of 3:

> [Benchmark Chart: dedicated-0112 — Dedicated load-generator client, three-way (httpjet 0.1.12) (c4-highcpu-8 client VM, same zone · full-host servers over VPC · h2load c=50 x100, 1M requests/cell · median of 3 rounds · 2026-11-08 · req/s)]

`wrk` cross-check (H1, 1 KiB, c=100, 15 s): httpjet **540,911**, nginx 439,433, OpenLiteSpeed 341,344 req/s. Dedicated cells never compare with same-host rows. Compare August 2026 dedicated data: 891k empty-body.

Same three servers, second regime: the 2026-11-08 lab VM re-run; its three-way chart is now the 0.2.0 one in Release 0.2.0 . The dedicated-client chart above stays the cross-server headline because it matches how LiteSpeed and nginx publish.

        ⎁   Honest caveats
This build ran on a shared production host here. This section forms no A/B against `0.1.11`. The rows exercise memoized and fast-serve paths directly. They exercise cache-hit serving and logging too. Treat older dedicated-host comparisons as approximate. Full CSV receipts are published with the release on the benchmark page .

## The origin cache result

Largest real-workload fact: the origin page cache . Each hit replaces a PHP render with a memory/tmpfs copy.

> [Benchmark Chart: cache-vs-php — One forum page: cache hit vs full PHP render (HTTPS loopback · PGO · 152 KB page · req/s)]

2026-08-30 refresh, real `/help/*` hits, shared host: ~5.4k req/s h2, ~6.7k h1. Hit ratio reads low structurally: ~51% of GET-200s are one-shot bot crawls beyond any TTL. Lever there: edge TTL.

## At the instruction floor

See Where the time actually goes above. It merges this material there.

## File egress: sendfile and kTLS

> [Benchmark Chart: sendfile — File egress receipts (1 MiB bodies, c=50) (loopback · 2026-09-09 · req/s)]

Plain H1: bounded nonblocking `sendfile(2)`. TLS 1.3 H1: kernel TLS only via `--ktls=auto` + physical `tls-hw-tx-offload`. Production virtual NIC: `off [fixed]`. Forced software kTLS measured worse. `auto` refuses it. Details: Protocol stacks .

## The codegen tier — PGO + mimalloc

Production: PGO + mimalloc + `-C target-cpu=native`. `scripts/build-pgo.sh` (outside public export) runs instrument → loopback drive → rebuild. Load: h2 hits dominant, plus h2/h1 static, PHP. Frame pointers kept for pprof. Tuning belongs to one deployment. Build neutral artifacts separately.

        !   A non-PGO benchmark is not a benchmark
Debug builds run ~5× slower. Plain release differs ~10% by layout alone. Build both sides identically, interleave runs. Harness (`scripts/bench-suite.sh`, `scripts/bench-report.py`) and CSVs stay outside public export.

## Knobs that actually move production

| Lever | Effect |

| Page-cache opt-in coverage and TTLs (app side) | The dominant lever: every hit removes a PHP render. |

| `--page-cache-admit-threshold 1` with dictionaries | Cache on first sight when storage is cheap; watch `httpjet_cache_hit_ratio_real`. |

| `--cf-send-zstd` | Hands the CDN the cheapest encoding to produce; no browser-visible change. |

| Fast-memo eligibility of the docroot chain | Ineligible chains pay full pipeline per request. Fix directives, keep memo. |

| `--rewrite-ua-classify` | Collapses UA diversity onto few outcome-cache entries. |

| TLS resumption & certified idle window | ECDSA, AES-128-GCM, `--tls-session-tickets 0`, `--trusted-proxy-idle-secs` cut handshake CPU. |

| PHP: opcache, worker count, slow endpoints | `--php-slow-log` attribution. Pool rarely bottlenecks (p99.9

SUMMARY: Test results, protocol coverage, and parity checks.
